Most first-time visitors should start with Shinjuku or Shibuya if they want to experience Tokyo at full volume. ## Current System (Before April 2027)

Guests staying in Tokyo hotels and ryokan pay a tax of 100 yen per person per night for rooms costing between 10,000 yen and 15,000 yen, and 200 yen per person per night for rooms costing 15,000 yen or more. Accommodation less than 10,000 yen is currently exempt.

The tax is calculated on the pre-tax room rate excluding meals.

## New System (From April 2027)

From April 2027, the tax-free threshold will be raised to 13,000 yen per person per night, while stays above that amount will be charged a three-percent fee.

The new tax will also apply to private holiday rentals and guesthouses, which were previously exempt.

The updated system is projected to generate around 19 billion yen ($133 million) in annual revenue.

Based on the search results, here's a comparison of these three popular areas in Hakone for a one-night ryokan stay:

## Hakone-Yumoto

Hakone-Yumoto is the gateway to Hakone and a convenient area to stay in. It's a transportation hub with direct access to the Hakone Tozan Line, buses, and the Hakone Ropeway, and offers a variety of accommodation options, including traditional ryokans and hotels. However, it can get quite crowded, especially on weekends and holidays. Hakone-Yumoto wins on pure convenience, with trains from Odawara ending here, buses fanning out across the region, shops selling snacks and souvenirs.

## Gora

Gora is located along the Hakone Tozan Cablecar route, known for its hot springs and beautiful scenery, and is a peaceful and relaxing area with several ryokans and hotels. It's a central point for many of Hakone's attractions, including the Hakone Open-Air Museum, Hakone Ropeway and Hakone Gora Park. Gora is recommended as the base because it sits in the middle of the classic Hakone experience, with easy reach to museums, restaurants, and ryokan clustered nearby.

## Sengokuhara

Located in the northern part of Hakone, Sengokuhara is a quieter area surrounded by mountains and forests. Sengokuhara is a bit more laid back and less crowded than Hakone-Yumoto and Gora, but it is also a bit more remote and less accessible by public transportation. Sengokuhara is home to stylish accommodations that emphasize relaxing away from it all, with classy ryokan and boutique hotels, making it ideal if you prefer soaking in an onsen and waking up to nature rather than crowds.

## Recommendation for One Night

For a balanced first visit, stay in Gora; for maximum convenience, stay in Hakone-Yumoto; and for Sengokuhara only if nature and relaxation are priorities.

The Hakone Ropeway offers scenic transport through Owakudani, a volcanic area famous for its desolate landscape and mountain views. The system features three segments connecting Sounzan, Owakudani, Ubako, and Togendai stations.

- **February–November:** 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM
- **December–January:** 9:00 AM – 4:15 PM

Each segment takes approximately 15 minutes:
- Sounzan to Owakudani
- Owakudani to Ubako
- Ubako to Togendai

## Key Attractions
- **Mt. Fuji views:** Best seen between Ubako and Owakudani stations, particularly in mornings during summer
- **Valley scenery:** The ropeway passes 130 meters above the valley floor between Sounzan and Owakudani
- **Seasonal features:** Cherry blossoms (April-May), hydrangeas (June-July), autumn leaves (late October–mid-November)

## Amenities & Services
- OWAKUDANI KITCHEN restaurant on second floor of Owakudani Station
- Free wheelchair lending service
- Baby changing facilities at all stations
- Paid luggage storage (500 yen)
- Credit cards and electronic money accepted

The Hakone Freepass and "OWAKUDANI 2-Day Pass" provide cost savings for multi-attraction visits.

# Accommodation Tax Base Definition

## What's Included in 宿泊料金 (Accommodation Charge)

The tax base encompasses "bedding fees, bathing charges, sleepwear costs, cleaning fees at lodging facilities, and related service charges" regardless of how they're labeled, as long as they're mandatory charges associated with the accommodation itself.

## Exclusions

Yes, the definition explicitly excludes:

- **Meals**: "Amounts related to food and beverages provided with accommodation"
- **Consumption Tax**: "Consumption tax, local consumption tax, hot spring tax, accommodation tax and other taxes"

Additional excluded items: vehicle charges, tobacco, phone services, laundry, souvenirs, tips, and voluntary gratuities.

## Current Tax Rates (as of Sept. 1, 2026)

| Per Person Per Night | Tax Rate |
|---|---|
| Under ¥5,000 | Tax-free |
| ¥5,000–¥14,999 | ¥200 |
| ¥15,000–¥19,999 | ¥400 |
| ¥20,000+ | ¥500 |

## Who Pays

Guests are the nominal taxpayers, but "the special collection agent collects accommodation tax alongside room charges" at lodging facilities. The accommodation facility operator bears responsibility for remittance to Osaka Prefecture.

The Jingu Gaien District Type 1 Urban Redevelopment Project is a large-scale redevelopment advancing around Kasumigaoka-cho in Shinjuku Ward and Kita-Aoyama 1-chome and 2-chome in Minato Ward. The ginkgo tree-lined street, a symbol of Jingu Gaien, was completed in 1923 (Taisho 12). ## Development Details

The project, which will take over a decade to complete, will see the aging rugby and baseball stadiums razed and rebuilt, with a new hotel by the latter stadium standing next to a pair of almost 200-meter-tall (650-foot) skyscrapers containing office space and upmarket serviced apartments, as well as another 80-meter (260-foot) tower.

## Public Concerns

The plan has sparked public anger, demonstrations and even lawsuits from outraged Tokyo residents, with over 225,000 people signing a petition calling for authorities to withdraw support for the project.

## November Temperature in Hakone

During November, Hakone experiences moderate daytime temperatures of 16°C (61°F) and cooler nights around 10°C (50°F). More specifically, the average high temperature is 17.5°C (63.5°F) and the average low temperature is 7.1°C (44.8°F).

Hakone's specific areas experience slightly different conditions due to elevation differences. Sengokuhara, at an altitude of 645 meters, has a tendency to be three or four degrees cooler than Hakone-Yumoto. This means Gora and Sengokuhara areas will be somewhat colder than the overall averages.

## Weather Conditions & Rainfall

Around 139 mm (5.5 in) is typical rainfall, with rain expected on around 11 days. The weather is usually moderately chilly and breezy, with temperatures ranging from 49—61°F (9—16°C).

## Hakone Autumn Foliage Schedule by Elevation

The high peaks of Mt. Kamiyama and Mt. Tokyo to Kyoto delivery arrives the next day. In most cases, luggage shipped between major cities on Honshu arrives the following day.

## Service Details

Takkyubin (also written takuhaibin, and branded TA-Q-BIN by Yamato Transport) is Japan's everyday parcel-courier service. You hand the bag to your hotel or a convenience store, it's scanned and trucked overnight, and delivered to your next hotel under your name and check-in date.

## Pricing Structure

Price is set by the bag's size (length + width + height, in cm) and the distance. A normal check-in suitcase is Size 120–160.

## Peak Timing and Crowds

The final two weeks of November are among the most crowded in Kyoto's year, with weekends during the peak foliage period (typically November 18 to 30) being severely crowded at the main spots. The predicted best viewing period for 2026 is November 15 – December 5.

To avoid the worst crowds, timing is crucial:

## Overtourism Management

Kyoto is actively managing overtourism by promoting six peripheral districts - Fushimi, Ohara, Takao, Yamashina, Nishikyo and Keihoku - to pull visitors out of the jammed centre.

# Sumo in Japan: Key Information

## Tournament Schedule & Venues
Six annual tournaments occur in: Tokyo (January, May, September), Osaka (March), Nagoya (July), and Fukuoka (November). Each tournament runs 15 days with one bout per day for top-ranked wrestlers.

## Ticket Information
Tickets go on sale approximately one month before tournaments and typically sell out, especially for weekends and national holidays. Three seat types exist:

- **Ringside seats**: Most expensive and hardest to obtain
- **Box seats**: Japanese-style, typically seat four people (all tickets must be purchased even if not fully used)
- **Balcony seats**: Western-style seating on the second floor

Purchase options include the [official vendor](https://sumo.pia.jp/), [BuySumoTickets](https://buysumotickets.com/), convenience stores, or stadiums.

## Sumo Stable Visits
Most stables don't accept independent tourists. Guided tours are the practical option, offered by companies like Klook, Rakuten, and BuySumoTickets for approximately 10,000 yen per person (4,000 yen for additional group members). Visitors must sit silently for 2-3 hours.

## Sumo-Related Attractions
**Ryogoku District** (Tokyo's sumo center) features:
- Sumo Museum (free admission, weekdays only)
- Ekoin Temple (historic tournament site)
- Chanko nabe restaurants (sumo wrestlers' staple hot pot dish)

## Hakone transport prices — verified August 2026

All figures below are adult, one-way unless stated. Everything checked against a live page today; derived/unconfirmed items are flagged at the end.

### 1. Hakone Freepass — current prices

| Version | 2-day | 3-day |
|---|---|---|
| From **Shinjuku** (incl. Odakyu round trip) | **¥7,100** | **¥7,500** |
| From **Odawara** (Hakone area only) | **¥6,000** | **¥6,400** |

Child: Shinjuku ¥1,600 / ¥1,850; Odawara ¥1,500 / ¥1,750.
Sources: https://odakyu-global.com/passes/hakone-freepass/ , https://hakonetrip.odakyu-global.com/passes/hakone-freepass/ , https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2358_008.html

**Price revision:** effective **1 October 2025**, +¥1,000 adult / +¥500 child on every variant (Shinjuku 2-day ¥6,100→¥7,100, 3-day ¥6,500→¥7,500; Odawara 2-day ¥5,000→¥6,000, 3-day ¥5,400→¥6,400). Same increase for paper and digital. Old→new table shown live at https://www.hakonenavi.jp/transportation/ticket/freepass/ (also https://www.hakonenavi.jp/groupnews/13925/ , https://essential-japan.com/news/hakone-free-pass-price-set-to-increase-from-october-2025/). No further revision found for 2026.

### 2. Coverage
Unlimited rides on **8 modes** (official list, odakyu-global.com/passes/hakone-freepass/):
- Odakyu Line — round trip Shinjuku (or your boarding station) ↔ Odawara, **plus free travel between Odawara and Hakone-Yumoto**; the Odawara version has no Odakyu segment
- Hakone Tozan Railway (Odawara–Hakone-Yumoto–Gora)
- Hakone Tozan Cable Car (Gora–Sounzan)
- Hakone Ropeway (Sounzan–Owakudani–Togendai), all sections
- Hakone Sightseeing Cruise / pirate ship (Togendai–Hakone-machi–Moto-Hakone), ordinary cabin
- Hakone Tozan Bus (designated areas)
- Odakyu Hakone Highway Bus (designated areas)
- Tokai Bus (designated areas)
Plus discounts at ~70 facilities.

**Not covered:** the **Romancecar limited express surcharge** (explicit on the official page); ship Special Cabin upgrade (+¥500/segment, https://samuraicarjapanjdm.jp/hakone-sightseeing-cruise-lake-ashi/); buses outside the designated zones.

### 3. Romancecar, Shinjuku → Hakone-Yumoto
- Limited express surcharge: **¥1,200 paper / ¥1,150 digital (e-Romancecar)**, one way — https://odakyu-global.com/passes/romancecar/
- It is **on top of** the Freepass. Official example: ¥1,200 + ¥7,100 = **¥8,300** for pass + one Romancecar leg.
- Total without a pass: **¥2,470 paper / ¥2,420 digital** one way (https://livejapan.com/en/in-tokyo/in-pref-kanagawa/in-hakone_odawara/article-a0003297/) → implies a base fare of **¥1,270**.
- Times: **Romancecar ≈ 80 min** direct; **regular express ≈ 120 min** with a transfer at Odawara (both from odakyu-global.com/passes/romancecar/ and hakonetrip.odakyu-global.com/passes/romancecar/).

### 4. Odawara → Hakone-Yumoto without the pass
**¥360**, about **14–15 min**, Hakone Tozan Line local — https://ekitan.com/transit/fare/sf-1759/st-2792 (page dated Aug 2026).

### 5. Buying it
- **Digital: yes.** EMot Online Tickets and the EMot app (both odakyu-global.com/passes/hakone-freepass/ and hakonenavi.jp/transportation/ticket/freepass/). Digital and paper cost the same.
- **Foreign tourists: yes**, no residency/passport restriction — it is a general-sale pass, marketed in English on Odakyu's global site, sold via EMot, travel agents, and Odakyu Sightseeing Service Centers.
- **Odawara station: yes.** hakonenavi.jp lists 小田急線小田原駅 and the 小田原駅前案内所 among sale points, plus Hakone Tozan Railway stations, Seven-Eleven, and vending machines.

### 6. Is it worth it for 1 night / 2 days doing the standard loop?
Current individual fares for the loop (Yumoto → Gora → Sounzan → Togendai → Moto-Hakone → bus back):

| Segment | Fare | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Odawara → Hakone-Yumoto | ¥360 | ekitan.com/transit/fare/sf-1759/st-2792 |
| Hakone-Yumoto → Gora (Tozan train) | ¥460 | ekitan.com/transit/fare/sf-2792/st-9738 |
| Gora → Sounzan (cable car) | ¥430 | same |
| Sounzan → Togendai (ropeway) | ¥2,000 (flat fare since 1 Oct 2025, was ¥1,500) | hakonenavi.jp/groupnews/13925/ ; travel.watch.impress.co.jp/docs/news/2025379.html |
| Togendai → Moto-Hakone (pirate ship) | ¥1,700 (since 1 Oct 2025, was ¥1,200) | same |
| Moto-Hakone-ko → Hakone-Yumoto (Tozan bus) | ¥1,210 | ekitan.com/transit/bus-fare/sf-1012545/st-1012517 |
| Hakone-Yumoto → Odawara | ¥360 | as above |

- **Loop from Odawara: ¥6,520** vs **¥6,000** pass → **saves ¥520**, plus any extra local bus rides (¥300–1,200 each) and facility discounts. Worth it, but the margin is thin — one extra bus hop makes it clearly positive.
- **From Shinjuku:** substitute ¥1,270 each way Shinjuku↔Hakone-Yumoto for the two ¥360 legs → **¥8,340** vs **¥7,100** pass → **saves ¥1,240**. Clearly worth it. (Add ¥1,150–1,200/leg if you want the Romancecar either way.)
- Verdict: **yes for a 1-night/2-day standard loop**, decisively so from Shinjuku. It stops being worth it only if you skip the ropeway or the boat (e.g. Shinjuku → Lake Ashi one-way and back the same way ≈ ¥5,000).

### 7. JR TOKYO Wide Pass (2026)
- **¥16,000 adult / ¥8,000 child, 3 consecutive days** — raised from ¥15,000/¥7,500 on **14 March 2026**. https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2361_06.html ; https://www.kkday.com/en/blog/88992/jr-tokyo-wide-pass-guide
- **Odawara: covered** (JR East Tokaido line, area extends to Atami/Ito) — but **not on the Tokaido Shinkansen**, which is JR Central. https://tokyocheapo.com/travel/tokyo-wide-pass/
- **Hakone area: not covered at all** — no Tozan railway, cable car, ropeway, boat or bus; and **no Odakyu Romancecar**. https://japan-trails.com/media/jr-tokyo-wide-pass/
- So the natural combination is Tokyo Wide Pass (or a plain JR ticket) to Odawara + the **¥6,000 Odawara-version Freepass**.

### Figures I could NOT confirm from a live primary source
- **Odakyu base fare Shinjuku→Hakone-Yumoto ¥1,270** — *derived* (¥2,470 paper total − ¥1,200 surcharge; ¥2,420 digital − ¥1,150). Not read off a live fare table; ekitan's Shinjuku fare page 404'd and the JR/Odakyu fare finders were unreachable.
- **jreast.co.jp returned HTTP 403** on all English pass pages and on the 28 Jan 2026 press PDF, so the ¥16,000 Tokyo Wide Pass price and the 14 Mar 2026 date rest on japan-guide + KKday, not the operator. Two Odakyu PDFs also failed to parse; their contents were confirmed instead via hakonenavi's HTML fare table.
- **Ropeway ¥2,000** is described as a flat/uniform fare; I confirmed the ¥2,000 figure and the ¥500 increase, but not a per-section breakdown.
- Exclusion of **Izuhakone Group services** (Komagatake ropeway, Izuhakone buses/boats) is the well-known situation but was not verified on a live page today.

Sources: [Odakyu Freepass (official)](https://odakyu-global.com/passes/hakone-freepass/), [HAKONE TRIP Freepass](https://hakonetrip.odakyu-global.com/passes/hakone-freepass/), [Odakyu Romancecar (official)](https://odakyu-global.com/passes/romancecar/), [Hakone Navi Freepass fares](https://www.hakonenavi.jp/transportation/ticket/freepass/), [Hakone Navi fare revision notice](https://www.hakonenavi.jp/groupnews/13925/), [Travel Watch fare revision](https://travel.watch.impress.co.jp/docs/news/2025379.html), [Essential Japan price increase](https://essential-japan.com/news/hakone-free-pass-price-set-to-increase-from-october-2025/), [Ekitan Odawara–Hakone-Yumoto](https://ekitan.com/transit/fare/sf-1759/st-2792), [Ekitan Hakone-Yumoto–Sounzan](https://ekitan.com/transit/fare/sf-2792/st-9738), [Ekitan Moto-Hakone bus](https://ekitan.com/transit/bus-fare/sf-1012545/st-1012517), [Japan Guide Freepass](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2358_008.html), [Japan Guide Tokyo Wide Pass](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2361_06.html), [Tokyo Cheapo Tokyo Wide Pass](https://tokyocheapo.com/travel/tokyo-wide-pass/), [Japan Trails Tokyo Wide Pass](https://japan-trails.com/media/jr-tokyo-wide-pass/), [LIVE JAPAN Romancecar](https://livejapan.com/en/in-tokyo/in-pref-kanagawa/in-hakone_odawara/article-a0003297/), [Hakone Sightseeing Cruise guide](https://samuraicarjapanjdm.jp/hakone-sightseeing-cruise-lake-ashi/)

## Recommendation

**Stay: Tokyo Station area — specifically the Kyobashi / Nihonbashi / Hatchobori side of Chuo-ku, not Marunouchi itself.**

Reasoning: with both a Hakone and a Kyoto leg, you'll be dragging luggage to a Shinkansen twice. From Kyobashi/Nihonbashi that's a 5–10 minute walk or one subway stop to the platform where the Tokaido Shinkansen *starts* (so you board an empty train and get luggage space). Kyoto is direct; Hakone is Kodama→Odawara in ~40 min. You also get Yamanote, five subway lines, N'EX direct, the ¥1,500 TYO-NRT bus from Narita, and Asakusa Line direct-ish service to Haneda. **Check-in / check-out.** Japanese business hotels are rigid: 15:00 in, 10:00–11:00 out. ## 1. Base comparison — Hakone-Yumoto vs Gora vs Sengokuhara

**Hakone-Yumoto** (~100m elevation) — terminus of the Odakyu Romancecar from Shinjuku (~85–95 min direct). Maximum convenience: you step off the train and walk to your ryokan. Downside: it's the most crowded, most souvenir-shop-ish part of Hakone, and it's *before* the loop, so you backtrack nothing but you also see nothing scenic from your window. Foliage peaks **late Nov–early Dec** here (lowest elevation).

**Tonosawa** — one stop past Yumoto on the Tozan line, 5 min. Practically the same access as Yumoto but a quiet river gorge instead of a shopping street. This is where the best value-for-atmosphere ryokan sit (Yama no Chaya, Kansuiro). Strong recommendation for a one-night stay.

**Miyanoshita / Kowakidani** (~450–600m) — mid-mountain, on the Tozan railway between Yumoto and Gora. Historic resort quarter (Fujiya Hotel). Good compromise: real mountain scenery, still on the rail line, ~25–35 min from Yumoto.

**Gora** (~550m) — end of the Tozan railway, start of the cablecar. This is the *hinge* of the classic loop, so it's the most efficient base if you want to do railway → cablecar → ropeway → Owakudani → Lake Ashi pirate ship → bus in one clean pass. Roughly 40 min from Yumoto by Tozan railway (switchbacks, scenic). Foliage peaks **mid-to-late November**.

**Sengokuhara** (~650–700m) — bus-only, no rail. Quiet, pampas grass fields, Mt Fuji views from the north side. Beautiful, but it is **off the loop** and bus-dependent in both directions, which is a real cost when you only have one night and a Shinkansen to catch. Foliage + susuki (pampas) peak **late Oct–mid November** — earliest of the three.

**Verdict for your trip (arrive from Tokyo, leave for Kyoto):** stay **Gora** if the loop is the priority, or **Tonosawa/Yumoto** if the ryokan itself is the priority. Both keep you on the rail line so the morning departure is simple: Tozan railway down to Hakone-Yumoto → Odakyu 15 min to Odawara → Shinkansen Hikari/Kodama to Kyoto (~2h05–2h20 from Odawara). Note **Nozomi does not stop at Odawara** — you want Hikari.

I'd **skip Sengokuhara** for a single night: you'd bus in from Yumoto (~30–40 min) and bus back out the next morning with luggage, and the loop becomes awkward.

**A clean one-night shape:** Romancecar to Yumoto → drop bag → do the loop that afternoon (Gora cablecar → ropeway → Owakudani → pirate ship → bus back to Yumoto/Gora) → check into ryokan by ~17:00 → next morning check out ~11:00 → Odawara → Kyoto. If you stay in Gora, do the loop on arrival day and take the bus back to Gora at the end.

**November foliage:** elevation matters a lot. Early-to-mid Nov favors Owakudani/Sengokuhara/Lake Ashi; mid-to-late Nov favors Gora and Miyanoshita; late Nov favors Yumoto/Tonosawa gorge. **Mid-November (~Nov 10–20) is the widest overlap** — you'd catch Gora and Lake Ashi at peak with the high country just past and Yumoto coming on.

## 2. Specific ryokan — three price bands

All prices below are **published/typical rates, not live quotes for your dates**. Nothing is bookable-confirmed here; treat these as bands to shop against.

### ~¥25–30k/person — Hakone Gora Onsen Setsugetsuka (季の湯 雪月花)
- **Location:** Gora, 1-minute walk from Gora Station. Kyoritsu Resort/Dormy group, 158 rooms. Operating and booking.
- **Rate (published, per person, 2 meals, tax incl.):** weekday **¥25,460–26,480**; holiday-eve/Saturday **¥29,540–34,630**. Solidly in your lower band even on a Saturday.
- **Private open-air bath in room:** **Yes — all 158 rooms** have a hinoki (cypress) private open-air bath. This is unusual at this price and is the single most important fact for a tattooed guest.
- **Kashikiri:** **3 private open-air baths ("杜の湯" — Kangetsu, Manten, Hanagasumi), free, no reservation** — first-come, use when the door's unlocked. 15:00–25:00 and 05:00–10:00, ~40 min per use, 2 people capacity. No showers in them, stair access.
- **Tattoo policy:** **Not stated on the official site or FAQ.** Assume the *large communal bath* is off-limits (Japanese chain-hotel default) — but with an in-room open-air bath plus free private baths, tattoos are a non-issue here in practice.
- **Times:** check-in 15:00, check-out 11:00. Dinner in two seatings, 17:15 and ~19:45. Bathing tax ¥150/person (age 13+).
- **Caveat:** it's large and hotel-like, not an intimate ryokan. Best value on this list.

### ~¥35k/person — Yama no Chaya (四季を味わう宿 山の茶屋), Tonosawa
- **Location:** Tonosawa, one stop past Hakone-Yumoto — a secluded riverside/gorge setting reached over a small footbridge. 15 rooms only. Operating, direct booking + phone 0460-85-5493.
- **Rate:** an Ikyu standard plan was reported at **¥72,842 for 2 people, 1 night, 2 meals ≈ ¥36,400/person.** Published-rate reference, not a live quote; rotenburo-tsuki rooms and November weekends will run higher.
- **Private open-air bath in room:** **Yes — 11 of 15 rooms** have private open-air hot-spring baths (plus 4 standard rooms without). Ask specifically for a 露天風呂付き room.
- **Kashikiri:** the "Keikoku" (渓谷) private open-air bath, **¥5,500 per 45-minute session**, 15:00–24:00, only **8 slots per day, first-come at check-in** — so arrive early if you want it.
- **Tattoo policy:** **explicitly tattoo-friendly.** Their own FAQ answers the tattoo question with "はい、ご利用頂けます" (yes, you may use the baths), and third-party tattoo guides list Yama no Chaya as welcoming tattooed guests into the public onsen *without requiring coverage*. This is rare and makes it my top pick if tattoos are a concern.
- **Times:** check-in **15:00–18:00** (hard 18:00 cutoff), check-out 10:00; late check-out to 11:00 for ¥5,500.
- **Why it fits:** small, atmospheric, genuinely traditional, and 5 minutes from Hakone-Yumoto — the easiest possible morning departure for Kyoto.

### ~¥45k/person — two options, both at or slightly over the top of your band

**Hakone Ginyu (箱根吟遊), Miyanoshita**
- 20 rooms on a cliff over the Hayakawa gorge; 5-min walk from Miyanoshita Station (Tozan line) or 1-min from the Miyanoshita bus stop from Odawara. Operating.
- **Rate (published, per person, 2 meals):** weekday **¥46,750–69,740 incl. tax.** The entry plan is just above ¥45k on a weekday; a November Saturday will be well above your band. Be realistic: this is a ¥50k+/person property in foliage season.
- **All rooms have a private open-air bath** with a terrace over the valley — so tattoos are functionally a non-issue in the room.
- **Kashikiri:** yes — one rental bath, plus the Ginyu Spa pavilion can be reserved privately 21:00–23:00.
- **Tattoo policy:** **not published.** Communal baths should be assumed tattoo-restricted; contact them directly.

**Hakone Kowakien Ten-yu (箱根小涌園 天悠), Kowakidani**
- 150 rooms, **all with private open-air hot-spring baths**; free shuttle ~10 min from Gora Station. Fujita Kanko. Operating.
- **Rate (published):** weekday from **¥47,190/person incl. tax, 2 meals** — again just over your ceiling, more on weekends.
- **Tattoo policy:** not on the official FAQ, but multiple Japanese sources state **tattooed guests cannot use the large communal bath** — the in-room open-air bath is the intended workaround.
- **Times:** check-in 15:00, check-out **11:00** (generous). Contact them if arriving after 20:00; dinner may not be held.

**Honest read on the ¥45k band:** in November foliage season, ¥45k/person with two meals buys you the *entry plan on a weekday* at Ginyu or Ten-yu, not a good room on a Saturday. If you want a genuine luxury feel inside budget, you'll get more for the money at ~¥35k at Yama no Chaya than at ~¥45k at the bottom of Ginyu's ladder.

# PART 1 — Namba vs Umeda for first-timers

## Midosuji Line (the spine connecting them)
- Umeda ⇄ Shinsaibashi ⇄ Namba on the Osaka Metro Midosuji Line: **~8–10 min, ~¥240**, trains every 2–4 min. This is the single most useful line in Osaka — it also runs Shin-Osaka → Umeda → Yodoyabashi → Honmachi → Shinsaibashi → Namba → Tennoji.
- Practical implication: the two districts are not really an either/or for *access* — they're 10 minutes apart. The choice is about which walk-out-the-door experience you want and which day trips are frictionless.

## Shin-Osaka (Shinkansen)
- **From Umeda**: Midosuji Line, 4 stops, **~9 min, ¥240**. Also JR Kyoto Line from Osaka Station, 1 stop, ~4 min.
- **From Namba**: Midosuji Line direct, **~15–16 min, ~¥290**. No transfer, same line.
- Verdict: Umeda is faster but Namba is a single-seat ride. Not a decisive factor for a 2-night stay.

## Kansai Airport (KIX)
**From Namba — Nankai (private railway, own terminal above/below Namba):**
- **Rapi:t** limited express: **~34–39 min to Namba**. Ordinary fare ¥970 + limited-express seat charge; the commonly-sold discounted digital ticket is **¥1,410 (Regular Seat) / ¥1,590 (Super Seat)**. All-reserved, luggage racks, most services are Rapi:t β.
- **Airport Express (空港急行)**: ~43–48 min, **¥970**, no reservation, runs very frequently. Genuinely fine with suitcases outside rush hour.
- Nankai Namba Station is directly connected to the Takashimaya building and the Namba hotel cluster — often a **2–8 minute walk with luggage, no transfer at all**.

**From Umeda — JR Haruka and alternatives:**
- **Yes, Haruka does stop at Osaka Station.** Since the March 2023 opening of the **Umekita underground platforms** (platforms 21–24) at Osaka Station, Haruka calls there and no transfer at Tennoji/Shin-Osaka is needed. Airport-bound Haruka typically departs from **platform 21**. Times from KIX: Tennoji ~30 min, **Osaka (Umekita) ~45–50 min**, Shin-Osaka ~50 min, Kyoto ~75 min.
- **Important caveat**: the Umekita platforms are at the *west/south* end of the Osaka Station complex. From the Umekita concourse to the Midosuji subway Umeda station, Hankyu Osaka-umeda, or many Umeda hotels is a **further 5–10 minute underground walk** through a large, signposted but genuinely confusing complex. First-timers routinely lose 10–15 minutes here.
- Haruka is also the **most expensive** option (~¥2,400–2,900 one-way unreserved/reserved depending on season) unless you hold a JR Pass or the discounted ICOCA & Haruka ticket.
- Cheaper JR option from Osaka Station: **Kansai Airport Rapid (関空快速)**, direct, **~65–70 min, ¥1,210**, but the train splits at Hineno and is a commuter train with limited luggage space.
- **Airport Limousine Bus** to Umeda/Osaka Station: ~60 min, ~¥1,800, luggage in the hold — the easiest option for Umeda if traffic cooperates.

**KIX verdict: Namba wins clearly.** Nankai from Namba is cheaper, faster, and involves no long underground walk.

## Food and nightlife
**Namba / Minami** — this is the Osaka people picture:
- **Dotonbori** (Glico sign, Ebisubashi, takoyaki/kushikatsu stalls) — 5–10 min walk from Namba Station.
- **Hozenji Yokocho**, **Amerikamura**, **Shinsaibashi-suji arcade**, **Sennichimae Doguyasuji** (kitchenware street) all within walking distance.
- **Kuromon Ichiba Market** — ~8 min walk from Namba, at Nippombashi Station. Best 09:00–14:00; heavily tourist-oriented now but still the classic seafood-on-a-stick stop.
- **Shinsekai / Tsutenkaku** (kushikatsu, retro Showa atmosphere) — 2 stops on the Sakaisuji Line or ~10 min from Namba via Ebisucho/Dobutsuen-mae.
- Street-level, chaotic, open late, cheap-to-mid. You can eat well without any planning.

**Umeda / Kita**:
- **Department store dining**: Hankyu Umeda, Daimaru, Grand Front Osaka, Hep Five, Lucua. Excellent, reliable, ends early (most restaurants close 22:00–23:00).
- **Umeda Sky Building** Floating Garden Observatory; **Kita-Shinchi** for upscale/expense-account dining and bars (expensive, less approachable without Japanese).
- Cleaner, more corporate, better for shopping and rainy days; weaker for spontaneous street-food wandering.

**Food verdict: Namba, decisively, for a first trip.**

## Day trips
- **Nara** — **Namba wins.** Kintetsu Nara Line departs from **Osaka-Namba Station** (same station complex): Rapid Express ~40 min, **¥680**; Limited Express ~36 min, +~¥520 reserved seat. Arrives at **Kintetsu Nara**, which is a ~5 min walk from Nara Park/deer — far better than JR Nara Station, which is a 20+ min walk out.
- **Kyoto** — **Umeda wins.** JR Special Rapid from **Osaka Station**: ~29 min, **~¥580**, to Kyoto Station. Or **Hankyu** from **Osaka-umeda**: ~43 min, **~¥410**, to **Kyoto-Kawaramachi** — which drops you at Gion/Pontocho/Nishiki, better for sightseeing than Kyoto Station. From Namba you'd either ride Midosuji to Umeda first (+10 min), or take **Keihan from Yodoyabashi** (10 min up Midosuji) to Gion-Shijo, ~55 min total, ~¥430.
- **Kobe** — **Umeda wins.** JR Special Rapid Osaka → Sannomiya ~21 min, ~¥420; Hankyu/Hanshin from Umeda ~28–32 min, ~¥330. From Namba there is a direct option: **Hanshin Namba Line** rapid express Osaka-Namba → Kobe-Sannomiya, ~40 min, ~¥420, no transfer — so Namba is not badly served here.

*Fare caution: several Kansai operators have revised fares in 2025–2026. Treat all fares above as accurate-to-the-nearest-¥50 rather than exact for November 2026.*

## RECOMMENDATION: **Stay in Namba** (Namba / Shinsaibashi / Nipponbashi triangle)

Reasoning, in priority order:
1. **Two nights is short.** With ~1.5 usable evenings, the value of stepping out of the hotel into Dotonbori/Kuromon/Shinsekai without a train ride is very high. Umeda gives you department stores you can find in any Japanese city.
2. **Airport transfer is the biggest logistics risk with luggage**, and Namba→KIX by Nankai is the simplest airport link in Kansai: one train, one platform, ~¥970–1,410. The Umeda equivalent requires the Umekita underground walk or a bus.
3. **Nara is the natural day trip from a 2-night Osaka base** (Kyoto usually gets its own separate nights on a first Japan trip), and Kintetsu from Osaka-Namba is the single best Nara connection in the region.
4. **The Kyoto/Kobe advantage of Umeda costs you only ~10 minutes** on the Midosuji Line, and Namba still has a direct Hanshin train to Kobe.
5. Namba is more legible on foot. Umeda Station is one of the most confusing station complexes in Japan (JR Osaka, Hankyu Osaka-umeda, Hanshin Osaka-umeda, three separate subway "Umeda" stations, plus Kitashinchi) — a poor thing to hand a jet-lagged first-timer.

**Choose Umeda instead only if**: you are doing Kyoto and Kobe as day trips on both days, you want department-store shopping as a main activity, or you're connecting straight through to Shin-Osaka Shinkansen early on the departure morning.

# PART 3 — Osaka accommodation tax (宿泊税), current for 2026

**Yes, the rates were revised — the change took effect for stays from 1 September 2025 (Reiwa 7)** and these are the rates in force for November 2026.

### Current bands (Osaka Prefecture, effective 1 Sep 2025 →)

| Accommodation charge, **per person per night** | Tax |
|---|---|
| Under ¥5,000 | **Exempt** |
| ¥5,000 – ¥14,999 | **¥200** |
| ¥15,000 – ¥19,999 | **¥400** |
| ¥20,000 and above | **¥500** |

### Previous bands (before 1 Sep 2025)
| Under ¥7,000 | Exempt |
| ¥7,000 – ¥14,999 | ¥100 |
| ¥15,000 – ¥19,999 | ¥200 |
| ¥20,000+ | ¥300 |

So the revision **doubled every rate** and **lowered the exemption threshold from ¥7,000 to ¥5,000**, pulling budget and mid-range stays into the net for the first time.

### The mechanics you asked about — confirmed
- **Yes, it is per person, per night** (not per room, not per stay).
- **Yes, the band is determined by the per-person rate**, not the room total. Divide the room rate by the number of guests first.
- **Tax base = the lodging-only charge (素泊まり料金).** It **includes** bedding, bathing, sleepwear, cleaning and mandatory service charges. It **excludes** meals and beverages, consumption tax, local consumption tax, bathing tax, the accommodation tax itself, plus transport, laundry, phone, souvenirs and tips.
- It is a **prefectural** tax, so it applies across all of Osaka Prefecture — Namba, Umeda, Nakanoshima, minpaku, everywhere. There is no separate Osaka City levy on top.
- The hotel collects it as a special collection agent and remits it; guests are the nominal taxpayers.

### Worked example for your trip
A **¥24,000/night room total for 2** = ¥12,000 per person per night → falls in the ¥5,000–14,999 band → **¥200 per person per night = ¥400 per night for the two of you = ¥800 for 2 nights.** Negligible, but it will appear as a separate line.

If you land a ¥32,000 room (¥16,000 pp), you'd be in the ¥400 band — ¥800/night for two. Note the cliff edge: the per-person band boundaries mean a small rate increase can double the tax.

### One thing to watch — the 1 March 2026 billing change
Several major chains changed **how** the tax is presented, effective 1 March 2026. Sotetsu Hotels, for example: reservations made **on or after 1 March 2026** have the accommodation tax **charged separately from the room rate and collected on site**, even for prepaid bookings; reservations made by 28 Feb 2026 had it bundled into the displayed room rate. Practical effect for a November 2026 booking made now: **expect a small separate cash/card charge at check-in**, and don't assume the OTA total already includes it. This is a presentation change, not a rate change.

- **Tokyu Stay Kyoto Sanjo-Karasuma** (also listed as "Ryogaemachi-dori"): 392 Kakimotocho, Ryogaemachi-dori, Nakagyo-ku. **Karasuma Oike Stn — 2 min; Karasuma Sanjo — 5 min.**

## Recommendations against your ¥15,000–28,000 band

**For Nov 18–21 (peak foliage):**
1. **Mitsui Garden Hotel Kyoto Shijo — ¥17,797.** The only hotel that gives you a real large public bath, a central Shijo-Karasuma location, and a peak-date price near the bottom of your band. Best overall pick.

**(a) Morning training / heya visits — Tokyo**
- Most stables **do not accept independent tourists**. Guided tours are the practical route.
- **Price: ~¥10,000 per person** (~¥4,000 for additional group members), via Klook, Rakuten Travel Experiences, GetYourGuide, Magical Trip, or [BuySumoTickets](https://buysumotickets.com/).
- Reality check: you sit silently on a hard floor for 2–3 hours. It is authentic and genuinely worthwhile, but it is not a show.
- **Book 3–6 weeks ahead.** Slots are small (often 10–15 people) and November is high season. Consequence of not booking: no access at all — there is no walk-up option.
- **Arashio-beya street-window viewing** (free, from the sidewalk): I **could not verify** its 2026 status. This has been intermittently suspended. Treat as unconfirmed.

**(b) Tourist sumo shows**
- **Yokozuna Tonkatsu Dosukoi Tanaka** (Ryogoku) — could not verify 2026 pricing/booking. It is a tonkatsu restaurant with sumo theming, not a show venue.

- **Sumo Museum**, Ryogoku Kokugikan — **free**, weekdays only, no booking.

**Honest verdict:** the retired-wrestler demonstration shows aimed at tourists are mid-tier — entertaining, heavily staged, overpriced at ~¥10,000+. The morning practice tour is the better spend. If sumo matters to you, the real answer is that November is the wrong month for this itinerary.

- **No longer same-day walk-up queueing.** Sales are now **online only**, via a dedicated system: **https://www.e-tix.jp/shochiku_makumi/en/**

# Japan IC Cards, Fares & Luggage — Verified 2026 Status

## 1. IC Cards

### Unregistered Suica/PASMO suspension — OVER
- Suspension began June 2023 (chip shortage); **registered** cards returned Sept 2024; **unregistered/anonymous Suica, PASMO and Rinkai Suica sales fully resumed 1 March 2025**, purchasable directly from station ticket machines. As of 2026 regular cards are freely on sale. — https://www.timeout.com/tokyo/news/unregistered-suica-and-pasmo-transport-cards-to-resume-sales-from-march-022125
- Regular Suica/PASMO: **¥500 refundable deposit + charge (machines typically start at ¥1,500)**; valid 10 years from last use; refund at issuer counter minus **¥220** handling fee. — https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2359_002.html (updated 27 Jul 2026)

### Welcome Suica (red physical card)
- **No deposit, no issue fee**; you pay only the loaded value. **Valid 28 days**; **remaining balance is NOT refundable**. Cash top-up only.
- Sold at Haneda and Narita (JR East Travel Service Centers / dedicated Welcome Suica machines), plus Tokyo, Shinagawa, Shibuya, Shinjuku, Ikebukuro, Ueno, Yokohama, Sendai stations and Japan Rail Café Tokyo. — https://livejapan.com/en/in-tokyo/in-pref-tokyo/in-tokyo_train_station/article-a0005633/ , https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2359_002.html

### Welcome Suica Mobile — exists, iPhone only
- Launched **6 March 2025**. Free, **no deposit**, **180-day validity** (reissue a new one in-app after expiry). **iPhone 8+/Apple Watch only — no Android.** Top-up via Apple Pay or cash at konbini. No balance refund.
- 2026 additions: integrated with JR-EAST Train Reservation for Shinkansen/Narita Express reserved seats; **local-train Green Car tickets added March 2026**. — https://apps.apple.com/us/app/welcome-suica-mobile/id6738336566 , https://glostravel.com/en/article/welcome-suica-mobile-guide
- Note: jreast.co.jp/multi/wsmlp/ returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, so the official page could not be read directly.

### Mobile Suica / Apple Wallet for foreign tourists
- **Yes** — a non-Japanese Apple ID works. Add via Wallet → Transit Card → Japan → Suica. No Japanese App Store account needed, English supported, no deposit.
- **Top-up with foreign cards: Mastercard and Amex work; foreign-issued Visa is blocked at network level** for Suica top-up in Apple Wallet. JCB works. Workaround: cash at any station machine with the "チャージ/IC Recharge" button, or use Welcome Suica Mobile.
- **Android: effectively unavailable to tourists** — the Japanese IC apps require Osaifu-Keitai hardware, which phones sold outside Japan do not have. Google Wallet does not offer Suica for foreign-market Androids. — https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2359_002.html , https://komarilab.com/guides/ic-card-iphone-android/

### PASMO PASSPORT → replaced
- **PASMO PASSPORT was discontinued (sales ended Oct 2024).** Successor **"TOURIST PASMO" launched 20 May 2026**: denominations **¥1,000–¥10,000**, **no deposit**, **valid 28 days from issue**, **no refunds**, cannot be reissued if lost. Sold only at **Haneda (Keikyu, T1/T2/T3)** and **Narita (Keisei, T1/T2)**. Max balance ¥20,000. — https://www.pasmo.co.jp/tourist-pasmo/ , https://tokyocheapo.com/travel/tourist-pasmo/

### ICOCA (JR West)
- Regular ICOCA is on sale normally in 2026: **¥500 refundable deposit + charge (typically ¥1,500 initial = ¥2,000 total)**, same refund rules. — https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2359_002.html
- **KANSAI ONE PASS is being discontinued**: sales began winding down **1 November 2025**, all sales to end by end of FY2026. Existing cards remain usable as ordinary ICOCA. Price was ¥3,000 (¥500 deposit + ¥2,500 value). — https://en.traicy.com/posts/2025022620069/

### Interoperability
- All ten major IC cards (Suica, PASMO, ICOCA, PiTaPa, etc.) are mutually usable across most major urban areas — Suica works on Kyoto city buses, Kyoto subway, Osaka Metro; ICOCA works throughout Tokyo. — https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2359.html
- **Exceptions travelers actually hit:** (a) you cannot tap in in one fare region and tap out in another — e.g. no IC travel Tokyo→Nagoya on local JR across the JR East/JR Central boundary; (b) some rural/regional buses and small private lines take only local cards or cash; (c) commuter passes and some discounts are not interoperable; (d) IC balance cannot pay Shinkansen fares without a separate product.

### New 2026 developments
**Suica renewal (JR East):** migration from card-stored value to a **cloud/centre-server architecture**. Mobile Suica app renewed **spring 2026** (local-train Green Car support); **by autumn 2026** the app becomes a full payment app with **code (QR) payments**, **bank-account/credit-card linking and deferred/post-pay fares**, removing the **¥20,000 balance cap** constraint for code payments. Suica Penguin mascot retires end of FY2026 (31 Mar 2027). — https://www.jreast.co.jp/e/press/2024/pdf/20241210.pdf , https://en.japantravel.com/article/suica-2026-and-beyond/71597

**Contactless Visa/Mastercard tap-to-ride at gates** (japan-guide, updated **25 Mar 2026** — https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2359_credit_card_tap.html):
- **Tokyo — accepted:** Tokyo Metro, Toei, Odakyu, Keio, Tokyu, Keikyu, Yurikamome, Tsukuba Express. Tobu/Seibu selected stations only. **Not accepted: JR East, Keisei, Tokyo Monorail.**
- **Kansai — accepted:** **Osaka Metro (all lines, with automatic 1-day fare capping)**, Hankyu, Hanshin, **Nankai**, Kintetsu, Kobe Subway, Sanyo. **Not accepted: JR West, Keihan, Kyoto city subway, Kyoto city buses, Eizan, Randen.**
- Other: Fukuoka Subway/Nishitetsu (capping), Sapporo Subway (capping), Kintetsu in Nagoya. Hiroshima none.
- **Hard constraint:** tap-to-pay only works if **both** entry and exit stations support it.
- ⚠️ **Conflict flagged:** insidekyoto.com claims **Keihan** accepts tap-to-ride and Osaka Metro's own English page advertises contactless from April 2026; japan-guide (dated) lists Keihan as not accepting. Treat Keihan as unconfirmed. **Kyoto remains the weak spot — its buses and subway do not take credit-card tap, so an IC card is still genuinely needed in Kyoto.**

# Kyoto & Osaka Accommodation Research — Nov 2026

## ⚠️ Read this first: your dates may not be peak

The single most useful thing I found. **2026 foliage is forecast to run late.** Above-normal summer temps (JMA seasonal outlook) push peak koyo ~3–5 days later than the historical average nationwide. For Kyoto:

- Central temples (Eikan-do, Nanzen-ji, Kiyomizu-dera, Philosopher's Path): **Nov 18 – Dec 2**
- Tofuku-ji, Arashiyama, Ohara: **Nov 22 – Dec 5**
- Kurama/Kibune/Mt Hiei (higher elevation, earlier): **Nov 5–15**
- City-wide peak density: **~Nov 29 – Dec 3**

So **Nov 18–21 lands at the front edge of color, not the peak.** That's arguably the sweet spot: real foliage at the major central temples, but ahead of the worst crowd-and-price crush of the final week. If you can shift later you get better color at much worse prices; if you shift earlier you save money but may get mostly green.

**Honesty caveat:** these are travel-media projections. The authoritative Japanese forecasts (Weathernews, tenki.jp) don't publish 2026 koyo dates until **September 2026** — about a month from now. Worth re-checking before you lock non-refundable rates.

**Booking timing:** the standard guidance is 4–6 months ahead for foliage season, 6–9 months if dates are fixed. At ~3 months out you are late but not shut out — business-hotel chains (the ones below) release and re-release inventory far closer in than ryokan do. Saturdays are the first to go.

---

## KYOTO — Neighborhood recommendation

### The transit reality you need to understand

Kyoto's transit situation genuinely changed, and most older advice is stale:

- **The ¥700 one-day city bus pass is dead.** Sales ended Sept 2023; passes stopped being accepted end of March 2024. It was killed specifically to push tourists off buses onto the subway. The replacement is the **Subway & Bus One-Day Pass at ¥1,100**.
- **Buses in foliage season are the failure mode.** Routes along Shijo-dori and around Kyoto Station suffer significant delays mid-November to early December, and fill to capacity — meaning full buses drive past your stop. This is the thing that wrecks itineraries.
- **The subway is immune to surface congestion.** Two lines only: **Karasuma** (north–south, through Kyoto Station) and **Tozai** (east–west), crossing at **Karasuma-Oike**. Small network, but in peak season "underground and slower on the map" beats "direct bus" constantly.

### ✅ Recommendation: Downtown — Shijo-Karasuma / Karasuma-Oike

This is my clear pick for a first-time pair in peak foliage, for one reason above all: **it is the only area that puts you on the subway spine AND within walking distance of dinner.**

- **Karasuma Line** to Kyoto Station in ~5 minutes, 2–3 stops. You get Shinkansen and day-trip access without living next to the station.
- **Tozai Line** at Karasuma-Oike handles the Higashiyama/Nanzen-ji side.
- **Hankyu Kawaramachi** is right there: direct to Osaka-Umeda, ~43 min, **¥410** — cheaper and often more convenient than JR.
- **Walkable dinner** — Nishiki Market, Pontocho, Kiyamachi, Gion all on foot. This matters enormously in November, when you come back cold and tired at 17:30 and do *not* want another packed bus.
- You can walk to Gion/Higashiyama for early-morning temple visits, which is the actual crowd-avoidance strategy (dawn arrivals beat the 10am tour buses by 2+ hours of queueing).

### 🥈 Runner-up: Kyoto Station area

Better if you're doing heavy day-tripping (Nara, Osaka, Himeji) or arriving/leaving with big luggage. Unbeatable for the Shinkansen and every bus route originates there. **The cost:** the dining scene is malls, department store floors, and chains — it lacks the atmospheric evening you probably came to Kyoto for, and you'll commute into the interesting parts of the city daily.

### ❌ Not recommended as a base

- **Higashiyama/Gion** — gorgeous and atmospheric, and best for dawn temple access, but **no subway station of its own**. You're bus- or taxi-dependent, exactly the thing that breaks down in foliage season. Great to walk to, bad to stay in.
- **Arashiyama** — do not base here. ~30 minutes from Kyoto Station via a lengthy two-train transfer, and critically, **it empties out at night**: most local restaurants close early, last orders around 18:30. It's a half-day trip, not a base.

## KYOTO ACCOMMODATION TAX — the critical question, definitively answered

### The new bands are confirmed correct
Your reported figures are accurate. Effective **March 1, 2026**, per person per night:

| Accommodation charge (per person/night) | Tax | Was |
|---|---|---|
| Under ¥6,000 | ¥200 | ¥200 (unchanged) |
| ¥6,000 – ¥19,999 | ¥400 | ¥200 |
| ¥20,000 – ¥49,999 | ¥1,000 | ¥500 |
| ¥50,000 – ¥99,999 | ¥4,000 | ¥1,000 |
| ¥100,000+ | ¥10,000 | ¥1,000 |

Applies to **stays on or after March 1, 2026 regardless of when you booked or paid.**

### ✅ THE ANSWER: the band is based on the PER-PERSON rate — room total ÷ number of guests

This is confirmed by **Kyoto City's own official operator guidance**, which gives an explicit worked example using a twin room:

> **20,000円 ÷ 2人 ＝ 10,000円　⇒　1人1泊当たりの宿泊料金は10,000円**
> *(¥20,000 ÷ 2 people = ¥10,000 ⇒ the accommodation charge per person per night is ¥10,000)*

The city's example runs both occupancies of the same ¥20,000 twin room: **1 occupant** → ¥20,000/person → higher band; **2 occupants** → ¥10,000/person → lower band.

**Applied to your case:** a **¥25,000 double room for two = ¥12,500 per person** → falls in the **¥6,000–¥19,999 band → ¥400 per person per night → ¥800/night for the two of you.** For 3 Kyoto nights: **¥2,400 total.**

Not the ¥1,000/person band. **Sharing a room halves your per-person rate and very often drops you a full band.**

### ⚠️ Warning: many secondary sources get this wrong
I found a widely-circulated travel-industry article stating the tax "multiplies based on the number of guests regardless of room configuration," illustrated with a family of four in one ¥80,000 room each paying ¥4,000 (¥16,000 total). **That is incorrect** under the official rule: ¥80,000 ÷ 4 = ¥20,000/person → ¥1,000 each → ¥4,000 total, a **4× overstatement**. Trust the city's page, not the aggregators.

### What counts as the "accommodation charge"
Per Kyoto City — it's the **room-only rate (素泊まり料金: room + service charge)**:
- **Included:** cleaning fees, bedding fees, bathing fees, sleepwear fees, service/gratuity charges
- **Excluded:** **meal charges** and **consumption tax**

**Two practical consequences:** (1) if your rate bundles breakfast, the meal portion is stripped out before banding — which can push you *down* a band; (2) the banding figure is the **pre-consumption-tax** number, so a ¥25,000 tax-inclusive rate is ~¥22,700 for tax purposes, ~¥11,400/person. Comfortably in the ¥400 band either way.

**Bottom line: the Kyoto tax is a non-event at your budget — ¥800/night for two.** The scary ¥10,000 headline figure targets ¥100,000+/person luxury ryokan. Don't let it drive your planning.

## OSAKA

**Disclosure:** my web search budget was exhausted before I could verify Osaka hotel rates and the tax bands to the same standard as Kyoto. The transit analysis below is solid; the hotel and tax sections are flagged where uncertain, and I'd rather tell you that than fabricate precision.

### Namba vs Umeda — ✅ Recommendation: **Namba**

For a **2-night first-timer stay**, Namba wins clearly. The reasoning:

**Namba's case:**
- **Dotonbori, Shinsekai, and Kuromon Market are all walkable.** For a 2-night stay, the evenings *are* the trip — you have essentially one full day and two nights. Namba lets you walk out of the hotel into the thing you came for. Umeda means a subway ride each way to see it.
- **Kansai Airport: Nankai from Namba is the decisive advantage.** Nankai Airport Express runs **direct, no transfer, ~45 min, ~¥970**; the Rapi:t limited express is faster and reserved. Umeda has **no direct KIX rail link** — you transfer, or take the JR Haruka which is built around Tennoji and Shin-Osaka.
- **Nara day trip** is easiest from Namba via the **Kintetsu Nara line**, landing you at Kintetsu Nara — much closer to Nara Park and the deer than JR Nara station.
- **Midosuji Line** connects Namba to everything, including Umeda in ~8 minutes for ~¥240. You are never cut off from Umeda; the reverse is equally true, which is why the walkability tiebreak decides it.

**Umeda's case (why it's the runner-up, not wrong):**
- Better for **Kyoto** — **Hankyu Osaka-Umeda → Kyoto-Kawaramachi, ~43 min, ¥410**, cheapest and drops you downtown. JR Osaka Station → Kyoto Special Rapid is ~30 min for ¥560–580.
- Slightly better for **Shin-Osaka/Shinkansen** (one short Midosuji hop) and for **Kobe**.
- Better if you prefer department-store dining and a polished, less raucous environment.

**The tiebreak:** Namba→Shin-Osaka on the Midosuji Line is direct and only a few minutes longer than Umeda→Shin-Osaka. Umeda's Shinkansen edge is small; Namba's Dotonbori-on-foot and direct-KIX edges are large. **Stay in Namba.**

*One caveat I flagged but couldn't fully verify: the Osaka Station "Umekita" underground platforms now give Umeda some Haruka/KIX access. Even so, Nankai from Namba remains simpler and cheaper. Worth a check if airport logistics are decisive for you.*

### Osaka hotels
The same chains you're already considering all have strong Namba-area properties — **Dormy Inn Premium Namba** (Dormy always has a large communal bath, and the Namba property is well regarded), **Sotetsu Fresa Inn Osaka Namba**, **Mitsui Garden Hotel Osaka Japan-Bashi**, and **Hotel Gracery Osaka Namba**. Osaka runs meaningfully cheaper than Kyoto in November — it has no foliage premium — so **¥15,000–22,000 for a twin is a realistic expectation**, comfortably inside your band, and your Osaka nights should be the easy part of this trip.

I was not able to verify specific November 2026 rates, bath facilities per property, or breakfast pricing for these to the standard I applied in Kyoto. I'd treat the above as a shortlist to check rather than verified findings.

### Osaka accommodation tax — genuinely unresolved
I got **conflicting figures** and could not reach the Osaka Prefecture official page (multiple URL patterns 404'd):

- **Long-standing structure** (in place since 2019, and corroborated by a source describing Osaka as "¥100–¥300 per person per night"): under ¥7,000 exempt; ¥7,000–¥15,000 = ¥100; ¥15,000–¥20,000 = ¥200; ¥20,000+ = ¥300.
- **One 2026 source** instead reported: under ¥5,000 exempt; ¥5,000–¥15,000 = ¥200; ¥15,000–¥20,000 = ¥400; ¥20,000+ = ¥500 — and stated there was no 2026 revision.

I can't adjudicate these without the official source. **Either way this is trivial for you** — on a ~¥20,000 twin, your per-person rate is ~¥10,000, putting you in a low band: **¥200–¥400 per night for two, so under ¥800 for both Osaka nights.** It does not affect any decision. Verify at the prefecture's official 宿泊税 page if you want the exact number.

Note that Osaka's tax is levied by the **prefecture**, and like Kyoto's it is assessed per person per night on the room-only charge — so the same room-total ÷ occupants logic should apply.

### 🥈 Runner-up: Kyoto Station area

Better if you're doing heavy day-tripping (Nara, Osaka, Himeji) or arriving/leaving with big luggage. - **Higashiyama/Gion** — gorgeous and atmospheric, and best for dawn temple access, but **no subway station of its own**. You're bus- or taxi-dependent, exactly the thing that breaks down in foliage season. Great to walk to, bad to stay in.

## KYOTO ACCOMMODATION TAX — the critical question, definitively answered

### The new bands are confirmed correct
Your reported figures are accurate. Effective **March 1, 2026**, per person per night:

| Accommodation charge (per person/night) | Tax | Was |
|---|---|---|
| Under ¥6,000 | ¥200 | ¥200 (unchanged) |
| ¥6,000 – ¥19,999 | ¥400 | ¥200 |
| ¥20,000 – ¥49,999 | ¥1,000 | ¥500 |
| ¥50,000 – ¥99,999 | ¥4,000 | ¥1,000 |
| ¥100,000+ | ¥10,000 | ¥1,000 |

Applies to **stays on or after March 1, 2026 regardless of when you booked or paid.**

### ✅ THE ANSWER: the band is based on the PER-PERSON rate — room total ÷ number of guests

This is confirmed by **Kyoto City's own official operator guidance**, which gives an explicit worked example using a twin room:

> **20,000円 ÷ 2人 ＝ 10,000円　⇒　1人1泊当たりの宿泊料金は10,000円**
> *(¥20,000 ÷ 2 people = ¥10,000 ⇒ the accommodation charge per person per night is ¥10,000)*

The city's example runs both occupancies of the same ¥20,000 twin room: **1 occupant** → ¥20,000/person → higher band; **2 occupants** → ¥10,000/person → lower band.

**Applied to your case:** a **¥25,000 double room for two = ¥12,500 per person** → falls in the **¥6,000–¥19,999 band → ¥400 per person per night → ¥800/night for the two of you.** For 3 Kyoto nights: **¥2,400 total.**

Not the ¥1,000/person band. **Sharing a room halves your per-person rate and very often drops you a full band.**

### ⚠️ Warning: many secondary sources get this wrong
I found a widely-circulated travel-industry article stating the tax "multiplies based on the number of guests regardless of room configuration," illustrated with a family of four in one ¥80,000 room each paying ¥4,000 (¥16,000 total). **That is incorrect** under the official rule: ¥80,000 ÷ 4 = ¥20,000/person → ¥1,000 each → ¥4,000 total, a **4× overstatement**. Trust the city's page, not the aggregators.

### What counts as the "accommodation charge"
Per Kyoto City — it's the **room-only rate (素泊まり料金: room + service charge)**:
- **Included:** cleaning fees, bedding fees, bathing fees, sleepwear fees, service/gratuity charges
- **Excluded:** **meal charges** and **consumption tax**

**Two practical consequences:** (1) if your rate bundles breakfast, the meal portion is stripped out before banding — which can push you *down* a band; (2) the banding figure is the **pre-consumption-tax** number, so a ¥25,000 tax-inclusive rate is ~¥22,700 for tax purposes, ~¥11,400/person. Comfortably in the ¥400 band either way.

**Bottom line: the Kyoto tax is a non-event at your budget — ¥800/night for two.** The scary ¥10,000 headline figure targets ¥100,000+/person luxury ryokan. Don't let it drive your planning.

# Japan transport logistics — 10 days, 2 people, November 2026
Route: arrive Tokyo → Hakone → Kyoto (+ Nara day trip) → Osaka → depart KIX. All figures **per person, yen, adult**.

**Critical context:** JR East implemented its **first-ever fare revision on 14 March 2026** (avg +7.1%; Yamanote base fare ¥150→¥160). Hakone-area fares rose **1 Oct 2025**. Kyoto subway fares rose **1 Oct 2025**. Several widely-cited blog figures are stale.

---

## 1. Airport transfers

### Narita → central Tokyo
| Option | Fare | Time |
|---|---|---|
| **N'EX to Tokyo Sta.** | **¥3,070** ⚠️ | 53–60 min |
| N'EX to Shinjuku/Shibuya/Ikebukuro | ¥3,250 ⚠️ | ~80–85 min |
| **N'EX TOKYO Round Trip Ticket** (foreign passport only, 14 days) | **¥5,200** | — |
| **Keisei Skyliner** to Nippori/Ueno | **¥2,470** (¥2,465 IC) | 41/43 min |
| Keisei Main Line ltd. exp. (no surcharge) | ~¥1,260 | 90–100 min |
| **Airport Bus TYO-NRT** → Tokyo Sta./Ginza | **¥1,500** (¥3,000 late-night) | 65–90 min |
| Airport Limousine Bus | ~¥3,100 | ~100 min |

⚠️ **Flag:** sources conflict on whether ¥3,070/¥3,250 are pre- or post-14-Mar-2026 revision. The round-trip ticket demonstrably went ¥5,000→¥5,200 on that date, so budget **¥3,100–3,400** for N'EX one-way. Skyliner ¥2,470 is confirmed on Keisei's own fare page.

### Haneda → central Tokyo
| Option | Fare | Time |
|---|---|---|
| **Keikyu → Shinagawa** | **¥327 IC** | 11–14 min |
| Keikyu through-service → Higashi-Ginza/Asakusa | ¥599 IC | ~32 min |
| **Tokyo Monorail → Hamamatsucho** | **¥520 / ¥519 IC** | 13–18 min |

**Haneda is materially cheaper and faster** — ~¥400–600 vs ¥1,500–3,400. Worth paying more for a Haneda flight.

### Kansai → KIX
| Option | Fare | Time |
|---|---|---|
| **Kyoto → KIX, HARUKA tourist one-way ticket** (passport required) | **¥2,200** | ~75 min |
| — same price as **WEST QR HARUKA** digital, which *includes a reserved seat* | ¥2,200 | |

## 2. Nationwide JR Pass — the arithmetic

**7-day Ordinary JR Pass = ¥50,000** (¥53,000 via overseas agencies from 1 Oct 2026; official JR site stays ¥50,000).

Sum of every **JR-eligible** fare this itinerary generates:

| Leg | JR fare |
|---|---|
| Haneda → Hamamatsucho (Tokyo Monorail — *is* covered) | 520 |
| Tokyo local JR (Yamanote portion of 4 days, ~half of local spend) | ~1,600 |
| Tokyo → Odawara, Hikari non-reserved | 3,370 |
| Odawara → Kyoto, Hikari non-reserved | 11,770 |
| Kyoto ↔ Nara, JR Nara Line round trip | 1,440 |
| Kyoto → Osaka, JR Special Rapid | 580 |
| Osaka → KIX, Haruka non-reserved | ~2,400 |
| **Total JR value** | **≈ ¥21,700** |

Substituting Narita + N'EX instead of Haneda: **≈ ¥24,200**.

**Verdict: the 7-day JR Pass loses by ~¥26,000–28,000 per person. Do not buy it.** Three independent reasons:
1. **Value gap.** You'd need roughly **2.3× more JR travel** to break even. This route is one long shinkansen leg and a handful of short hops.
2. **Duration mismatch.** 7 days doesn't cover a 10-day trip, and the pass's biggest asset (the Odawara→Kyoto leg) sits mid-trip.
3. **It actively distorts the itinerary.** The Hakone approach — Odakyu, Tozan railway, ropeway, pirate ship — is **entirely non-JR**. Holding a JR Pass pushes you onto the worse Tokyo→Odawara-by-shinkansen routing (¥3,370 + ¥6,000 Odawara Freepass = ¥9,370) instead of the better ¥7,100 Shinjuku Freepass.

Break-even would require something like Tokyo→Kyoto→Hiroshima→Tokyo inside 7 days. That is not this trip.

### Regional passes, evaluated

| Pass | Price | Verdict for this route |
|---|---|---|
| **Hakone Freepass, Shinjuku 2-day** | **¥7,100** | ✅ **Buy.** See §4 arithmetic — saves ¥1,240 and removes all ticketing friction. |
| **Kyoto Subway & Bus 1-Day Pass** | **¥1,100** | ✅ Buy *per heavy-bus day only*. Break-even ≈ 5 bus rides. |
| **Osaka Enjoy Eco Card** | ¥820 weekday / ¥620 weekend | 🟡 Marginal. Break-even ≈ 4 Metro rides. Buy on a temple/museum-hopping day. |
| **JR Kansai Area Pass 1-day** | ¥2,800 | ❌ Skip. Its headline benefit is Haruka to KIX — but the tourist HARUKA ticket does that for **¥2,200**. Only wins if you cram Nara + Osaka + Haruka into one day. |
| **Kansai Railway Pass Lite** (ex-Kansai Thru Pass, renamed & repriced 1 Apr 2026) | ¥5,200 (2-day) / ¥6,500 (3-day) | ❌ Skip. **Excludes Kyoto subway and all JR.** Your realistic private-rail spend (Kintetsu Nara ¥1,520 + Hankyu ¥410 + Nankai ¥970 ≈ ¥2,900) is barely half the price. |
| **JR Tokyo Wide Pass** | **¥16,000** (raised from ¥15,000 on 14 Mar 2026) | ❌ Skip. Covers Odawara on the *conventional* JR line only — **not the Tokaido Shinkansen** (JR Central), **not Romancecar**, and **nothing inside Hakone**. Only pays off with Nikko/Karuizawa/Fuji day trips. |

**Nozomi vs Hikari:**

## 4. Hakone

**Hakone Freepass** (prices raised +¥1,000 on 1 Oct 2025):

| | 2-day | 3-day |
|---|---|---|
| **From Shinjuku** (incl. Odakyu round trip) | **¥7,100** | ¥7,500 |
| From Odawara (Hakone area only) | ¥6,000 | ¥6,400 |

**Covers 8 modes:** Odakyu Line (Shinjuku↔Odawara round trip + free Odawara–Hakone-Yumoto travel) · Hakone Tozan Railway · Tozan Cable Car · Hakone Ropeway (all sections) · Hakone Sightseeing Cruise / pirate ship (ordinary cabin) · Hakone Tozan Bus · Odakyu Highway Bus · Tokai Bus — all in designated zones. Plus discounts at ~70 facilities.

**Does NOT cover:** the Romancecar surcharge, ship Special Cabin (+¥500/segment), Izuhakone Group services (Komagatake ropeway), buses outside designated zones.

**Romancecar surcharge, Shinjuku → Hakone-Yumoto: ¥1,200 paper / ¥1,150 digital**, one way, **on top of** the Freepass. Romancecar ≈ **80 min direct**; regular express ≈ **120 min with a transfer at Odawara**. Odakyu's own worked example: ¥7,100 + ¥1,200 = ¥8,300.

**Odawara → Hakone-Yumoto without the pass:** ¥360, 14–15 min.

### Is the Freepass worth it? Yes — here's the loop arithmetic

| Segment | Fare |
|---|---|
| Odawara → Hakone-Yumoto | ¥360 |
| Hakone-Yumoto → Gora (Tozan train) | ¥460 |
| Gora → Sounzan (cable car) | ¥430 |
| Sounzan → Togendai (ropeway) | ¥2,000 *(was ¥1,500 before Oct 2025)* |
| Togendai → Moto-Hakone (pirate ship) | ¥1,700 *(was ¥1,200)* |
| Moto-Hakone → Hakone-Yumoto (bus) | ¥1,210 |
| Hakone-Yumoto → Odawara | ¥360 |

- **From Odawara:** ¥6,520 à la carte vs **¥6,000** pass → saves ¥520 (thin, but any extra bus hop widens it).
- **From Shinjuku:** swap the two ¥360 legs for ¥1,270 each way → ¥8,340 vs **¥7,100** pass → **saves ¥1,240.** Clear win.

**Buy the Shinjuku version, not the Odawara version.** Going Tokyo→Odawara by shinkansen (¥3,370) + Odawara pass (¥6,000) = ¥9,370, which is ¥2,270 *worse* than the ¥7,100 Shinjuku pass for a ~50-minute time saving.

Available **digitally via EMot** (same price as paper), sold to anyone (no passport restriction), and available at Odawara station, Tozan railway stations, Seven-Eleven and vending machines.

### Why it matters — the oversized baggage rule (confirmed on JR Central's official page)
- Baggage with **3 dimensions summing 160–250 cm** requires a **mandatory advance "Oversized Baggage Area" seat reservation** on the Tokaido/Sanyo Shinkansen.
- Over **250 cm total: banned outright.**
- The reservation is **free** — same price as a normal reserved seat.
- Boarding without one: **¥1,000 penalty**, and staff will make you stow it where directed.
- **Critically: you cannot bring oversized baggage into non-reserved cars at all.** So a large suitcase forces you out of the cheap non-reserved option.

👉 A typical 28-inch checked suitcase is ~160 cm total and lands right on the threshold. **Forward the big bags Tokyo→Kyoto for ¥3,200 and travel the Odawara→Kyoto leg with a daypack.** This is doubly valuable here because Hakone involves a ropeway, a boat and several bus transfers where full-size luggage is genuinely miserable — send the bags on the morning you leave Tokyo and they'll be at the Kyoto hotel when you arrive.

Toyosu is a modern district built on an artificial island in Tokyo Bay, located close to Odaiba. The area was originally created in the 1930s and has since been expanded and developed.

### 3. Tax-free shopping — **THIS CHANGES MID-TRIP**

- **From 1 November 2026**, Japan switches from exemption-at-the-register to **pay-then-refund-at-departure**. ([japan-guide](https://www.japan-guide.com/news/tax-free-shopping.html), [JNTO/japan.travel](https://www.japan.travel/en/ca/news/changes-are-coming-to-tax-free-shopping-in-japan/))
- If your trip straddles 1 Nov 2026, **purchases before that date use the old system** (10% deducted at checkout, sealed consumables bags), **purchases from 1 Nov use the new one** (you pay the full 10%, reclaim at the airport). Plan big purchases accordingly.
- New-system mechanics: minimum **¥5,000 pre-tax per store per day (unchanged)**; the ¥500,000 consumables cap is **abolished**; the general-goods/consumables split and the sealed-packaging rule are **abolished**; single **90-day** export window replaces the old 30-day/6-month split; at departure you process the claim at a **customs kiosk or via Visit Japan Web in the departure lobby before check-in**, then collect the refund by whatever method the store specified.
- **[UNCONFIRMED]** Refund method (cash vs. card vs. store-specific app) and whether a handling fee is deducted — official material only says "the method provided by the store."
- Already in force since 1 April 2025: goods shipped home by international parcel are no longer tax-exempt.

**Nationwide Japan Rail Pass — price rise on 1 October 2026** ([official price page](https://japanrailpass.net/en/purchase/price/), [Impress Watch](https://www.watch.impress.co.jp/docs/news/2100482.html)):

| | Ordinary (to 30 Sep) | **Ordinary (from 1 Oct 2026)** | Green (to 30 Sep) | **Green (from 1 Oct 2026)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7-day | ¥50,000 | **¥53,000** | ¥70,000 | **¥74,000** |
| 14-day | ¥80,000 | **¥84,000** | ¥110,000 | **¥116,000** |
| 21-day | ¥100,000 | **¥105,000** | ¥140,000 | **¥147,000** |

Child (6–11) is half: ¥27,000 / ¥42,000 / ¥53,000 ordinary from October.
**Important caveat:** the increase applies to overseas agents; JR said the **official web service (JAPAN RAIL PASS Reservation) will hold the old prices "for the time being"** to push direct sales, with no end date announced. japan-guide's rail-pass page (updated 2026) also states the rise applies "except for passes purchased through the official JR website." **[FLAG]** The official English price page presents the new prices without that carve-out, so verify at purchase time — potential ¥3,000 saving by buying direct.

**Nozomi/Mizuho supplement** (added Oct 2023): pass holders can ride Nozomi/Mizuho by buying a supplementary ticket. **Tokyo ⇄ Shin-Osaka: ¥4,960. Tokyo ⇄ Kyoto: ¥4,960.** Same price for green car, reserved and unreserved. ([japanrailpass.net special ticket](https://japanrailpass.net/en/use/special-ticket/))

**Relevant regional passes** (all via [japan-guide rail pass pages](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2361.html)):
- **JR Tokyo Wide Pass — ¥16,000 / 3 consecutive days** (child ¥8,000). Covers JR East Kanto + parts of Nagano/Niigata/Yamanashi/Shizuoka plus Izukyu, Fujikyu, Tobu-Nikko. **Does not cover the Tokaido Shinkansen** (JR Central) and does not cover Odakyu — so it is **useless for Tokyo→Odawara by Shinkansen and useless for Hakone**.
- **Hokuriku Arch Pass — ¥35,000 / 7 days.** Tokyo↔Osaka via the Hokuriku Shinkansen/Kanazawa; **explicitly excludes the Tokaido/Sanyo Shinkansen**. Only pays off if you actually route via Kanazawa. Wrong tool for your itinerary.
- **JR Kansai Area Pass** — ¥2,800 / ¥4,800 / ¥5,800 / ¥7,000 for 1/2/3/4 days. Local + rapid JR in Kansai, plus Haruka to KIX. **No Shinkansen.**
- **JR Kansai WIDE Area Pass** — ¥12,000 / 5 days; includes Sanyo Shinkansen Shin-Osaka–Okayama but **excludes the Tokaido Shinkansen Kyoto–Shin-Osaka**.
- **JR Kansai–Hiroshima Area Pass** — ¥17,000 / 5 days; includes Sanyo Shinkansen (incl. Nozomi/Mizuho) Shin-Osaka–Hiroshima. Only relevant if you add Hiroshima.
**[UNCONFIRMED]** Whether these JR East / JR West regional passes were repriced alongside the March 2026 JR East fare revision — the japan-guide pages were last updated 14 March 2026 and still show the prices above, which is good evidence but not an official confirmation.

**Break-even for Tokyo → Odawara → Kyoto → Shin-Osaka → Tokyo** (walk-up, regular season, ordinary car — fares itemised in §5):

| Build | Cost |
|---|---|
| All reserved, Nozomi on the return | ¥33,700 |
| All reserved, Hikari on the return | ¥33,380 |
| All unreserved | ¥30,370 |
| Mixed & cheapest sensible (unreserved Tokyo→Odawara, reserved Odawara→Kyoto, local train Kyoto→Osaka ¥580, Nozomi reserved Osaka→Tokyo) | ¥30,880 |

**Verdict: the nationwide 7-day pass is clearly NOT worth it.** At ¥50,000 (official web) you lose ~¥16,300; at ¥53,000 (agent, from 1 Oct) you lose ~¥19,300 — and that's before the ¥4,960 Nozomi supplement if you want the fast train. You'd need roughly **¥50,000+ of JR travel inside 7 consecutive days**; this route generates ~¥33,700. Even a plain Tokyo⇄Shin-Osaka round trip by reserved Nozomi is only ¥29,440. The pass would only start to make sense if you bolt on something like a Hiroshima or Tohoku round trip. Note also the pass covers **none** of the Hakone leg (Odakyu, Tozan railway, ropeway, boats are all private).
**Better play:** buy point-to-point, and use **Smart EX (free) or EX予約 (¥1,100/yr)** for the Tokaido Shinkansen legs — Smart EX knocks ~¥200 off reserved seats and EX予約 more, and both let you reserve from abroad.
