## Japan 10-Night Accommodation Plan — Nov 2026, 2 people

**Critical framing:** it is August 2026. November is ~3 months out, so this is not a "how early should we book" question anymore — it's a **book in the next 2–4 weeks** question. Details in §5.

---

### 1. TOKYO — 4 nights

**Recommendation: Tokyo Station area, specifically the Kyobashi / Nihonbashi / Hatchobori side of Chuo-ku** (not Marunouchi's office blocks, which die after 21:00).

Why it wins for this itinerary: you drag luggage to a Shinkansen twice (Hakone, Kyoto). The Tokaido Shinkansen *originates* at Tokyo Station — you board an empty train and get luggage space. Kyoto is direct; Odawara (Hakone) is ~35–40 min by Kodama. You also get Yamanote, five subway lines, N'EX direct from Narita (55 min), the ¥1,500 Airport Bus TYO-NRT, and Asakusa Line service toward Haneda. Deep business-hotel supply in your band, safe/quiet streets, 10 min walk to Ginza.

**Runner-up: Shinjuku.** Best raw network reach and the only *direct* Odakyu Romancecar to Hakone-Yumoto (~85 min), plus unmatched nightlife. Costs: Shinjuku Station is genuinely disorienting for four days, and you must book west or south side, **not inside Kabukicho**.

Quick verdict on the others: Shibuya (great, but pricier and fewer twins under ¥28k), Ueno (best Narita access via Skyliner 41 min/¥2,580, ~20–30% cheaper, but no Tokaido Shinkansen), Asakusa (**no Yamanote line** — real handicap), Ginza (excellent but priciest per m² and dead late).

| Hotel | Station | Large bath | Est. Nov 2026, twin, 2 people |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sotetsu Fresa Inn Tokyo-Kyobashi** | Kyobashi 2 min, Tokyo Stn 8 min walk | No | **¥19,000–26,000** |
| **Dormy Inn PREMIUM Tokyo Kodenmacho** | Kodenmacho 20 sec (Hibiya) | **Yes** — 11F open-air w/ skyline, sauna | **¥23,000–31,000** (breakfast included) |
| **Dormy Inn Tokyo Hatchobori Natural Hot Spring** | Hatchobori 2 min | **Yes** — genuine natural onsen + rotenburo | **¥25,000–35,000** |

Notes: Fresa Inn rooms are small even by Tokyo standards — book a **twin**, not a double, and not the cheapest class. Free Sotetsu Hotels Club membership + direct booking gets you 14:00 check-in / 12:00 check-out. Dormy chain includes free late-night ramen (*yonaki soba*). Kodenmacho's included breakfast offsets ~¥3,000–5,000/night vs the Fresa.

Mitsui Garden Kyobashi and Dormy Inn Premium Ginza are both excellent but running ~¥37,000–42,000 — above band in November.

---

### 2. HAKONE — 1 night (the splurge)

**Base: Gora** if the classic loop is the priority (it's the hinge — end of the Tozan railway, start of the cablecar), or **Tonosawa/Hakone-Yumoto** if the ryokan itself is the priority. Both keep you on the rail line, so the morning departure is clean: Tozan → Hakone-Yumoto → Odakyu 15 min → Odawara → **Hikari** Shinkansen to Kyoto (~2h05). *Nozomi does not stop at Odawara.*

**Skip Sengokuhara** for a single night — it's bus-only, off the loop, awkward in both directions with luggage.

Foliage by elevation: Sengokuhara/Owakudani peak earliest (late Oct–mid Nov), Gora/Miyanoshita mid-to-late Nov, Yumoto/Tonosawa latest. **Nov 10–19 is the widest overlap.**

| Ryokan | Location | Per person, 2 meals | Tattoos | Private bath |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Setsugetsuka** (季の湯 雪月花) | Gora, 1 min from station | **¥25,460–26,480 weekday** / ¥29,540–34,630 Sat | Not stated; assume communal bath restricted | **All 158 rooms have private hinoki open-air bath**, plus 3 free kashikiri baths, no reservation |
| **Yama no Chaya** (山の茶屋) | Tonosawa, 15 rooms | **~¥36,400** | **Explicitly tattoo-friendly** — their own FAQ says yes to the public bath, no covering required. Rare. | 11 of 15 rooms have private open-air baths; kashikiri ¥5,500/45 min, only 8 slots/day, first-come at check-in |
| **Hakone Ginyu** (吟遊) | Miyanoshita, 20 rooms, cliff over gorge | **¥46,750–69,740** | Not published; assume communal restricted | All rooms have private open-air bath + terrace; rental bath available |
| *Alt:* **Kowakien Ten-yu** | Kowakidani, shuttle from Gora | from ¥47,190 weekday | Communal bath **not** open to tattooed guests | All 150 rooms have private open-air bath |

**My pick: Yama no Chaya on a Tue–Thu around Nov 10–19.** Tattoo-friendly in the public bath (genuinely rare), atmospheric, 15 rooms, 5 min from Hakone-Yumoto for both arrival and the Kyoto departure. **Setsugetsuka is the better-value alternative** at ~¥26k weekday with an in-room open-air bath in every room.

Honest read on the ¥45k band: in foliage season that buys you the *entry plan on a weekday* at Ginyu or Ten-yu, not a good room on a Saturday. ¥35k at Yama no Chaya gets you more.

**Ryokan mechanics:** check-in 15:00 with a **hard arrival cutoff** for meal plans — Yoshiike requires 17:00, Yama no Chaya closes check-in at 18:00, Setsugetsuka seats dinner at 17:15/19:45. Plan to arrive by 16:30. Check-out is 10:00 at traditional ryokan, 11:00 at resort-style. **Hakone bathing tax ¥150/person/night** on top of quoted rates. No lodging tax — Hakone announced one but it starts April 2028.

---

### 3. KYOTO — 3 nights

**Recommendation: Downtown — Shijo-Karasuma / Karasuma-Oike.**

The key fact most older advice misses: **the ¥700 one-day bus pass was abolished** (accepted through March 2024; replacement is the ¥1,100 Subway & Bus pass), specifically to push tourists onto the subway. In foliage season the buses are the failure mode — routes along Shijo and around Kyoto Station fill to capacity and drive past your stop.

Downtown is the only area that puts you on the **subway spine and within walking distance of dinner**. Karasuma Line to Kyoto Station in ~5 min; Tozai Line at Karasuma-Oike for Higashiyama; Hankyu Kawaramachi direct to Osaka-Umeda (43 min, ¥410); Nishiki, Pontocho, Kiyamachi, Gion all on foot. That last point matters enormously when you come back cold at 17:30 and do *not* want another packed bus. You can also walk to Gion for dawn temple visits — the actual crowd-avoidance strategy.

**Runner-up: Kyoto Station area** — better for heavy day-tripping (Nara, Himeji) and luggage days, but the dining is malls and chains.

**Not as a base:** Higashiyama/Gion has **no subway station** — bus/taxi dependent, exactly what breaks in November. Arashiyama empties at night (last orders ~18:30) and is a two-train transfer away.

| Hotel | Station | Large bath | Est. Nov 2026, twin |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Mitsui Garden Hotel Kyoto Sanjo PREMIER** | Karasuma-Oike / Sanjo | **Yes** — 90 m² cave-motif bath, free, 15:00–25:00 & 06:00–09:00 | ¥20,000–26,000 early Nov; ¥30,000–40,000 peak. **Check-out 12:00** |
| **Mitsui Garden Kyoto Kawaramachi Jokyoji** | Teramachi arcade, just off Shijo — dead center | **Yes** — free, 2F | similar |
| **Dormy Inn Premium Kyoto Ekimae** | 3 min from Kyoto Stn | **Yes** — real natural hot spring (Jōyō onsen source) | ¥16,000–22,000 early Nov; ¥26,000–35,000+ Nov 18–21 |
| *Budget anchor:* **Almont Hotel Kyoto** | 5 min, Kyoto Stn Hachijo East | Yes, spa/large bath | Own site advertises from ¥6,500/person w/ breakfast = **~¥13,000 for two** (low-season floor). **Check-in 14:00** |

**Useful trick — Mitsui's Kyoto Baggage Service:** ¥500/piece between Kyoto Station and four Mitsui Garden properties. Drop at the station by noon on arrival, collect at your hotel from 15:00; reverse on departure. Solves the worst luggage moments of a Kyoto stay.

**Foliage timing wrinkle:** 2026 is forecast to run **late** (warm summer). Central temples ~Nov 18–Dec 2, Tofuku-ji/Arashiyama ~Nov 22–Dec 5, city-wide peak density ~Nov 29–Dec 3. So **Nov 18–21 is the front edge of color, not the peak** — arguably the sweet spot: real color at the central temples, ahead of the worst crush. The authoritative Japanese forecasts (Weathernews, tenki.jp) publish in **September** — re-check before locking non-refundable rates.

---

### 4. OSAKA — 2 nights

**Recommendation: Namba.** For a 2-night stay you effectively have one full day and two evenings, and the evenings *are* the trip. Dotonbori, Kuromon Market, and Shinsekai are walkable from Namba; from Umeda they're a subway ride each way. Namba also has the **direct Nankai to Kansai Airport** (~45 min, ~¥970, no transfer) — Umeda has no direct KIX rail link — and Kintetsu to Nara, which drops you far closer to the deer park than JR Nara.

Umeda's counter-case: better for Kyoto (Hankyu to Kawaramachi, 43 min/¥410) and marginally better for Shin-Osaka. But Namba→Shin-Osaka on the Midosuji Line is direct and barely longer, so that edge is small while Namba's walkability edge is large.

Candidates in band: **Dormy Inn Premium Namba** (large communal bath, well regarded), **Sotetsu Fresa Inn Osaka Namba**, **Mitsui Garden Hotel Osaka Japan-Bashi**, **Hotel Gracery Osaka Namba**. Osaka has **no foliage premium**, so ¥15,000–22,000 for a twin is realistic — this should be the easy part of the trip. I was not able to verify per-property November rates to the same standard as Tokyo/Kyoto; treat this as a shortlist to price yourself.

---

### 5. November demand reality — you are late, but not shut out

Standard guidance for foliage season is 4–6 months ahead for hotels, 10–12 months for famous ryokan. Industry reporting from July 2026 said **premium Kyoto ryokan for the late-November window were expected to sell out by August** and called end-of-July the last realistic booking window for top-tier properties.

You are past that for the trophy properties but fine for your actual target segment. Business-hotel chains — Dormy, Mitsui Garden, Sotetsu, Almont — release and re-release inventory much closer in than ryokan do.

**Concretely:**
- **Book Hakone this week or next.** Yama no Chaya has 15 rooms, Ginyu has 20. A mid-November Saturday may already be gone; weekdays should still be open.
- **Book Kyoto within 2–3 weeks.** Mid-November pushes Kyoto rates **30–60% above baseline**, and it is the second-most expensive window of the year after cherry blossom. Saturdays go first.
- **Tokyo and Osaka can wait another few weeks** but there's no advantage in waiting — take free-cancellation rates now.
- **If you book late (October):** expect 2–3× premiums on what's left in Kyoto, and expect the *survivors* to be the properties nobody wanted — bad locations, single beds, or Otsu (10 min by train, ~40% cheaper, and the genuine fallback if Kyoto proper is picked clean).

**Date engineering is your biggest lever.** Japanese ryokan price on 平日 (weekday) vs 休前日 (Saturday/pre-holiday, which includes Fridays). Setsugetsuka's own published rates show it: **¥25,460 weekday vs ¥34,630 pre-holiday** — ~30% for the identical room.

**Avoid: Nov 1–2** (eve of Culture Day, Tue Nov 3) and **Nov 20–23** (Sat/Sun/Mon three-day weekend around Labor Thanksgiving Day, Mon Nov 23) — that last one collides exactly with Gora's foliage peak and is the worst stretch of the month for both price and availability. **Target Mon–Thu nights in the Nov 9–19 window.**

---

### 6. Practical notes

**Check-in/out.** Japanese business hotels are rigid: 15:00 in, 10:00–11:00 out. Exploitable exceptions: Sotetsu Fresa Inn 14:00/12:00 with free membership + direct booking; Almont Kyoto and Hotel Gracery check in at 14:00; Mitsui Garden Kyoto Sanjo PREMIER checks out at 12:00.

**Luggage.** Every hotel listed will hold bags free before check-in and after check-out — universal at Japanese business hotels, rarely advertised, just ask. **For Hakone, forward instead:** send the big suitcases **Tokyo hotel → Kyoto hotel** via Yamato takkyubin and take an overnight bag to Hakone. This matters more than usual — the Tozan railway's switchback cars, cablecars, ropeway gondolas, and ryokan stairs are all hostile to suitcases. Cost ~¥1,650–2,530 per case, **next-day delivery**; hand it over the morning you leave for Hakone and it's waiting in Kyoto when you arrive. Same-day Tokyo→Kyoto isn't reliable, which is why the Hakone night is the perfect buffer.

**Breakfast: assume NOT included** unless stated. Dormy Inn Premium Kodenmacho includes it. Otherwise Sotetsu ¥1,650/person, Mitsui Garden ~¥2,420, KOKO ¥1,800, Dormy Ginza ¥2,500. At ¥3,300–5,000 per couple per morning, a konbini or standing-soba breakfast is often better value. Ryokan rates always include dinner + breakfast.

**Accommodation tax — smaller than the headlines suggest.** The key mechanic: **the tax band is set by the per-person rate = room total ÷ number of occupants.** Kyoto City's own operator guidance gives the worked example (¥20,000 ÷ 2 = ¥10,000/person). Sharing a room routinely drops you a full band.

- **Tokyo:** under ¥10,000/person exempt; ¥10,000–14,999 → ¥100/person/night; ¥15,000+ → ¥200. A room under ¥20,000 is **fully exempt**; ¥20,000–28,000 costs ¥100/person. Worst case 4 nights × 2 people = **¥800**. *The April 2027 switch to a 3% levy does not apply to you.*
- **Kyoto (new bands from March 1, 2026):** under ¥6,000 → ¥200; ¥6,000–19,999 → ¥400; ¥20,000–49,999 → ¥1,000; ¥50,000–99,999 → ¥4,000; ¥100,000+ → ¥10,000. A ¥25,000 double = ¥12,500/person → **¥400/person/night = ¥800/night**, so **¥2,400 for 3 nights**. The scary ¥10,000 headline targets ¥100,000+/person luxury only. Note the band uses the **room-only, pre-consumption-tax** figure — meal charges are stripped out first, which can push you down a band. Beware: several widely-circulated travel articles get the shared-room math wrong by up to 4×.
- **Osaka:** prefectural, low band applies — roughly **¥200–400/night for two**, under ¥800 for both nights. (I got conflicting figures from secondary sources and couldn't reach the prefecture's official page; it doesn't affect any decision at your budget.)
- **Hakone:** no lodging tax; **bathing tax ¥150/person/night**.

<result>## Japan 10-Night Accommodation Plan — Nov 2026, 2 people

**Critical framing:** it is August 2026. November is ~3 months out, so this is not a "how early should we book" question anymore — it's a **book in the next 2–4 weeks** question. Details in §5.

---

### 1. TOKYO — 4 nights

**Recommendation: Tokyo Station area, specifically the Kyobashi / Nihonbashi / Hatchobori side of Chuo-ku** (not Marunouchi's office blocks, which die after 21:00).

Why it wins for this itinerary: you drag luggage to a Shinkansen twice (Hakone, Kyoto). The Tokaido Shinkansen *originates* at Tokyo Station — you board an empty train and get luggage space. Kyoto is direct; Odawara (Hakone) is ~35–40 min by Kodama. You also get Yamanote, five subway lines, N'EX direct from Narita (55 min), the ¥1,500 Airport Bus TYO-NRT, and Asakusa Line service toward Haneda. Deep business-hotel supply in your band, safe/quiet streets, 10 min walk to Ginza.

**Runner-up: Shinjuku.** Best raw network reach and the only *direct* Odakyu Romancecar to Hakone-Yumoto (~85 min), plus unmatched nightlife. Costs: Shinjuku Station is genuinely disorienting for four days, and you must book west or south side, **not inside Kabukicho**.

Quick verdict on the others: Shibuya (great, but pricier and fewer twins under ¥28k), Ueno (best Narita access via Skyliner 41 min/¥2,580, ~20–30% cheaper, but no Tokaido Shinkansen), Asakusa (**no Yamanote line** — real handicap), Ginza (excellent but priciest per m² and dead late).

| Hotel | Station | Large bath | Est. Nov 2026, twin, 2 people |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sotetsu Fresa Inn Tokyo-Kyobashi** | Kyobashi 2 min, Tokyo Stn 8 min walk | No | **¥19,000–26,000** |
| **Dormy Inn PREMIUM Tokyo Kodenmacho** | Kodenmacho 20 sec (Hibiya) | **Yes** — 11F open-air w/ skyline, sauna | **¥23,000–31,000** (breakfast included) |
| **Dormy Inn Tokyo Hatchobori Natural Hot Spring** | Hatchobori 2 min | **Yes** — genuine natural onsen + rotenburo | **¥25,000–35,000** |

Notes: Fresa Inn rooms are small even by Tokyo standards — book a **twin**, not a double, and not the cheapest class. Free Sotetsu Hotels Club membership + direct booking gets you 14:00 check-in / 12:00 check-out. Dormy chain includes free late-night ramen (*yonaki soba*). Kodenmacho's included breakfast offsets ~¥3,000–5,000/night vs the Fresa.

Mitsui Garden Kyobashi and Dormy Inn Premium Ginza are both excellent but running ~¥37,000–42,000 — above band in November.

---

### 2. HAKONE — 1 night (the splurge)

**Base: Gora** if the classic loop is the priority (it's the hinge — end of the Tozan railway, start of the cablecar), or **Tonosawa/Hakone-Yumoto** if the ryokan itself is the priority. Both keep you on the rail line, so the morning departure is clean: Tozan → Hakone-Yumoto → Odakyu 15 min → Odawara → **Hikari** Shinkansen to Kyoto (~2h05). *Nozomi does not stop at Odawara.*

**Skip Sengokuhara** for a single night — it's bus-only, off the loop, awkward in both directions with luggage.

Foliage by elevation: Sengokuhara/Owakudani peak earliest (late Oct–mid Nov), Gora/Miyanoshita mid-to-late Nov, Yumoto/Tonosawa latest. **Nov 10–19 is the widest overlap.**

| Ryokan | Location | Per person, 2 meals | Tattoos | Private bath |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Setsugetsuka** (季の湯 雪月花) | Gora, 1 min from station | **¥25,460–26,480 weekday** / ¥29,540–34,630 Sat | Not stated; assume communal bath restricted | **All 158 rooms have private hinoki open-air bath**, plus 3 free kashikiri baths, no reservation |
| **Yama no Chaya** (山の茶屋) | Tonosawa, 15 rooms | **~¥36,400** | **Explicitly tattoo-friendly** — their own FAQ says yes to the public bath, no covering required. Rare. | 11 of 15 rooms have private open-air baths; kashikiri ¥5,500/45 min, only 8 slots/day, first-come at check-in |
| **Hakone Ginyu** (吟遊) | Miyanoshita, 20 rooms, cliff over gorge | **¥46,750–69,740** | Not published; assume communal restricted | All rooms have private open-air bath + terrace; rental bath available |
| *Alt:* **Kowakien Ten-yu** | Kowakidani, shuttle from Gora | from ¥47,190 weekday | Communal bath **not** open to tattooed guests | All 150 rooms have private open-air bath |

**My pick: Yama no Chaya on a Tue–Thu around Nov 10–19.** Tattoo-friendly in the public bath (genuinely rare), atmospheric, 15 rooms, 5 min from Hakone-Yumoto for both arrival and the Kyoto departure. **Setsugetsuka is the better-value alternative** at ~¥26k weekday with an in-room open-air bath in every room.

Honest read on the ¥45k band: in foliage season that buys you the *entry plan on a weekday* at Ginyu or Ten-yu, not a good room on a Saturday. ¥35k at Yama no Chaya gets you more.

**Ryokan mechanics:** check-in 15:00 with a **hard arrival cutoff** for meal plans — Yoshiike requires 17:00, Yama no Chaya closes check-in at 18:00, Setsugetsuka seats dinner at 17:15/19:45. Plan to arrive by 16:30. Check-out is 10:00 at traditional ryokan, 11:00 at resort-style. **Hakone bathing tax ¥150/person/night** on top of quoted rates. No lodging tax — Hakone announced one but it starts April 2028.

---

### 3. KYOTO — 3 nights

**Recommendation: Downtown — Shijo-Karasuma / Karasuma-Oike.**

The key fact most older advice misses: **the ¥700 one-day bus pass was abolished** (accepted through March 2024; replacement is the ¥1,100 Subway & Bus pass), specifically to push tourists onto the subway. In foliage season the buses are the failure mode — routes along Shijo and around Kyoto Station fill to capacity and drive past your stop.

Downtown is the only area that puts you on the **subway spine and within walking distance of dinner**. Karasuma Line to Kyoto Station in ~5 min; Tozai Line at Karasuma-Oike for Higashiyama; Hankyu Kawaramachi direct to Osaka-Umeda (43 min, ¥410); Nishiki, Pontocho, Kiyamachi, Gion all on foot. That last point matters enormously when you come back cold at 17:30 and do *not* want another packed bus. You can also walk to Gion for dawn temple visits — the actual crowd-avoidance strategy.

**Runner-up: Kyoto Station area** — better for heavy day-tripping (Nara, Himeji) and luggage days, but the dining is malls and chains.

**Not as a base:** Higashiyama/Gion has **no subway station** — bus/taxi dependent, exactly what breaks in November. Arashiyama empties at night (last orders ~18:30) and is a two-train transfer away.

| Hotel | Station | Large bath | Est. Nov 2026, twin |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Mitsui Garden Hotel Kyoto Sanjo PREMIER** | Karasuma-Oike / Sanjo | **Yes** — 90 m² cave-motif bath, free, 15:00–25:00 & 06:00–09:00 | ¥20,000–26,000 early Nov; ¥30,000–40,000 peak. **Check-out 12:00** |
| **Mitsui Garden Kyoto Kawaramachi Jokyoji** | Teramachi arcade, just off Shijo — dead center | **Yes** — free, 2F | similar |
| **Dormy Inn Premium Kyoto Ekimae** | 3 min from Kyoto Stn | **Yes** — real natural hot spring (Jōyō onsen source) | ¥16,000–22,000 early Nov; ¥26,000–35,000+ Nov 18–21 |
| *Budget anchor:* **Almont Hotel Kyoto** | 5 min, Kyoto Stn Hachijo East | Yes, spa/large bath | Own site advertises from ¥6,500/person w/ breakfast = **~¥13,000 for two** (low-season floor). **Check-in 14:00** |

**Useful trick — Mitsui's Kyoto Baggage Service:** ¥500/piece between Kyoto Station and four Mitsui Garden properties. Drop at the station by noon on arrival, collect at your hotel from 15:00; reverse on departure. Solves the worst luggage moments of a Kyoto stay.

**Foliage timing wrinkle:** 2026 is forecast to run **late** (warm summer). Central temples ~Nov 18–Dec 2, Tofuku-ji/Arashiyama ~Nov 22–Dec 5, city-wide peak density ~Nov 29–Dec 3. So **Nov 18–21 is the front edge of color, not the peak** — arguably the sweet spot: real color at the central temples, ahead of the worst crush. The authoritative Japanese forecasts (Weathernews, tenki.jp) publish in **September** — re-check before locking non-refundable rates.

---

### 4. OSAKA — 2 nights

**Recommendation: Namba.** For a 2-night stay you effectively have one full day and two evenings, and the evenings *are* the trip. Dotonbori, Kuromon Market, and Shinsekai are walkable from Namba; from Umeda they're a subway ride each way. Namba also has the **direct Nankai to Kansai Airport** (~45 min, ~¥970, no transfer) — Umeda has no direct KIX rail link — and Kintetsu to Nara, which drops you far closer to the deer park than JR Nara.

Umeda's counter-case: better for Kyoto (Hankyu to Kawaramachi, 43 min/¥410) and marginally better for Shin-Osaka. But Namba→Shin-Osaka on the Midosuji Line is direct and barely longer, so that edge is small while Namba's walkability edge is large.

Candidates in band: **Dormy Inn Premium Namba** (large communal bath, well regarded), **Sotetsu Fresa Inn Osaka Namba**, **Mitsui Garden Hotel Osaka Japan-Bashi**, **Hotel Gracery Osaka Namba**. Osaka has **no foliage premium**, so ¥15,000–22,000 for a twin is realistic — this should be the easy part of the trip. I was not able to verify per-property November rates to the same standard as Tokyo/Kyoto; treat this as a shortlist to price yourself.

---

### 5. November demand reality — you are late, but not shut out

Standard guidance for foliage season is 4–6 months ahead for hotels, 10–12 months for famous ryokan. Industry reporting from July 2026 said **premium Kyoto ryokan for the late-November window were expected to sell out by August** and called end-of-July the last realistic booking window for top-tier properties.

You are past that for the trophy properties but fine for your actual target segment. Business-hotel chains — Dormy, Mitsui Garden, Sotetsu, Almont — release and re-release inventory much closer in than ryokan do.

**Concretely:**
- **Book Hakone this week or next.** Yama no Chaya has 15 rooms, Ginyu has 20. A mid-November Saturday may already be gone; weekdays should still be open.
- **Book Kyoto within 2–3 weeks.** Mid-November pushes Kyoto rates **30–60% above baseline**, and it is the second-most expensive window of the year after cherry blossom. Saturdays go first.
- **Tokyo and Osaka can wait another few weeks** but there's no advantage in waiting — take free-cancellation rates now.
- **If you book late (October):** expect 2–3× premiums on what's left in Kyoto, and expect the *survivors* to be the properties nobody wanted — bad locations, single beds, or Otsu (10 min by train, ~40% cheaper, and the genuine fallback if Kyoto proper is picked clean).

**Date engineering is your biggest lever.** Japanese ryokan price on 平日 (weekday) vs 休前日 (Saturday/pre-holiday, which includes Fridays). Setsugetsuka's own published rates show it: **¥25,460 weekday vs ¥34,630 pre-holiday** — ~30% for the identical room.

**Avoid: Nov 1–2** (eve of Culture Day, Tue Nov 3) and **Nov 20–23** (Sat/Sun/Mon three-day weekend around Labor Thanksgiving Day, Mon Nov 23) — that last one collides exactly with Gora's foliage peak and is the worst stretch of the month for both price and availability. **Target Mon–Thu nights in the Nov 9–19 window.**

---

### 6. Practical notes

**Check-in/out.** Japanese business hotels are rigid: 15:00 in, 10:00–11:00 out. Exploitable exceptions: Sotetsu Fresa Inn 14:00/12:00 with free membership + direct booking; Almont Kyoto and Hotel Gracery check in at 14:00; Mitsui Garden Kyoto Sanjo PREMIER checks out at 12:00.

**Luggage.** Every hotel listed will hold bags free before check-in and after check-out — universal at Japanese business hotels, rarely advertised, just ask. **For Hakone, forward instead:** send the big suitcases **Tokyo hotel → Kyoto hotel** via Yamato takkyubin and take an overnight bag to Hakone. This matters more than usual — the Tozan railway's switchback cars, cablecars, ropeway gondolas, and ryokan stairs are all hostile to suitcases. Cost ~¥1,650–2,530 per case, **next-day delivery**; hand it over the morning you leave for Hakone and it's waiting in Kyoto when you arrive. Same-day Tokyo→Kyoto isn't reliable, which is why the Hakone night is the perfect buffer.

**Breakfast: assume NOT included** unless stated. Dormy Inn Premium Kodenmacho includes it. Otherwise Sotetsu ¥1,650/person, Mitsui Garden ~¥2,420, KOKO ¥1,800, Dormy Ginza ¥2,500. At ¥3,300–5,000 per couple per morning, a konbini or standing-soba breakfast is often better value. Ryokan rates always include dinner + breakfast.

**Accommodation tax — smaller than the headlines suggest.** The key mechanic: **the tax band is set by the per-person rate = room total ÷ number of occupants.** Kyoto City's own operator guidance gives the worked example (¥20,000 ÷ 2 = ¥10,000/person). Sharing a room routinely drops you a full band.

- **Tokyo:** under ¥10,000/person exempt; ¥10,000–14,999 → ¥100/person/night; ¥15,000+ → ¥200. A room under ¥20,000 is **fully exempt**; ¥20,000–28,000 costs ¥100/person. Worst case 4 nights × 2 people = **¥800**. *The April 2027 switch to a 3% levy does not apply to you.*
- **Kyoto (new bands from March 1, 2026):** under ¥6,000 → ¥200; ¥6,000–19,999 → ¥400; ¥20,000–49,999 → ¥1,000; ¥50,000–99,999 → ¥4,000; ¥100,000+ → ¥10,000. A ¥25,000 double = ¥12,500/person → **¥400/person/night = ¥800/night**, so **¥2,400 for 3 nights**. The scary ¥10,000 headline targets ¥100,000+/person luxury only. Note the band uses the **room-only, pre-consumption-tax** figure — meal charges are stripped out first, which can push you down a band. Beware: several widely-circulated travel articles get the shared-room math wrong by up to 4×.
- **Osaka:** prefectural, low band applies — roughly **¥200–400/night for two**, under ¥800 for both nights. (I got conflicting figures from secondary sources and couldn't reach the prefecture's official page; it doesn't affect any decision at your budget.)
- **Hakone:** no lodging tax; **bathing tax ¥150/person/night**.

---

### Accommodation subtotal

Assuming **Mon–Thu-leaning dates in the Nov 9–19 window**:

| Tokyo (Kyobashi/Nihonbashi business hotel) | 4 | ¥22,000 | ¥88,000 |
| Hakone (Yama no Chaya, ~¥36.4k/person, 2 meals) | 1 | ¥73,000 | ¥73,000 |

**Scenario range:**
- **Lean** (Setsugetsuka in Hakone at ¥52,000, Almont/Dormy weekday rates elsewhere): **~¥225,000**
- **Mid** (above): **~¥281,000**
- **High** (Ginyu in Hakone ~¥94,000, weekend dates, Kyoto at peak): **~¥355,000**

**Swapping Hakone alone moves the total by ¥42,000** — it's the single biggest lever, and Setsugetsuka gives you an in-room private open-air bath at half Ginyu's price.

---

### Honest caveats

**I could not retrieve live November 2026 quotes.** Booking.com, Agoda, Trip.com and the official Sotetsu/Dormy booking engines all returned JS-only shells to automated fetching, including with explicit November 2026 date parameters. Everything in the rate columns is **modelled from published "from" rates, TripAdvisor average bands, and Kayak seasonality data** — treat as **±25%**. What *is* verified from official hotel sites: every property's existence and current operation, station distances, bath facilities, check-in/out times, and breakfast pricing. The Hakone ryokan rates come from the Hakone Ryokan Association's published rate listings, which are reliable but are list rates, not availability.

Two other soft spots: the 2026 foliage forecast is travel-media projection until the Japanese meteorological services publish in September, and I could not verify Osaka per-property rates or adjudicate the conflicting Osaka tax figures.

**One action item:** price 4 consecutive Sun–Thu nights yourself on Booking.com or Agoda and lock free-cancellation rates now. At three months out you still have real choice; by late September in this band, you likely won't.

## Japan — November 2026 events research

Verified today (2026-08-09) via live sources. Anything not yet officially announced is flagged.

---

### 1. Tori-no-ichi 2026 — CONFIRMED

**2026 is a "ni-no-tori" year: only TWO fairs, no San-no-tori.**

| | Date | Day |
|---|---|---|
| **Ichi-no-tori** | **Sat 7 November 2026** | 赤口 |
| **Ni-no-tori** | **Thu 19 November 2026** | 友引 |

Confirmed by the official Asakusa Tori-no-ichi site (https://torinoichi.jp/ — "本年は二の酉のため、11月7日(土)、19日(木)"), by Washi/Otori Shrine's own site (https://otorisama.or.jp/kotoshi.html), and by https://www.taian-calendar.com/festival-for-money-business/torinoichi/torinoichi-2026.html. (The next rooster day after Nov 19 is Dec 1, hence no third fair.)

**Caution:** several English pages (e.g. https://www.japanistry.com/event/tori-no-ichi-2-hanazono-shrine/, the Magical-Trip guides) still show **Nov 12 & 24 — those are 2025 dates and are wrong for 2026.**

**Venues**
- **Otori Shrine (鷲神社), Asakusa** — 3-18-7 Senzoku, Taito-ku. Official hours **00:00–24:00** (full 24 h), kicked off by the *ichiban-daiko* drum at midnight. **Yoimiya (宵宮開運福寿祭): Fri 6 Nov 23:15 and Wed 18 Nov 23:15** — explicitly listed on https://otorisama.or.jp/kotoshi.html. This is the largest fair in Tokyo.
- **Juzaisan Chokoku-ji (鷲在山 長國寺)** — 3-19-6 Senzoku, Taito-ku, immediately adjacent to Otori Shrine; same two dates, same overnight running (https://torinoichi.jp/link/).
- **Hanazono Shrine (花園神社), Shinjuku** — 5-17-3 Shinjuku. Runs a 4-day format: eve (前夜祭) + main day for each tori. 2025 was 11 Nov eve / 12 Nov main and 23 Nov eve / 24 Nov main (https://www.enjoytokyo.jp/event/389312/). **By that pattern 2026 = eve Fri 6 Nov + main Sat 7 Nov, eve Wed 18 Nov + main Thu 19 Nov — INFERRED, not yet posted by the shrine** (hanazono-jinja.or.jp was unreachable at time of research; tel 03-3209-5265). ~600,000 visitors; famous for the *misemono-goya* freak-show tent and Kabukicho crowds.
- **Ohtori Shrine (大鳥神社), Meguro** — 3-1-2 Shimomeguro, 3 min from Meguro Stn. Same two dates. Typical hours roughly **08:00–23:00**, with *kumade-no-mai* rake dance from **19:00** (https://www.walkerplus.com/event/ar0313e324282/, https://omatsurijapan.com/search/m/2374/) — **times are past-year/typical, not a 2026 announcement.**

Ichi-no-tori falling on a **Saturday** in 2026 means unusually heavy crowds.

---

### 2. Meiji Jingu Gaien Ginkgo Festival (いちょう祭り) — **effectively DISCONTINUED; treat as not happening**

- The festival has **not been held since 2019**. Cancelled 2020–22 for COVID, and **2023, 2024, 2025 cancelled due to the Jingu Gaien redevelopment works**. The official site (https://www.meijijingugaien.jp/event/) still shows **15 Nov – 1 Dec 2019** as the last edition; no 2026 dates anywhere.
- What survives is the craft market, renamed **「森の職人展」(Mori no Shokunin-ten)** — 2025 ran approx **21 Nov – 7 Dec 2025**.
- **Ginkgo avenue light-up 2025: 22–30 Nov 2025, approx. 16:30–19:30** (https://www.enjoytokyo.jp/event/2000799/). **No 2026 dates announced.** Expect a similar late-Nov window; check meijijingugaien.jp from ~October.
- **Peak foliage**: typically ~20 Nov to early December.
- **Redevelopment**: the Jingu Gaien District Type-1 Urban Redevelopment (Meiji Jingu Baseball Stadium + Chichibunomiya Rugby Stadium rebuild/site-swap, plus two ~190 m towers and an 80 m tower) is **actively under construction as of 2026**. The 1923 ginkgo avenue itself still stands and is viewable, but **access routes, closures and surrounding scenery change with construction progress**; the Gaien site's 重要なお知らせ currently carries notices on redevelopment and weekend/holiday road restrictions. Context: https://www.english.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/w/000-101-000786, https://www.cnn.com/style/tokyo-jingu-gaien-redevelopment-project-hnk-intl/index.html, and the ICOMOS "Heritage Alert" campaign (225,000+ petition signatures).

---

### 3. Hakone Daimyo Gyoretsu — Nov 3, 2026 (high confidence, not yet formally posted)

- Held **every year on 3 November (Culture Day)**; 2026 = **Tuesday 3 Nov**. The **72nd** edition was 3 Nov 2025; 2026 would be the **73rd**. Hakone Tourism Association (https://www.hakone.or.jp/6321) states the fixed 3 Nov date but **has not yet published a 2026 page** — flag as expected-but-unconfirmed.
- **Route/timings (2025 actual, https://www.hakone-ryokan.or.jp/blog/10119.html — use as the template):**
  - 09:30 opening ceremony at the **Hatajuku Ichirizuka** (old Tokaido), ~20 *yakko* performers
  - **11:30 depart Hotel Nanpuso** (Yumoto onsen, Taki-dori)
  - 12:00 arrive **Tenseien** — lunch break
  - 13:30 depart Tenseien
  - 14:00 depart Onsen-guchi
  - **15:00 arrive Yumoto Fujiya Hotel** (finish)
  - Main leg runs along **National Route 1** through Hakone-Yumoto.
- ~170 costumed participants. **Traffic restrictions approx. 11:00–15:00** — use trains, not cars (https://www.yumotofujiya.jp/news/daimyogyoretsu.html).
- Held in light rain; cancelled in heavy rain. Note 2025 had **no public participant recruitment**.

---

### 4. Kyoto Jidai Matsuri — **OCTOBER, not November**

- **Thu 22 October 2026**, procession (時代行列) departs **Kyoto Imperial Palace, Kenreimon, 12:00**, to Heian Jingu. Postponed to **23 Oct** if rain. Fixed annual date of 22 Oct (https://ja.kyoto.travel/event/single.php?event_id=7049, https://kyototravel.info/jidaimatsuri).
- Wider festival span: 参役宣状祭 15 Oct → 後日祭 23 Oct.
- **Kurama Fire Festival (鞍馬の火祭, Yuki Shrine)** — same night, **Thu 22 October 2026, from ~18:00** (https://e-kyoto.jp/yuki-jinja-kurama-no-himatsuri.html, https://kyototravel.info/kuramanohimatsuri). Prefectural road Kyoto–Hirogawara–Miyama closed **15:00 → 01:00**. Access is **Eizan Electric Railway only** — no cars/taxis. Recent years enforce strict crowd control: you stay inside roped lanes, move one-way, and **cannot stop to watch**. Neither event is in November.

---

### 5. Arashiyama Momiji Matsuri — **Sunday 8 November 2026**

- Fixed as the **2nd Sunday of November**; 1 Nov 2026 is a Sunday, so the 2nd Sunday = **8 Nov 2026**. **The organiser has not posted an explicit 2026 date** (https://www.arashiyamahoshokai.com/event/arashiyama-momiji-matsuri) — date is derived from the rule, flag accordingly.
- **~10:00–15:00**, on the **Oi River upstream of Togetsukyo Bridge**. Decorated boats (Tenryu-ji boat, imayo boat, Heian court-music boat) perform on the water. **Free to watch from the bank; paid grandstand seating available.** Organiser: Arashiyama Hoshokai, tel 075-861-0012 (https://ja.kyoto.travel/event/single.php?event_id=4066).

---

### 6. Kyoto Arashiyama Hanatouro — **DISCONTINUED (ended December 2021)**

- Ran 2005–2021. Both **Arashiyama Hanatouro and Higashiyama Hanatouro were terminated after the FY2021 (20th-anniversary) editions**; the final Arashiyama run was **10–19 December 2021** (https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/京都・嵐山花灯路, https://www.kyokanko.or.jp/news/20211102/).
- Replaced from FY2022 by the **「花灯路・ライトアップ支援事業」** — a Kyoto City equipment-loan scheme (lanterns, lighting rigs) that supports *individual* temple/neighbourhood illuminations rather than one central event (https://hanatouro.kyoto.travel/?page_id=1976). So Arashiyama in Nov/Dec 2026 has temple-by-temple light-ups, not Hanatouro.

---

### 7. Nara — 78th Shosoin Exhibition — **CONFIRMED: 24 Oct – 9 Nov 2026**

- **Sat 24 October – Mon 9 November 2026**, **Nara National Museum, East & West Wings** (50 Noborioji-cho, Nara). **Open every day, no closing days.** Announced 14 July 2026.
- **Hours: 08:00–18:00; until 20:00 on Fri, Sat, Sun and holidays.** Last entry 60 min before close.
- **60 treasures, 11 shown for the first time.** Headliners: **漆胡瓶 (Shikkohei, lacquered Persian-style ewer)** on the poster, **紅牙撥鏤碁子 (ivory go stones)** owned by Emperor Shomu, 鳥獣花背方鏡, and 虹龍 (recently identified as a mummified Japanese marten).
- **Tickets: prices and the purchase system are due to be published in LATE AUGUST 2026 — NOT YET AVAILABLE as of 9 Aug.** Sources: https://www.narahaku.go.jp/news/20260714_15715/, https://shosoin-ten.jp/, https://artexhibition.jp/topics/news/20260714-AEJ2947917/, https://par-ple.jp/nara-ken/nara-shi/tourism/00175/.
- The official site's ticket section references **前売 (advance), 日時指定 (date/time-designated) and オータムレイト (Autumn Late, discounted late-afternoon) tickets** as the option set, consistent with recent years — **but the 2026 specifics are unpublished.** Assume a **timed-entry advance reservation will be required** and book the moment sales open; this is one of Japan's most oversubscribed exhibitions. Info line: 050-5542-8600 (Hello Dial).

---

### 8. Kobe Luminarie — **NOT in November or December 2026**

- The event **moved out of December**. The next edition, the **32nd Kobe Luminarie, runs 29 January – 7 February 2027** (https://www.kobe-luminarie.jp/).
- **Three venues: Meriken Park, Higashi Yuenchi Park, and the Kyu-Kyoryuchi (former foreign settlement).**
- **Meriken Park has a paid viewing zone** with a special admission ticket:
  - Advance — weekday **¥500**, weekend **¥750**
  - Same-day — weekday **¥1,000**, weekend **¥1,500**
  - Group rates available
- Lighting hours not yet posted on the outline page. **There is no Luminarie during a Nov 2026 trip** — if that was on the itinerary, it needs to be dropped or the trip re-timed to late Jan 2027.

---

### 9. Other notable November 2026 items

**Tokyo**
- **DESIGNART TOKYO 2026 — 30 Oct – 8 Nov 2026**, theme **"Hibiki"** (https://designart.jp/). Note: this is the *de facto* successor to the old **Tokyo Design Week**, which ceased operating after 2016 — do not look for TDW.
- **Meiji Jingu autumn festivals** (https://www.meijijingu.or.jp/event/): **1 Nov 鎮座記念祭** (shrine-founding anniversary, dedicatory performances on the sacred stage), **3 Nov 秋の大祭/例大祭** — the big one, imperial envoy, **yabusame horseback archery** and martial/performing-arts dedications; **23 Nov 新嘗祭** (harvest thanksgiving); **Onzo-sai** on Rittō (beginning of winter, ~7 Nov). **Exact 2026 times/programmes not published** — tel 03-3379-5511.
- **Shichi-Go-San: 15 November** (Sunday in 2026) — expect major congestion at Meiji Jingu, Hie, Tomioka Hachimangu etc. on the surrounding weekends.
- Note: **Ichi-no-tori (7 Nov) is a Saturday and Culture Day (3 Nov) is a Tuesday** — the 1st weekend is heavy.

**Sumo**
- **Kyushu Basho: 8–22 November 2026, Fukuoka Kokusai Center** (https://www.buysumotickets.com/sumo/fukuoka-sumo-tournaments). Consistent with the standard 2nd-Sunday start. **General tickets on sale ~19 September 2026**, pre-orders from mid-August. Note this is **Fukuoka, not Tokyo/Osaka** — there is no Tokyo basho in November.

**Kyoto**
- **Autumn foliage peak: mid-November to early December**, varying by site (Kiyotaki early–late Nov; Kamigamo Shrine mid–late Nov; Enri-an and Nenbutsu-ji late Nov–early Dec).
- **Night illuminations (紅葉ライトアップ)** at Kiyomizu-dera, Daigo-ji, Tenju-an, Murin-an, Kyoto Botanical Garden etc. **2026 dates are NOT yet officially announced** — kiyomizudera.or.jp's news page as of today only carries the August night viewing. An aggregator (kyototravel.info) projects Kiyomizu-dera at **21–30 Nov 2026**, which should be treated as a **projection, not a confirmation**. Temples typically publish autumn schedules in **September**. Eikan-do, Kodai-ji, Tofuku-ji and Rurikoin also run autumn programmes — verify each individually in Sept/Oct.
- **京都非公開文化財特別公開** (special openings of normally-closed cultural properties) usually runs an autumn session late Oct–mid Nov; **2026 programme not yet published** on kyoto-kankou.or.jp.
- Nothing replaces Hanatouro as a single Arashiyama-wide night event (see #6).

**Nara**
- **Shosoin Exhibition, 24 Oct – 9 Nov** (above) is the marquee November event.
- **Deer antler cutting (鹿の角きり)** — important change: it **moved from October to November**. 2025 was **8–9 Nov 2025, 11:45–15:00** (gates 11:15, last entry 14:30) at the **Kasuga Taisha Roku-en cutting ring in Nara Park**; ¥1,000 adults / ¥500 elementary (https://naradeer.com/event/tsunokiri.html). **2026 dates NOT yet announced** — if the pattern holds it would be a weekend in early-to-mid November; worth re-checking in September.
- **Kasuga Taisha** publishes no detailed November calendar yet; monthly 旬祭 on the 1st/11th/21st. Its landmark **Kasuga Wakamiya On-Matsuri is 15–18 December**, i.e. **outside November**. Tel 0742-22-7788.
- **Lightup Promenade Nara** (year-round illumination of World Heritage buildings) operates through November.

**Osaka**
- **Osaka Marathon is NOT in November** — the next edition is **28 February 2027**; entry ran 28 Jul – 28 Aug 2026 (https://www.osaka-marathon.com/).
- **Midosuji Illumination** normally starts in early/mid November and runs to end-December; **its official domain (midosujiillumination.jp) no longer resolves**, so the event's 2026 status/branding could not be verified — flag as **unconfirmed, needs re-check** via Osaka Prefecture tourism channels.

**Hakone**
- Daimyo Gyoretsu (3 Nov) is the only major festival; autumn foliage around Lake Ashi/Gora peaks **early-to-mid November**, ahead of Kyoto.

---

### Summary of what is still unconfirmed for 2026
1. Hanazono Shrine's own eve/main day announcement (dates derived from the confirmed rooster days).
2. Meguro Ohtori Shrine hours (past-year figures).
3. Jingu Gaien ginkgo light-up dates — and whether the Icho Matsuri proper returns at all (it almost certainly does not).
4. Hakone Daimyo Gyoretsu official 2026 posting and exact 2026 timings.
5. Arashiyama Momiji Matsuri explicit 2026 date.

7. All Kyoto autumn illumination and special-opening dates — **due ~September 2026**.
8. Nara deer antler cutting 2026 dates.
9. Midosuji Illumination 2026 (official site dead).

---

## 6. Other passes

- **JR Tokyo Wide Pass** — **[UNVERIFIED]**: I believe the price is now **¥15,000 adult / ¥7,500 child for 3 consecutive days** (raised from ¥10,180 in 2024). Covers JR East around Greater Tokyo *plus* Shinkansen/limited express to Nikko, Karuizawa, GALA Yuzawa, Mt. Fuji area, Izu. **Only worth it if you take at least one long day trip** (e.g. Nikko or Karuizawa) — it is poor value for travel purely inside the 23 wards. jreast.co.jp 403'd; verify the price.
- **Tokyo Metro 24-hour Ticket** — **[UNVERIFIED]** ~¥600 adult, Metro-only (no Toei). Only better than the ¥800 Tokyo Subway Ticket if you're certain you'll avoid Toei lines, which is hard for a first-timer (Oedo and Asakusa lines are Toei).
- **Toei One-Day Economy Pass** — **[UNVERIFIED]** ~¥700, Toei subway/bus/streetcar only. Rarely the right pick for a visitor.
- **Common One-Day Ticket (Metro + Toei)** — **[UNVERIFIED]** ~¥900, i.e. worse than the ¥800 24-hour Tokyo Subway Ticket. Skip.
- **Tokyo Combination / Tokyo Free Kippu** — **[UNVERIFIED]** ~¥1,600, adds JR within the 23 wards + Toei buses. Niche.
- **Nationwide JR Pass — NO, do not buy it for a Tokyo-only trip.** Since the October 2023 price increase it costs roughly ¥50,000 for 7 days, and it covers essentially nothing you'd use in Tokyo beyond the Yamanote Line (a few hundred yen a ride). It only makes sense with long-distance Shinkansen travel, e.g. Tokyo–Kyoto–Hiroshima round trips. **[VERIFIED-adjacent]** japan-guide notes the JR Pass does cover the Narita Express, but that single ~¥3,140 leg gets nowhere near justifying the pass.

---

## 7. Narita → central Tokyo

**[VERIFIED]** from [japan-guide Narita Airport access](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2027.html) and [Keisei Skyliner official](https://www.keisei.co.jp/keisei/tetudou/skyliner/us/index.php):

## 8. Haneda → central Tokyo

**[VERIFIED]** [Tokyo Monorail official](https://www.tokyo-monorail.co.jp/english/): **13 minutes** Haneda → Hamamatsucho, monorail and Yamanote Line each run **about every 5 minutes**, easy transfer at Hamamatsucho. **[VERIFIED]** [tokyo-haneda.com](https://www.tokyo-haneda.com/en/access/) and [Keikyu's Haneda site](https://www.haneda-tokyo-access.com/en/) confirm the Monorail serves **Hamamatsucho** and Keikyu serves **Shinagawa**, plus limousine bus, route bus, regular and app-dispatched taxi stands, and parking P2–P5. - **Airport Limousine Bus: ~¥1,000–1,400** to major hotel areas (Shinjuku, Ginza, Tokyo Station, Shibuya), 30–60 min depending on traffic. limousinebus.co.jp 403'd — **verify**.
- **Taxi: ~¥6,000–10,000** to central Tokyo, 30–45 min. Haneda operates **fixed-fare ("teigaku") taxis** to defined zones, typically in the ¥6,300–9,300 range depending on destination, plus expressway tolls and a late-night surcharge. **Verify current zone pricing at the airport taxi counter.**

- **Narita → central Tokyo: ~¥30,000** **[VERIFIED via japan-guide]**, 60–90+ minutes, explicitly *not recommended*. Fixed-fare services exist and run lower (~¥20,000–26,000 depending on zone) — **[UNVERIFIED]**.

## Practical recommendation for a November 2026 first-timer

1. **iPhone user:** add a Suica in Apple Wallet before you fly (works on any global iPhone 8+), and plan to **top up with cash at convenience stores** — assume your foreign Visa/Mastercard may be refused for in-Wallet top-ups. **Android user: buy a physical Suica or Pasmo on arrival** — normal anonymous cards have been back on sale since March 2025.
2. **Do not rely on tapping a contactless credit card** at Tokyo ticket gates in 2026.
3. **From Narita**, price the **Skyliner + Tokyo Subway Ticket combo** first; otherwise Skyliner discounted at ¥2,310, or **Airport Bus TYO-NRT at ¥1,500** if you're on a budget and not in a hurry. **From Haneda**, Monorail or Keikyu, both cheap and fast.
4. **Buy the 72-hour Tokyo Subway Ticket (¥1,500) at the airport** — validity starts at first use, so there's no downside to buying early. Remember it excludes JR.
5. **Skip the nationwide JR Pass.** Consider the Tokyo Wide Pass only if you're doing Nikko/Karuizawa/Fuji day trips.

# Kyoto — 3 days, November 2026

## 1. Kiyomizu-dera & southern Higashiyama

**Kiyomizu-dera** — Adult **¥500**, students ¥200. The increase was **April 2024** (¥400 → ¥500), *not* 2025 as sometimes reported ([kinabal.co.jp](https://kinabal.co.jp/gokyoto/kyoto/kiyomizudra-admission-fee/), [japan-guide](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3901.html)). Hours **6:00–18:00** (18:30 Jul–Aug). **No closing days.** Time needed 60–90 min.

Autumn night viewing (*yoru no tokubetsu haikan*): the temple's own gate-front association lists **2026: Nov 21–30, reception 17:30–21:00** (Jojuin garden 18:00–20:30) — [monzenkai.com/yakan](https://www.monzenkai.com/yakan). **2025 actual was Nov 22–Dec 7**, 17:30–21:30 (last entry 21:00), **¥500** adult ([kyoto-kanko-mapping](https://kyoto-kanko-mapping.com/autumn_leaves_lightup_map/), [souda-kyoto](https://souda-kyoto.jp/event/detail/lightup-autumn.html)). ⚠️ The 2026 window is listed as much shorter (10 days vs 16) — worth re-checking in September 2026. **Could not definitively confirm** whether a daytime ticket carries over; the standard practice is that the grounds clear at 18:00 and evening entry is a **separate ¥500**. Budget for paying twice.

**Sannenzaka / Ninenzaka** — Free, always open. Dead before 08:00, solid wall of people 10:00–16:00. Tripods and selfie sticks are discouraged; no formal fine here.

**Yasaka Pagoda (Hokan-ji)** — Interior **¥400** (junior-high age and up only; under-13s not admitted, steep stairs). Roughly **10:00–15:00/16:00 but opening days are irregular** — often shut; phone 075-551-2417. Treat entry as a bonus. The classic photo is from Yasaka-dori looking up, best before 08:00.

**Kodai-ji** — Official site: adult **¥800**, JHS/HS ¥400; **combined with Entoku-in ¥1,200**; 9:00–17:30 (recept. 17:00) ([kodaiji.com/haikan.html](https://www.kodaiji.com/haikan.html)). ⚠️ japan-guide still shows the older ¥600 / ¥900-combo figures — the official ¥800 is the one to trust. Autumn illumination **2025: Oct 24–Dec 14, 17:00–22:00 (recept. 21:30), ¥600**; Entoku-in same dates, ¥500. 2026 dates not yet posted. Kodai-ji has the **longest** autumn light-up window in Kyoto — very useful insurance against a late peak.

**Yasaka Shrine** — Free, always open, no closing days, 10–20 min. **Maruyama Park** — free, 24h; pleasant but it's a cherry-blossom park, not a top autumn site.

**Gion / Hanamikoji** — Photography is **banned on the private alleys** (not on Hanamikoji itself or other public streets), with signage threatening a **¥10,000 fine**, introduced Oct 2019 by the local *machizukuri* council. Since **March–May 2024** entire private lanes have been **closed to tourists outright** (first no-entry sign at Kosode-koji, 29 May 2024), with surveillance cameras installed. Enforcement is by residents/local council rather than police, and the fine is a private penalty of contested legal force — but signage and confrontation are real, and enforcement steps up in peak season. Practical rule: **stay on Hanamikoji and marked public roads, never photograph geiko/maiko without consent, never follow them.** Shirakawa canal area is quieter and less restricted. ([Japan Today](https://japantoday.com/category/national/kyoto%E2%80%99s-popular-tourist-spot-gion-to-forbid-photos-on-private-roads), [AFAR](https://www.afar.com/magazine/kyotos-gion-district-bans-photographing-geisha-on-private-streets), [Time Out](https://www.timeout.com/tokyo/news/kyoto-to-limit-tourist-access-in-the-historical-gion-geisha-district-031224), [japan-guide Gion](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3902.html))

## 2. Fushimi Inari Taisha

**Free, open 24h, no closing days** ([japan-guide](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3915.html)). Full summit loop **2–3 hours**; the **Yotsutsuji viewpoint is 30–45 min up**, roughly halfway, and japan-guide notes the trail offers little new beyond it — Yotsutsuji and back is the efficient **60–90 min** visit.

**Arrival timing:** peak congestion is **10:00–16:00**. Be at the *romon* gate **before 07:00** (06:30 ideal) for near-empty torii tunnels; alternatively **after ~20:00**, when it's lit and atmospheric but essentially deserted. Sunrise in Kyoto in late November is ~06:40, so a 06:45–07:00 start gives good light *and* no crowds. It's 5 min from Kyoto Station on the JR Nara Line (Inari Stn) — easy to do before breakfast.

## 3. Arashiyama

| Site | Adult | Hours | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bamboo grove | Free | 24h | **Arrive before 08:00.** Unwalkable 10:00–15:00 |
| Tenryu-ji | Garden **¥500**; +**¥300** halls (¥800 total); Cloud Dragon +**¥500** | 8:30–17:00 (recept. 16:50); halls to 16:45; dragon 9:00–16:30 | **Nov 14–30, 2026: garden opens 07:30** (confirmed) |
| Iwatayama Monkey Park | **¥800** | 9:00–16:30 (entry 16:00) | 10-min uphill hike; ⚠️ official site unreachable (expired cert) — price per japan-guide |
| Okochi Sanso | **¥1,000** incl. matcha + sweet | 9:00–17:00, no closing days | Genuinely quiet; best-value escape from the grove crowds |
| Giou-ji | **¥500** (students ¥100) | 9:00–16:30 | Moss + maple; small, 20 min |
| Jojakko-ji | **¥600** | 9:00–17:00 (recept. 16:30) | ⚠️ official ¥600, japan-guide still says ¥500. **Top-tier autumn**, hillside views |
| Togetsukyo Bridge | Free | — | Autumn colours on Mt. Arashiyama behind |

Tenryu-ji Cloud Dragon is **weekends/holidays only** normally, but runs **daily during the autumn special period** ([tenryuji.com/visit](https://www.tenryuji.com/visit/)).

**Hozugawa river cruise** — **¥6,000**, ~2 hours, hourly 9:00–15:00 (mid-Mar to mid-Dec). Walk-up or online timed reservation; **book ahead mid-Nov–early Dec**. Cancelled in bad weather / high or low water; closed Dec 29–Jan 4. No standing suspension found ([japan-guide](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3966.html)).

**Sagano Romantic Train** — **¥880 one way**, 25 min, Torokko Saga ↔ Torokko Kameoka, hourly 9:00–16:00 (to 17:00 on busy days). **All seats reserved**; the open-air "Rich Car" (car 5) is sold same-day at the station only. Closed most Wednesdays (but runs through peak season) and Dec 30–end Feb. **Book as early as possible for late November** — sales open one month ahead at JR West Midori-no-Madoguchi and online. Autumn evening light-up runs on the line Oct 25–Dec 29 ([japan-guide](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3965.html)).

Arashiyama = a **full day** if you include the train/boat; a **half day** (bamboo + Tenryu-ji + Okochi Sanso + bridge) otherwise.

## 4. Northwest Kyoto

| Site | Adult | Hours | Closed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Kinkaku-ji** | **¥500** (elem/JHS ¥300) | 9:00–17:00 | None |
| **Ryoan-ji** | **¥600** | 8:00–17:00 (Mar–Nov) | None |
| **Ninna-ji** | Grounds free; **Goten ¥800**; Reihokan extra | 9:00–17:00 | None |
| **Daisen-in** (Daitoku-ji) | ¥500 | 9:00–16:30 | None |
| **Zuiho-in** | ¥400 | 9:00–17:00 | None |
| **Ryogen-in** | ¥350 | 9:00–16:30 | Irregular |
| **Koto-in** | — | — | ⚠️ **Closed indefinitely** |

Kinkaku-ji's official fee revision was **1 April 2023**; the current adult rate is **¥500** ([shokoku-ji.jp/kinkakuji/access](https://www.shokoku-ji.jp/kinkakuji/access/)). Ryoan-ji at **¥600** reflects a rise from ¥500. **Koto-in — the famous maple-tunnel approach at Daitoku-ji — is closed indefinitely**; do not build an itinerary around it ([japan-guide Daitokuji](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3910.html)). Kinkaku-ji: arrive at 09:00 opening or after 16:00; it is a 30-minute one-way walk-through, and it is #2 most-visited in Kyoto.

## 5. Northern Higashiyama / Philosopher's Path

| Site | Adult | Hours |
|---|---|---|
| **Ginkaku-ji** | **¥1,000** (up from ¥500) | 8:30–17:00 (Mar–Nov) |
| Philosopher's Path | Free | ~2 km, 30–45 min walk |
| Nanzen-ji grounds + **Suirokaku aqueduct** | **Free** | — |
| Nanzen-ji **Hojo garden** | ¥600 | 8:40–17:00 |
| Nanzen-ji **Sanmon gate** | ¥600 | 8:40–17:00 |
| Nanzen-in | ¥400 | 8:40–17:00 |
| Konchi-in | ¥500 | 9:00–17:00 |
| Tenju-an | ¥500 | 9:00–16:45 |
| **Honen-in** | **Free** (grounds) | Buildings normally closed |
| **Shoren-in** | ¥600 day / **¥1,000** night | 9:00–17:00; night 18:00–22:00 |

Nanzen-ji buildings close **Dec 28–31** only. Honen-in hours could not be confirmed precisely; grounds are free and the mossy thatched gate is the draw.

**Eikan-do Zenrin-ji** — normal adult **¥1,000**, 9:00–17:00 (entry 16:00). **2025 autumn treasure exhibition (寺宝展): Nov 11–Dec 10, adult ¥1,000**; **light-up Nov 15–Dec 10, 17:30–21:00 (tickets to 20:30), ¥700**, a *separate* evening ticket. 2026 dates not yet posted. Eikan-do is arguably Kyoto's single best night illumination and gets 40–60 min queues at 18:00–19:00 — go at 17:30 sharp or after 20:00 ([eikando.or.jp](https://www.eikando.or.jp/haikan.html)).

**Shoren-in autumn night 2025: Nov 7–Dec 7** (one source says Nov 7–30), 18:00–22:00 (recept. 21:30), **¥1,000**.

## 6. Central & southern Kyoto

**Nishiki Market** — Free. Shops ~**9:00/10:00–18:00**; **no market-wide closing day** (individual shops close Wed or Sun). Worst crush **11:30–15:00**; go **10:00–11:00** or after 16:00. On eating: the Merchants' Association posts a **request, not a legal ban** — "stop eating while walking, use the eat-in corners at the shop where you bought the item." Eating standing directly in front of the selling shop is generally accepted; walking down the lane with food is not ([kyoto-nishiki.or.jp/manner](https://www.kyoto-nishiki.or.jp/manner/), [japan-guide](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3931.html)).

**Nijo Castle** — Grounds **¥800**; **+¥500 for Ninomaru Palace (¥1,300 combined)**; Honmaru Palace +¥1,000 with advance reservation. 8:45–17:00 (entry 16:00; Ninomaru to 16:10). Closed **Dec 29–31**; Ninomaru additionally closed **Tuesdays in Jan, Jul, Aug, Dec** — so **no Tuesday problem in November**. I found **no confirmation** of the proposed non-resident/foreign differential pricing being in force. Night event: **NAKED meets Nijo-jo autumn 2025 ran Oct 31–Dec 7, until 22:00, advance timed tickets, ¥1,600–2,400** depending on date/tier. 2026 not announced.

**Kyoto Imperial Palace** — **Free**, no reservation, walk-in. 9:00–16:30 Sep–Mar (last entry 40 min before). **Closed Mondays** (Tuesday if Monday is a holiday) and Dec 28–Jan 4. ~60 min; exteriors only. *Sento* Imperial Palace still requires advance booking via the Imperial Household Agency.

**To-ji** — Grounds 5:00–17:00; Kondo/Kodo halls 8:00–17:00 (last entry 16:30). **Adult ¥800** (prices stated as of 19 Mar 2026); Kanchi-in ¥600; Mie-do and Jiki-do free. **Autumn night viewing Oct 31–Dec 13, ¥1,000 adult / ¥500 HS**, including night access to the main halls; no group or combination discounts ([toji.or.jp/admission](https://toji.or.jp/admission/)). ⚠️ The official page is current-dated but I could not pin the event year — treat Oct 31–Dec 13 as the pattern and re-verify in autumn. The reflection of the five-storey pagoda in the pond is the signature shot. 2025 listings show Nov 1–Dec 14, 18:00–21:30, ¥1,000.

**Tofuku-ji** — from the official site ([tofukuji.jp/guide](https://tofukuji.jp/guide/)), with **2026 dates confirmed**:
- Autumn special period: **Nov 14 – Dec 6, 2026**. Tsutenkyo opens **08:30**, Hojo garden 09:00, both close 16:00.
- **Tsutenkyo + Kaisando: ¥600 normally → ¥1,000 in the autumn period.**
- **Hojo garden ¥500, rising to ¥600 from 1 Nov 2026.**
- **Combined ¥1,000 ticket is NOT sold during the autumn period.** Budget **¥1,600** to see both.
- Outside autumn: 9:00–16:00 (Apr–Oct), 9:00–15:30 (Dec 7–Mar). No closing days.
- **Photography restrictions on the Tsutenkyo and Garo bridges apply during the autumn special period**, and **tripods are banned throughout the grounds year-round.** In practice staff keep people moving across Tsutenkyo and stop photography from the bridge itself at peak — shoot the bridge from Garo-kyo instead.
- **No night illumination** at the main garden — Tofuku-ji is daytime only. ✔ Verified against multiple listings; it does not appear on any 2025 illumination roundup.
- Crowds: this is the single most crowded autumn site in Kyoto. **Be in line before the 08:30 opening.** By 10:00 the queue for Tsutenkyo can run 30–60 min.
- Nearby subtemples: **Komyo-in** (small, quiet, ~¥500 donation) and Reiun-in are worth it as overflow; ⚠️ I could not verify their current fees or hours.

**Kiyomizu-dera vs Tofuku-ji for autumn:** Tofuku-ji is the better *maple* experience — a dense valley of ~2,000 maples viewed from a bridge, unmatched density. Kiyomizu-dera is the better *place* — the stage, the city view, the whole Higashiyama walk around it, and it has the night illumination that Tofuku-ji lacks. **Do both, on the same day:** Tofuku-ji at 08:30 opening (it's 2 min from Kyoto Station on the JR Nara Line, or Keihan Tofukuji), then Keihan north to Kiyomizu-Gojo and walk up to Kiyomizu-dera for the afternoon, staying through the night illumination. That's the strongest single autumn day in Kyoto.

## 7. Autumn leaves — timing and ranking

**Typical Kyoto city peak: ~Nov 20 – Dec 5.** But recent years have run **late**:

- **2023** peak reported **Nov 26**
- **2024** peak reported **Dec 4** — described in Japanese sources as the latest in eight years, caused by high temperatures through mid-November
- **2025** peak reported **Nov 29**, with pre-season forecasts again calling for "later than average" after a very warm September/October

([japan-guide autumn color report archive](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2014.html), [blog.kanko.jp](https://blog.kanko.jp/))

**Planning implication for 2026:** the safest window for Kyoto *city* temples is **Nov 25 – Dec 5**. Nov 20–24 is a real gamble in a warm year; anything before Nov 18 will likely be green-to-turning in the city. If your dates are locked earlier in November, shift the itinerary north/west to the early-peaking areas.

**Elevation staggers the peak:** Takao, Kurama/Kibune and Ohara peak **~Nov 5–20**; city-centre temples **~Nov 20–Dec 5**; the very last colour clings on at Tofuku-ji and Eikan-do into the first week of December.

**Ranked best spots:**

1. **Tofuku-ji** — the maple valley from Tsutenkyo; unmatched density. Late Nov. Crowds: extreme.
2. **Eikan-do Zenrin-ji** — best combination of day *and* night viewing. Late Nov–early Dec. Extreme.
3. **Kiyomizu-dera** — colour + architecture + city panorama + night. Late Nov. Extreme.
4. **Ruriko-in** — the famous table-reflection shot. **Reservation required** (2025: Nov 8–Dec 7, lottery-based booking; **¥2,000**, cash only). October visits need no reservation. High.
5. **Nanzen-ji + Tenju-an** — aqueduct framed by maples, and the grounds are free. Late Nov. Moderate.
6. **Arashiyama — Jojakko-ji** (¥600) and **Giou-ji** (¥500) — hillside maples, far better than the bamboo grove in autumn. Late Nov. Moderate.
7. **Hogon-in** (Tenryu-ji subtemple) — superb, and one of the few Arashiyama night light-ups. Nov 14–Dec 7 (2025), ¥1,000 night.
8. **Kodai-ji** — best-lit night garden, longest season (late Oct–mid Dec). Extreme at night.
9. **Ohara — Sanzen-in / Hosen-in / Shorin-in** — moss and maple, an hour north. **Peaks ~Nov 10–20.** Moderate.
10. **Takao — Jingo-ji / Kozan-ji** — mountain gorge, **peaks ~Nov 5–15**, the earliest in Kyoto. Low-moderate.
11. **Kurama & Kibune** — Eizan Railway "maple tunnel" lit Nov 7–24 (2025), free. Early-mid Nov.
12. **Enko-ji** — reflection garden, one of the finest and less touristed. Late Nov. Moderate.
13. **Shinnyo-do / Konkai Komyo-ji** — big, uncrowded, adjacent to each other. Late Nov. Low.
14. **Bishamon-do** — the "red carpet" of fallen leaves on the approach steps; peaks *slightly later*, early Dec.
15. **Kitano Tenmangu Momiji-en** — 350 maples along a stream, day and night, ¥1,200. Nov 1–Dec 7.
16. **Daigo-ji**, **Manshu-in**, **Genko-an / Koetsu-ji / Shoden-ji** (Takagamine), **Komyo-ji** in Nagaokakyo — all excellent and materially less crowded.

**Ginkaku-ji / Philosopher's Path** is pleasant but not a top-tier maple site; treat it as a walk that links Ginkaku-ji → Honen-in → Eikan-do → Nanzen-ji, which is the best autumn *walking* route in the city.

The rest are walk-up. **Photography restrictions:** tripods are banned at essentially every night illumination; Tofuku-ji bans tripods year-round and restricts bridge photography in autumn.

## 9. Crowd-avoidance summary

- **Fushimi Inari:** through the gate by **06:45–07:00**, or after 20:00. Peak 10:00–16:00.
- **Kiyomizu-dera:** **06:00–07:30** (it opens at 06:00 — almost uniquely early, and this is Kyoto's single best crowd hack). Or return for the 17:30 night opening. Avoid 10:00–16:00.
- **Arashiyama bamboo grove:** **before 08:00**, ideally 07:00–07:30. By 09:30 it's shoulder-to-shoulder. Pair with Tenryu-ji's **07:30 autumn opening (Nov 14–30, 2026)**.
- **Tofuku-ji:** in the queue before the **08:30** autumn opening.
- **Nishiki Market:** 10:00–11:00.
- Kyoto's crowds are strongly weekday-dependent in November: **avoid weekends entirely** if your three days allow it, and note that the Nov 23 Labour Thanksgiving holiday creates a long weekend most years.

## 10. Kyoto transit

**The bus-only one-day pass is DISCONTINUED** — sales ended **30 September 2023** (it was ¥700), explicitly to reduce tourist crowding on city buses ([city.kyoto.lg.jp/kotsu/page/0000309762.html](https://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/kotsu/page/0000309762.html)).

Current options:
- **Subway & Bus One-Day Pass: ¥1,100 adult / ¥550 child.** Covers all subway lines, all city buses, Kyoto Bus, Keihan Bus and West JR Bus (some routes excluded). This is the pass to buy — but only if you'll make 5+ rides.
- **Subway One-Day Pass: ¥800.**
- **City bus flat fare: ¥230** in the central zone.

**The bus overcrowding problem is real** — buses on the Kiyomizu/Ginkaku-ji corridors regularly pass stops full, and luggage is discouraged. Kyoto's answer is the **Sightseeing Limited Express Bus**:
- **EX100** — Kyoto Station → Kiyomizu-dera (Gojozaka) → Gion → Heian Shrine → Ginkaku-ji
- **EX101** — Kyoto Station → Kiyomizu-dera only (short shuttle)
- **Kyoto Station to Kiyomizu-dera in 10 minutes**, vs 20+ on the local 206
- **Fare ¥500 adult / ¥250 child cash** — more than double the normal bus fare, but **the ¥1,100 Subway & Bus One-Day Pass IS valid** on it
- **Board at the front, pay on boarding**, exit at the rear (opposite of normal Kyoto buses)
- EX100 runs roughly **every 7–8 minutes in the morning**; both depart Kyoto Station bus terminal **stop D1**
- Verdict: **worth it.** ([city.kyoto.lg.jp/kotsu/webguide/ja/bus/limited_express.html](https://www2.city.kyoto.lg.jp/kotsu/webguide/ja/bus/limited_express.html))

**IC cards:** ICOCA/Suica/PASMO and the rest of the ten-card family work on **virtually all trains and buses in and around Kyoto**, including city buses and the subway. Buy or top up ICOCA at any JR West machine including Kyoto Station. Mobile Suica/ICOCA on iPhone works for foreign visitors (Apple Wallet, no Japanese card needed for Suica); Welcome Suica is a Tokyo-airport product and unnecessary here. ⚠️ The news about dropping IC cards concerns **rural** operators (Kumamoto, parts of Kyushu/Shikoku), **not Kansai** — Kyoto is unaffected.

**Taxis:** base **¥500 for the first 0.9 km**, then ¥100 per 255 m; 20% surcharge 22:00–05:00. **Kyoto Station → Kiyomizu-dera ≈ ¥1,410** — for two or more people that beats the bus on both cost and time, and this is the single best money-for-sanity trade in Kyoto. Use the **GO** app (Uber in Kyoto mostly dispatches the same taxi fleet). Expect scarcity at 17:00–19:00 in late November and after night illuminations end — walk a few blocks to a main road rather than waiting outside a temple gate.

**Rail alternatives to buses:** the two subway lines (Karasuma N–S, Tozai E–W) miss most temples, so use **Keihan** (Fushimi Inari via JR, but Gion-Shijo / Kiyomizu-Gojo / Tofukuji for Higashiyama), **Hankyu** (Kyoto-Kawaramachi for downtown/Gion), **JR Sagano Line** (Kyoto → Saga-Arashiyama, 15 min) and the **Randen tram** (Arashiyama ↔ Kinkaku-ji area via Kitano-Hakubaicho). Bicycle rental (¥1,000–1,500/day) is genuinely efficient in flat central Kyoto but poor for Arashiyama/Fushimi.

## 11. Kyoto → Nara

| Option | Time | Fare |
|---|---|---|
| **JR Miyakoji Rapid** (Kyoto → JR Nara) | ~45 min | **¥760** |
| **Kintetsu express (急行)** (Kyoto → Kintetsu Nara) | 42–50 min | **¥760** |
| **Kintetsu Limited Express (特急)** | ~35 min | **¥760 + ¥520 surcharge = ¥1,280** |

JR Miyakoji Rapid runs every 30 min; Kintetsu runs several trains an hour. ⚠️ japan-guide lists the JR fare as ¥720 and Kintetsu as ¥760–1,280; Japanese sources give ¥760 for both base fares — the small discrepancy is likely a recent fare revision. Budget ¥760.

**Which station:** **Kintetsu Nara is clearly better** — it is a few minutes' walk from Nara Park and Kofuku-ji, and ~30 min walk to Todai-ji. **JR Nara is 15–20 minutes further west** (~45 min walk to Todai-ji), requiring a bus or a long walk. **Take Kintetsu unless you hold a JR Pass**, in which case JR is free and the extra walk is the price. Kintetsu Limited Express requires a **reserved-seat surcharge** and is only worth ¥520 if you're short on time — the regular express is nearly as fast.

## 12. Kyoto → Osaka

| Option | Route | Time | Fare |
|---|---|---|---|
| **JR Special Rapid (新快速)** | Kyoto → Osaka Stn | ~30 min | **¥580** |
| **Shinkansen** | Kyoto → Shin-Osaka | ~14 min | ~¥1,450 unreserved ⚠️ *not verified this session* |
| **Hankyu Kyoto Line** | Kyoto-Kawaramachi → Osaka-Umeda | ~42 min | **¥410** |
| **Keihan Main Line** | Gion-Shijo → Yodoyabashi | ~50 min | **¥430** |

**Which to use:**
- **Umeda / Osaka Station area:** JR Special Rapid (fastest) or Hankyu (cheapest, and starts from downtown Kyoto rather than Kyoto Station).
- **Namba / Shinsaibashi:** Hankyu to Umeda then Midosuji subway, or Keihan to Yodoyabashi then one Midosuji stop.
- **Osaka Castle:** Keihan to Kyobashi, or JR to Osaka then the Loop Line to Osakajokoen.
- **USJ:** JR — Special Rapid to Osaka, then Loop Line to Nishikujo and the Yumesaki Line.
- **Shinkansen is not worth it** for Kyoto–Osaka: it saves ~15 minutes over JR Special Rapid for triple the fare and drops you at Shin-Osaka, which is not central.
- **Hankyu and Keihan limited express trains carry no surcharge** — they are included in the base fare, unlike JR/Kintetsu limited expresses. ⚠️ Widely true and I'm confident, but not directly verified this session. **Keihan Premium Car** is an optional reserved car with a surcharge of roughly ¥500 (⚠️ exact figure not verified).
