- https://sankan.kunaicho.go.jp/register/month/4201?locale=en
- **Katsura ¥1,000/adult** (confirmed — it does now charge). **Shugakuin free.** Sento Gosho fee unverified.
- Katsura English tours 09:20/11:20/13:20/15:20/16:20, ~60 min, ~20 people.
- Applications generally open **the 1st of the month, one month prior** → apply 1 Oct. Same-day standby exists but is unreliable in foliage season. Shugakuin's hillside is arguably the better November pick.

**Tokyo Imperial Palace tour** — free. Online opens **05:00 JST on the 1st of the prior month** (→ 1 Oct), closes 4 days before. https://sankan.kunaicho.go.jp/english/guide/koukyo.html. 200 slots online, plus a genuine **same-day standby** (Kikyo-mon gate, 09:00 / 12:30, up to 300). Closed Sun/Mon/holidays.

**Kyoto Imperial Palace — WALK-IN, free, no application** (changed in 2016). Just turn up. Closed Mondays.

**Tofuku-ji night viewing** — **reservation-only, no gate sale.** ¥2,800, capacity 1,020/night, booked through **JR Tokai's EX Ryosaki** platform, not the temple. 2025 window was Nov 19–Dec 7. **2026 dates not yet published — re-check https://tofukuji.jp in early-to-mid October.**
- Daytime autumn admission rises to **¥1,000** (Nov 14–Dec 6); combination tickets not sold in autumn.
- **Photography banned on both Tsutenkyo AND Gaunkyo bridges** during peak. Tripods banned year-round.

**Rurikoin** — **advance reservation required in foliage season.** Autumn 2026 opening confirmed: **1 Oct – 13 Dec 2026**, 10:00–17:00, **¥2,000**. https://rurikoin.komyoji.com/ — booking platform and window not verifiable (site 403'd). Check early-to-mid October. Far NE Kyoto (Eizan line), half-day.

**Sagano Romantic Train (Torokko)** — November is its busiest month. Tickets open **1 month ahead at 10:00 JST** and popular afternoon departures sell out in days. https://ars-saganokanko.triplabo.jp/home (~¥880 one-way, unverified).

## Tier 2: BOOK WEEKS AHEAD

**teamLab Planets TOKYO (Toyosu)** — https://teamlabplanets.dmm.com/ticket (official, DMM-run)
- Adult **from ¥3,600** dynamic; Premium Pass ¥12,000. Book **3–4+ weeks** out; same-day routinely gone.
- Run extended to **end of 2027** — safe for your trip. You wade barefoot through knee-deep water; wear shorts or rollable trousers, no skirts.

**teamLab Borderless (Azabudai Hills)** — open, relocated from Odaiba in Feb 2024. https://www.teamlab.art/e/tokyo/
- **¥3,600 base rising to ~¥5,600** on peak dates; ~¥200 on-site surcharge. Bookable ~1–2 months ahead; book 3–4 weeks out.

**Shibuya Sky** — https://www.shibuya-scramble-square.com/sky/
- **Online opens exactly 4 weeks ahead.** Tiered pricing: online ¥2,700 before 15:00 / **¥3,400 from 15:00**; on-site ¥3,000 / ¥3,700.
- November sunset is ~16:30, so the **15:30–16:30 slots** are the contested ones — book the hour the 4-week window opens.
- Open-air rooftop closes in rain/wind with no notice. Have a backup evening.

**Kabukiza single-act tickets — YOUR ASSUMPTION IS OUT OF DATE**
- **No longer a same-day queue.** Online only, **on sale 12:00 noon JST the day BEFORE** the performance: https://www.e-tix.jp/shochiku_makumi/en/
- **¥1,000–¥8,800** + ¥110 fee (the high end is a new "Upgraded 2nd-level" tier; standard is 4th floor). Max 4 tickets, no refunds.
- **3D Secure is mandatory** — enable it with your card issuer before you travel or the purchase fails.
- **Captioning device: ¥1,000, CASH ONLY, per act.** Carry ¥1,000 in cash.
- Full program: https://www.e-tix.jp/shochiku/ — opens ~the 14th of the prior month (→ ~14 Oct). English phone +81 3 6745-0888.
- **November is Kichirei Kaomise**, the most prestigious month of the kabuki year. Kabukiza runs **Nov 1–25, dark Nov 9 and 17**. Program not yet announced (expect late Sept/early Oct).

**Universal Studios Japan / Super Nintendo World — LARGELY UNVERIFIED.** usj.co.jp is fully JS-rendered and returned nothing.
- 1-Day Studio Pass **from ¥8,200 adult** (per Osaka Tourism Bureau). Official: https://www.usj.co.jp/
- **Could NOT verify** whether a timed Area Entry Ticket is still required for SNW, or Express Pass tiers/prices (historically ¥10,000–30,000+, and only some variants include SNW entry). **This is the single most consequential unknown — verify on the official app close to your date.** Express Passes sell out first and hardest.

**Toyosu tuna auction close-up deck** — advance lottery, ~100/day, 05:30. https://toyosu.jcdlotterysite.jp — apply roughly a month ahead (for November, early October). The **free 2F observation walkway** needs no booking.

**Hakone ryokan** — mid-to-late November is peak foliage and one of the busiest weekends of the year. **Book now.** Verified: Hakone Free Pass from Shinjuku **¥7,100 (2-day) / ¥7,500 (3-day)**, Romancecar +¥1,200 — https://odakyu-global.com/passes/hakone-freepass/. Day onsen at Hakone Yuryo ¥1,700–2,200; private bath for 2 (120 min) ¥10,400–11,400. *Ryokan price bands and tattoo policies could not be verified this session — assume ¥25,000–40,000 pp/night with half-board for moderate, and confirm tattoo policy at booking.*

**Sumo morning practice tour (Tokyo)** — ~¥10,000 pp via Klook / Magical Trip / BuySumoTickets. Book 3–6 weeks ahead; slots are 10–15 people. No walk-up.

**Samurai Restaurant (Shinjuku)** — from **¥8,000** incl. 2 drinks (some sources ¥9,000 advance / ¥10,000 day-of). Book 1–2 weeks ahead via GetYourGuide/Klook/Rakuten. https://giragiragirls.com/

**Pokémon Café** (Nihonbashi / Shinsaibashi) — reservation mandatory, monthly release, sells out in minutes. https://www.pokemoncenter-online.com/cafe/

## Tier 3: TURN UP

- **Kyoto Imperial Palace**, Fushimi Inari (free), Kinkaku-ji ¥500, Ginkaku-ji ¥500, Kiyomizu-dera ¥500, Nijo-jo ~¥1,300, bamboo grove.
- **All of Nara** — Todai-ji ¥800, Kasuga Taisha, deer park. **One exception to check: the Shosoin Exhibition at Nara National Museum**, traditionally late Oct–mid Nov, which does use advance timed tickets and sells out on weekends. Unverified for 2026 — check narahaku.go.jp.
- **Kyoto night illuminations — most are still pay-at-gate:** Kiyomizu-dera (~¥500), Eikando (~¥600–700), Kodai-ji (~¥600), Shoren-in (~¥800, least crowded — good pick), To-ji (~¥1,000), Kitano Tenmangu (~¥1,200 incl. tea). **All 2026 dates/prices unpublished as of August; announcements land late Sept–mid Oct.** Given Tofuku-ji and Rurikoin both moved to reservations, assume the trend spreads and re-check in October.
- **Arashiyama Hanatouro is discontinued** (ended 2021, never returned).
- Crowd reality: the Higashiyama cluster on a **late-November Saturday evening is genuinely unpleasant** — 45–90 min entry queues, gridlocked buses. Go on a weekday, pick two venues max, walk or taxi.
- **Sumo Museum** (Ryogoku Kokugikan) — free, weekdays.

## VERDICTS: skip these

**Ghibli Park (Aichi) — SKIP.** First-come sale **two months ahead on the 10th at 14:00 JST** (November → 10 Sep 2026). Premium pass ¥7,300–7,800 (the one worth having; Standard omits the Totoro house and the *Whisper of the Heart* shop). Five areas across a huge former Expo park = 6–8 hours, plus 2 hours Nagoya round-trip transit. That's one of your ten days. Do the Mitaka museum instead. https://ghibli-park.jp/en/ticket/

**Warner Bros. Studio Tour Tokyo — SKIP on a first trip.** ¥6,300–7,300 adult, ~4 hours inside plus transit to Nerima. It's excellent and faithful — but it is a *British* attraction that happens to be in Tokyo. Walk-up officially possible; on-site ticket office is **cash only**; date changes ¥1,500. https://www.wbstudiotour.jp/en/tickets/

**Sumo in November — not accessible.** The **Kyushu Basho runs Nov 8–22, 2026 in Fukuoka** (~5h from Osaka). Tickets go on sale 19 Sep via https://sumo.pia.jp/. It's a separate trip. Do the morning practice tour instead; the retired-wrestler tourist shows are staged and overpriced. Chanko nabe in Ryogoku (¥3,000–6,000, walk-in) is the low-risk pleasure.

**Robot Restaurant — permanently closed** (March 2020, never reopened). Samurai Restaurant is the successor; go for the show ticket only, the food is merely palatable.

**Samurai/ninja experiences — WEAKEST SECTION, needs fresh research.** Samurai Museum Shinjuku status unverified (site 403'd). General rule that holds: ninja cafes/restaurants are near-universal tourist traps; **sword/kembu lessons** where you actually handle a blade consistently get good reviews and need 1–2 weeks' notice.

## Rail, passes, and entry admin

**Shinkansen reservations** — open **1 month before at 10:00 JST**; the online Tokaido/Sanyo/Kyushu (smartEX/EX) service takes bookings up to **one year** ahead. In November you should reserve — not because trains sell out routinely, but because foliage weekends and the Tokyo→Kyoto leg with luggage are exactly when non-reserved cars get ugly. Nozomi goes fully-reserved only at New Year/Golden Week/Obon, so November is fine on that front. *Exact 2026 fares could not be verified — every JR fare source failed.*

**Oversized baggage (Tokaido/Sanyo/Kyushu/Nishikyushu):** sum of height+width+depth **over 160 cm** requires a free advance reservation for a last-row seat. **¥1,000 penalty** if you don't, and the JR Pass doesn't cover it. Most large checked suitcases (~28"+) exceed 160cm — check your bags before you book. Hard limit is 250 cm / 30 kg, two pieces.

**JR Pass — NOT worth it for this itinerary.** 7-day ordinary is **¥50,000 pp = ¥100,000 for two** against roughly ¥60,000 of actual travel. One long shinkansen leg plus a lot of private-rail and subway travel the pass doesn't cover. Two notes: it **cannot be bought at stations in Japan** (discontinued 2023), and from **1 Oct 2026 travel-agency prices rise to ¥53,000** while the official JR website holds at ¥50,000 — so if you ever buy one, buy direct.
Better: **Hakone Free Pass** (¥7,100), point-to-point shinkansen, and IC cards.

**IC cards** — Welcome Suica still available at limited locations, no deposit, no refund, 28-day expiry; the **Welcome Suica Mobile app gives 180 days on iPhone**. iPhone 8+ can add Suica/Pasmo/ICOCA to Apple Pay directly — do this, it sidesteps the physical-card supply problem entirely. **Android is a trap**: requires Osaifu-Keitai, absent from most non-Japanese phones; Samsung's worldwide Suica support isn't due until H1 2027.

**Visit Japan Web** — https://www.vjw.digital.go.jp (my fetch 404'd on a deep link; the service is live). Covers immigration and customs QR codes; officially "recommended," not mandatory, but it saves real time at the airport. **JESTA/ETA: unresolved** — the Immigration Services Agency homepage carried no announcement, which is a weak negative signal, not proof. Re-check before travel.

**Tax-free shopping — CHANGING, and partly verified.** Japan's move to a **refund-at-departure ("リファンド方式") model** is real and in active rollout: MLIT launched a tax-free-shop portal in **Jan 2026** and a traveler-facing portal in **Feb 2026**, and separate-delivery handling was abolished in March 2025. **I could NOT verify the exact in-effect date, the purchase threshold, whether the general-goods/consumables split and sealed-bag rule are abolished, or the airport procedure** — the detail pages were unreachable. The widely-reported target date is around **1 Nov 2026, i.e. right at your trip**, so you may straddle the changeover. **Verify at https://www.mlit.go.jp/kankocho/tax-free/ closer to travel and don't plan large purchases around either system.** Also note: tax-free goods must leave Japan unconsumed — penalties up to ¥500,000.

**Departure tax — THERE IS A 2026 INCREASE.** The National Tax Agency page explicitly references a "tax rate revision **effective July 2026**" — i.e. already in force for your trip. **The new amount could not be extracted** (old rate ¥1,000). Normally bundled into airfare. https://www.nta.go.jp/english/taxes/indirect/tourist_tax.htm

## Restaurants: the honest picture

**The cutoff is ~¥8,000–10,000 pp for dinner.** Below that, walk in (sometimes queue). Above it, book.

**Practical advice for you:** book exactly two things — **one Tokyo mid-tier omakase (¥15,000–30,000)** and **one Kyoto kaiseki LUNCH (from ~¥9,900)** — and walk in for everything else. The lunch-vs-dinner gap at good kitchens is ~40–50% for substantially the same food, and it's the single best value lever on the trip.

**Timing: you are almost exactly on time right now.** Kyoto ryotei kaiseki for November needs **2–3 months** → book in August/September. Top sushi ~1 month; OMAKASE-listed counters release on the **1st of the month** and go in seconds. At two weeks out in late October: Tokyo mid-tier omakase fine (especially weekday/lunch); famous Kyoto kaiseki on a foliage weekend, realistically nothing.

**Platforms**
| Platform | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **TableCheck** https://www.tablecheck.com/en/japan | Fully English, foreign cards, thousands of restaurants + most hotel restaurants. **Best first stop.** |
| **OMAKASE** https://omakase.in/en | English, Michelin partner, top sushi. ¥390/seat fee, ~¥3,000/mo premium tier for early access. Monthly release, ~1st. (Site 403'd; verified indirectly.) |
| **Pocket Concierge** https://pocket-concierge.jp | Amex-owned, ~800 high-end, **prepaid** — neatly solves the foreign-card and no-show-trust problem. (Site 403'd; still operating per secondary sources — verify.) |
| **Tabelog EN** https://tabelog.com/en/ | Best research tool in Japan; weak as a booking tool. Use to decide, book elsewhere. |
| **Ikyu** https://restaurant.ikyu.com | Best Kyoto ryotei inventory, but effectively Japanese-only and 3D Secure often fails on foreign cards. |
| **AutoReserve** https://autoreserve.com | Will place the Japanese phone call for you. Good mid-tier/teppanyaki coverage. |
| **byFood** https://www.byfood.com | Reservation assistance explicitly for restaurants closed to non-Japanese speakers. |
| **Paid agents** | BookNippon (from $15, refunds if they fail — best value), TableAll ($30–100), My Concierge Japan |
| **Hotel concierge** | Free, and still the highest success rate for anything hard. **Email at booking time, not on arrival.** |

**What you genuinely cannot get into.** *Ichigensan okotowari* ("no first-time customers") is alive in Gion and parts of Tokyo — it's a trust/credit filter, not xenophobia, and the only key is an introduction. Sushi Saito and Sushi Sugita are introduction-only; take them off the list. Many booking forms hard-require a Japanese phone number (workaround: use your hotel's). No-show deposits are real and enforced: **100% same-day, 50% within 2–3 business days, ¥30,000–50,000 pp exposure** — so do not speculatively double-book a night. **Bottom line: the top 1–2% is closed to you, and the ¥15,000–30,000 omakase and ¥9,900–15,000 kaiseki-lunch bands are where the actual pleasure lives anyway.**

**Walk-in and worth the queue.** Tokyo: **Fuunji** tsukemen ~¥1,200; **Tsuta** (first Michelin-starred ramen, ~¥1,500–1,800 — **no longer uses advance tickets since relocating, just queue**); **Nakiryu** tantanmen ¥1,200 (**tablet issues numbered tickets from 08:00** — no dawn queuing, closed Sun/holidays); **Ichiran ¥1,080**; **Rokurinsha** at Tokyo Station; **Tonkatsu Maisen** lunch from ¥1,180; **Uogashi Nihon-Ichi** standing sushi from ¥100/piece. **Toyosu Senkyaku Banrai** (opened 2024, ~70 shops, free entry, plus a free foot bath). **Tsukiji Outer Market** 05:00–14:00, **closed Sundays and Wednesdays** — go 09:00–10:00.
Kyoto: **Nishiki Market** — walk-in only, and note **eating while walking is prohibited and enforced**; go before 11:00.
Osaka: **Kushikatsu Daruma** ¥100–250/skewer (no double-dipping the sauce); **Mizuno** okonomiyaki ¥800–1,500, Bib Gourmand, 30–60 min queue; **Kuromon Ichiba** ¥500–1,000/dish, mornings.
Nara: **Nakatanidou** mochi pounding — no fixed schedule, it's luck.
Conveyor-sushi chains (Sushiro/Kura/Hama) all have **apps that let you take a queue number remotely** — genuinely useful on a Saturday.

# PART B — BUDGET (2 people, 10 days)

**Exchange rate, verified live 9 Aug 2026: ¥157.93 = $1** (open.er-api.com); ECB 7 Aug: ¥158.34. **Working rate ¥158 = $1** (¥10,000 ≈ $63). Historical trend could not be verified — carry a ±5% FX cushion.

## Food (per person)

Verified anchors (7-Eleven, week of Aug 4–7 2026): onigiri **¥160–227**, egg/tuna sandwich **¥281**, hot curry **¥538**, bento **¥700**. Yoshinoya gyudon regular **¥453**. The cheap floor in Japan is still genuinely cheap — it's the mid-tier that has inflated.

| Meal | Moderate |
|---|---|
| Konbini breakfast | ¥700 ($4.40) |
| Casual lunch (ramen ¥1,100–1,500 / teishoku ¥1,200–1,800 / gyudon ¥453) | ¥1,400 ($8.90) |
| Mid-range dinner (izakaya ¥4,000–6,500, yakitori ¥3,500–6,000, okonomiyaki ¥1,800–3,000, yakiniku ¥5,000–9,000) | ¥4,500 ($28.50) |
| Drinks/snacks (izakaya beer ¥600–900, konbini beer ¥230–280, café ¥500–800, vending ¥160–190) | ¥900 |
| **Daily food, per person** | **¥7,500 ($47.50)** |

Splurge tier pp: mid-tier omakase ¥18,000–35,000 · Kyoto kaiseki ¥15,000–30,000 (ryotei ¥30,000–50,000) · wagyu teppanyaki ¥15,000–30,000 · **1-star Michelin lunch ¥8,000–15,000 vs dinner ¥20,000–40,000.**

**10-day food total for two, incl. 2 splurge meals: ¥216,000 (~$1,370).** Range ¥170,000–290,000.
*(Base ¥150,000 + upgrading two dinners to kaiseki ¥22,000pp and omakase ¥20,000pp = +¥66,000.)*

## Attractions

Verified: Kiyomizu-dera ¥500 · Kinkaku-ji ¥500 · Fushimi Inari free · Todai-ji Daibutsuden ¥800 (¥1,200 w/ museum) · Nanzen-ji ¥600 · deer crackers ¥200 · Tokyo Skytree from ¥1,800 (¥3,000 combo). Typical Kyoto temple ¥400–600.

**¥2,000 pp/day → ¥40,000 (~$253) for two over 10 days.** Range ¥30,000–55,000. A teamLab visit for two is ~¥8,000 of that alone.

## Incidentals

- **Takkyubin luggage forwarding (verified):** suitcase <25kg **Tokyo→Kyoto/Osaka ¥3,200**, within Tokyo ¥3,000, to airport ¥3,700. **Do this** — forward the big bags Tokyo→Kyoto and do Hakone with an overnight bag. Hakone's transfers involve stairs, switchbacks, a ropeway and a boat. Budget ¥10,000–13,000.
- **Onsen (verified):** Hakone Yuryo adult ¥1,700–1,800 weekday / ¥2,000–2,200 weekend, towel ¥550. Private bath for 2, 120 min: ¥10,400–11,400. Tokyo sento ~¥550–600 (unverified).
- **Coin lockers (unverified):** ~¥400–500 small / ¥600–700 medium / ¥800–1,000 large; most major-station lockers take IC cards. Budget ¥3,000–5,000.
- **Connectivity:** **Airalo 10-day unlimited (Softbank) ≈ $35–36 each → ~$70 for two** — simplest option. Alternative: **Sakura Mobile pocket wifi ¥329/day → ~¥3,300 (~$21) for 10 days**, cheaper and covers both devices if either phone isn't eSIM-capable. Sakura gives 10% off for 2+ items. Ubigi and Japan Wireless unverified (URLs 404'd).
- **Souvenirs:** ¥30,000–80,000 for two; moderate ¥45,000.
- **Travel insurance:** unverified — no quoting source reachable. Rule of thumb 4–8% of trip cost → **$250–450** for two with medical + evacuation. Verify at Squaremouth/InsureMyTrip.

**Incidentals subtotal for two: ~¥70,000 ($443)** excl. insurance. Range ¥45,000–120,000.

## Cash vs card in 2026

**Carry ¥60,000–100,000 for two over 10 days; moderate ¥80,000 (~$506).** Don't bring it from the US — withdraw on arrival in **two pulls of ¥50,000** to minimize fees.

**Still cash-only:** temple and shrine admissions (essentially universal — this is your most reliable cash drain, ~¥2,000 pp/day in Kyoto and Nara), small owner-run restaurants, many ticket-vending-machine ramen shops, Nara deer crackers, some smaller ryokan (confirm at booking), festival stalls, some coin lockers, small-town taxis, and Kyoto city buses (IC card yes, credit card no). Also: the Kabukiza captioning device (¥1,000) and the WB Studio Tour on-site ticket office.

**ATMs (verified, Seven Bank / 7-Eleven, 28,000+ machines):** accepts Visa, PLUS, Mastercard, Maestro, Cirrus, UnionPay, Amex, JCB, Discover, Diners. **Per-withdrawal limit ¥100,000** (¥30,000 for magstripe-only cards). Visa/MC **24/7**. Fee amount is not published on the reachable page — historically ~¥110–220; assume ¥220 and minimize pulls. Japan Post ATMs also take foreign cards but keep business hours.

**Wise/Revolut** save ~2.5–3% vs a typical US bank FX fee — roughly **$100–135 on this trip**. They're debit products, so carry one true credit card for hotel pre-auth holds.

**Decline Dynamic Currency Conversion — always choose JPY.** Terminals and Seven Bank ATMs will offer to charge "in USD" with a 3–7% markup baked in. Accepting it throughout could cost you $150–300. This is the most common expensive avoidable error on a Japan trip.

**Tipping: none, anywhere.** Staff will chase you to return money. Upscale restaurants add a 10% service charge automatically.

## Grand total — 2 people, 10 days, excluding international flights

| Category | Moderate | USD | Range | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Accommodation (9 nights) | ¥300,000 | $1,900 | ¥220,000–450,000 | **unverified** |
| Food (incl. 2 splurges) | ¥216,000 | $1,370 | ¥170,000–290,000 | partly verified |
| Intercity transport | ¥60,000 | $380 | ¥50,000–75,000 | partly verified |
| Local transport (~¥1,200 pp/day; Kyoto bus ¥230, subway ¥260 verified) | ¥24,000 | $152 | ¥18,000–35,000 | partly verified |
| Attractions | ¥40,000 | $253 | ¥30,000–55,000 | **well verified** |
| Incidentals | ¥70,000 | $443 | ¥45,000–120,000 | partly verified |
| **Total excl. insurance** | **¥710,000** | **~$4,494** | ¥533,000–1,025,000 | |
| **Total incl. insurance** | **¥757,000** | **~$4,790** | $3,400–6,800 | |

**Accommodation is the weakest number and the one to verify first** — and the one most exposed to your dates. Kyoto in November foliage season runs 40–70% above shoulder season and good properties sell out 6+ months out. The ¥300,000 assumes ~¥30,000/night Tokyo, one Hakone ryokan night with two meals at ~¥60,000 for two, ~¥32,000/night Kyoto, ~¥28,000 Osaka. **Book Kyoto now.** *Kyoto's raised lodging tax could not be verified — budget a small extra.*

## Rail, passes, and entry admin

**Shinkansen reservations** — open **1 month before at 10:00 JST**; the online Tokaido/Sanyo/Kyushu (smartEX/EX) service takes bookings up to **one year** ahead. In November you should reserve — not because trains sell out routinely, but because foliage weekends and the Tokyo→Kyoto leg with luggage are exactly when non-reserved cars get ugly. Nozomi goes fully-reserved only at New Year/Golden Week/Obon, so November is fine on that front. *Exact 2026 fares could not be verified — every JR fare source failed.*

**Oversized baggage (Tokaido/Sanyo/Kyushu/Nishikyushu):** sum of height+width+depth **over 160 cm** requires a free advance reservation for a last-row seat. **¥1,000 penalty** if you don't, and the JR Pass doesn't cover it. Most large checked suitcases (~28"+) exceed 160cm — check your bags before you book. Hard limit is 250 cm / 30 kg, two pieces.

**JR Pass — NOT worth it for this itinerary.** 7-day ordinary is **¥50,000 pp = ¥100,000 for two** against roughly ¥60,000 of actual travel. One long shinkansen leg plus a lot of private-rail and subway travel the pass doesn't cover. Two notes: it **cannot be bought at stations in Japan** (discontinued 2023), and from **1 Oct 2026 travel-agency prices rise to ¥53,000** while the official JR website holds at ¥50,000 — so if you ever buy one, buy direct.
Better: **Hakone Free Pass** (¥7,100), point-to-point shinkansen, and IC cards.

**IC cards** — Welcome Suica still available at limited locations, no deposit, no refund, 28-day expiry; the **Welcome Suica Mobile app gives 180 days on iPhone**. iPhone 8+ can add Suica/Pasmo/ICOCA to Apple Pay directly — do this, it sidesteps the physical-card supply problem entirely. **Android is a trap**: requires Osaifu-Keitai, absent from most non-Japanese phones; Samsung's worldwide Suica support isn't due until H1 2027.

**Visit Japan Web** — https://www.vjw.digital.go.jp (my fetch 404'd on a deep link; the service is live). Covers immigration and customs QR codes; officially "recommended," not mandatory, but it saves real time at the airport. **JESTA/ETA: unresolved** — the Immigration Services Agency homepage carried no announcement, which is a weak negative signal, not proof. Re-check before travel.

**Tax-free shopping — CHANGING, and partly verified.** Japan's move to a **refund-at-departure ("リファンド方式") model** is real and in active rollout: MLIT launched a tax-free-shop portal in **Jan 2026** and a traveler-facing portal in **Feb 2026**, and separate-delivery handling was abolished in March 2025. **I could NOT verify the exact in-effect date, the purchase threshold, whether the general-goods/consumables split and sealed-bag rule are abolished, or the airport procedure** — the detail pages were unreachable. The widely-reported target date is around **1 Nov 2026, i.e. right at your trip**, so you may straddle the changeover. **Verify at https://www.mlit.go.jp/kankocho/tax-free/ closer to travel and don't plan large purchases around either system.** Also note: tax-free goods must leave Japan unconsumed — penalties up to ¥500,000.

## Restaurants: the honest picture

**The cutoff is ~¥8,000–10,000 pp for dinner.** Below that, walk in (sometimes queue). Above it, book.

**Practical advice for you:** book exactly two things — **one Tokyo mid-tier omakase (¥15,000–30,000)** and **one Kyoto kaiseki LUNCH (from ~¥9,900)** — and walk in for everything else. The lunch-vs-dinner gap at good kitchens is ~40–50% for substantially the same food, and it's the single best value lever on the trip.

**Timing: you are almost exactly on time right now.** Kyoto ryotei kaiseki for November needs **2–3 months** → book in August/September. ## Cash vs card in 2026

**Carry ¥60,000–100,000 for two over 10 days; moderate ¥80,000 (~$506).** Don't bring it from the US — withdraw on arrival in **two pulls of ¥50,000** to minimize fees.

**Still cash-only:** temple and shrine admissions (essentially universal — this is your most reliable cash drain, ~¥2,000 pp/day in Kyoto and Nara), small owner-run restaurants, many ticket-vending-machine ramen shops, Nara deer crackers, some smaller ryokan (confirm at booking), festival stalls, some coin lockers, small-town taxis, and Kyoto city buses (IC card yes, credit card no). Also: the Kabukiza captioning device (¥1,000) and the WB Studio Tour on-site ticket office.

**ATMs (verified, Seven Bank / 7-Eleven, 28,000+ machines):** accepts Visa, PLUS, Mastercard, Maestro, Cirrus, UnionPay, Amex, JCB, Discover, Diners. **Per-withdrawal limit ¥100,000** (¥30,000 for magstripe-only cards). Visa/MC **24/7**. Fee amount is not published on the reachable page — historically ~¥110–220; assume ¥220 and minimize pulls. Japan Post ATMs also take foreign cards but keep business hours.

**Wise/Revolut** save ~2.5–3% vs a typical US bank FX fee — roughly **$100–135 on this trip**. They're debit products, so carry one true credit card for hotel pre-auth holds.

**Decline Dynamic Currency Conversion — always choose JPY.** Terminals and Seven Bank ATMs will offer to charge "in USD" with a 3–7% markup baked in. Accepting it throughout could cost you $150–300. This is the most common expensive avoidable error on a Japan trip.

**Tipping: none, anywhere.** Staff will chase you to return money. Upscale restaurants add a 10% service charge automatically.

# Tokyo, November 2026 — verified findings

## Asakusa: Senso-ji + Nakamise-dori
- **Free.** Grounds open-air 24h. **Main hall (Hondo): Oct–Mar 6:30–17:00** (Apr–Sep 6:00–17:00). Other halls vary. [senso-ji.jp/guide](https://www.senso-ji.jp/guide/)
- Nakamise shops roughly 9:00/9:30–17:00–19:00, varying by shop — no official consolidated hours exist.
- **Best time: arrive 6:30–8:00.** Crowds build hard from 9:30 and peak 11:00–16:00. Shops shuttered early, but the painted shutters are themselves a sight. Evening after 19:00 is also quiet and the gate/pagoda are lit.
- Time needed: 1–1.5h.

## Tokyo Skytree
Confirmed: it uses **date-variable ("dynamic") pricing** — all published figures are "from" prices. [en.tokyo-skytree.jp/ticket](https://en.tokyo-skytree.jp/ticket/)
- **Tembo Deck (350m), advance online: from ¥1,800 adult** (child 6–14 from ¥900).
- **Combo Deck + Tembo Galleria (450m), advance online: from ¥3,000 adult** (child from ¥1,500).
- **Galleria add-on bought on the Deck: ¥1,400 adult / ¥700 child** (only if you already hold a Deck ticket).
- **Same-day at the 4F counter/machines costs ¥500 more per ticket** than online. For reference, [japan-guide](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3064.html) lists typical same-day rates of ¥2,400 weekday / ¥2,600 weekend for the Deck and ¥3,500 / ¥3,800 for the combo.
- **Hours 10:00–22:00 (from 9:00 Sun/holidays), last admission 21:00. No closing days.** Busy days use 30-minute entry slots; same-day can sell out.
- Advance tickets are not mandatory but are cheaper and safer. Time: 1–2h.

## Ueno
- **Ueno Park: free**, effectively always open (gates shut ~23:00–5:00).
- **Tokyo National Museum: ¥1,000 adult** (under-18 and 70+ free). **9:30–17:00, last entry 16:30**; until 20:00 Fri/Sat. **Closed Mondays** (open if a holiday, closed the next day). Online tickets **recommended, not required** — gate queues can top 30 min. Special exhibitions cost extra. 2–3h.
- **Ueno Zoo: ¥600 adult** (65+ ¥300). **9:30–17:00, last entry 16:00. Closed Mondays.** The COVID-era online date/time reservation is **no longer required** — buy at the gate. [tokyo-zoo.net](https://www.tokyo-zoo.net/ueno/visitor-info/tickets/index.html) 2–3h.
- **Planning note: both close Mondays — don't schedule Ueno on a Monday.**

## Meiji Jingu
- **Grounds free, open daily. November 2026: 6:10–16:10** (sunrise/sunset-based; verified on the official monthly table). [meijijingu.or.jp/en/visit](https://www.meijijingu.or.jp/en/visit/)
- **Meiji Jingu Gyoen (Inner Garden): ¥500** maintenance contribution. [official page](https://www.meijijingu.or.jp/en/whattosee/garden/) — **hours are not published on the official site**; commonly 9:00–16:00 Nov–Feb. Late-autumn maples are a listed highlight.
- **Meiji Jingu Museum: ¥1,000 adult. 10:00–16:30, last admission 16:00. Closed Thursdays.**
- Time: 1–1.5h grounds, +45 min each for garden/museum.

## Shibuya Sky — prices confirmed from the official site
It is **time-slot based, not fully dynamic**: two tiers split at 15:00. [shibuya-scramble-square.com/sky/ticket](https://www.shibuya-scramble-square.com/sky/ticket/)

| | Entry before 15:00 | Entry 15:00 onward |
|---|---|---|
| **WEB advance** | **¥2,700** | **¥3,400** |
| **Window (same-day)** | **¥3,000** | **¥3,700** |

Child (6–11) ¥1,200 at the window; under 6 free.
- **Hours 10:00–22:30, last entry 21:20.** Tickets are 20-minute timed slots.
- **Sunset slots (the ~16:00–16:30 entries in November, sunset ≈16:30) are the first to sell out — book as soon as your date opens.** The 15:00 cutoff means the sunset slot is also the expensive tier.
- **The rooftop SKY STAGE closes without notice for strong wind, rain, snow, or approaching thunderstorms**; the indoor gallery stays open and refunds are not generally given. In November wind closures are a real risk — have a backup.
- Time: 60–90 min.

## Free / no-ticket areas
- **Shibuya Crossing** — free. Best free vantage points: Shibuya Station's 2F Mark City walkway, Shibuya Hikarie 11F, and the Starbucks in Tsutaya. **Flag: I could not verify the current status of the Tsutaya Starbucks (it was closed for redevelopment) — check on arrival.** Magnet by Shibuya109's rooftop "Crossing View" charges a small fee.
- **Harajuku / Takeshita St / Omotesando** — no tickets. Takeshita is extremely crowded 11:00–18:00, especially weekends; go before 10:00. Omotesando is the calm architectural counterpoint; Cat Street connects Harajuku to Shibuya. Miyashita Park nearby.
- **Ginza** — no tickets. Chuo-dori becomes a pedestrian zone ("Hokosha Tengoku") weekend afternoons. Ginza Six rooftop garden is free. **Kabukiza single-act "Hitomakumi" tickets exist and are the cheap way to sample kabuki (~¥1,000–2,500, sold same-day at the dedicated window)** — **flag: exact 2026 prices not verifiable; the official page only confirms the product exists** ([kabukiweb.net](https://www.kabukiweb.net/theatres/kabukiza/)).
- **Akihabara** — no tickets. Yodobashi Akiba, Mandarake Complex, Radio Kaikan, Super Potato, gachapon halls. Chuo-dori pedestrian Sundays. **Flag: I could not verify the announced change to Japan's tax-free system (refund-at-departure) or its exact start date — verify before planning big purchases.**
- **Yanaka** — Yanaka Ginza shopping street and Yanaka Cemetery are free; a good low-key half-day walk combined with Nezu Shrine. **Flag: Asakura Museum of Sculpture and SCAI the Bathhouse hours/prices unverified.**

## Shinjuku Gyoen
- **¥500 adult** (65+/students ¥250, under-15 free). IC cards accepted.
- **Nov hours: 9:00–16:30, last entry 16:00** (Oct 1–Mar 14 schedule).
- **Closed Mondays — BUT open every day Nov 1–15, 2026** during the Chrysanthemum Exhibition.
- **No advance reservation required in November.** Optional WEB tickets just skip the queue. (Timed reservations are only ever floated for cherry-blossom weekends.)
- **Alcohol is banned**; bag checks at the gates. [env.go.jp official](https://policies.env.go.jp/national-garden/shinjukugyoen/guide/information/) Time: 1.5–2.5h.

## Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building — free, and worth it
- **Free admission**, 202m. [yokoso.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/tenbou](https://www.yokoso.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/tenbou/)
- **South Observatory: 9:30–21:30, closed 1st & 3rd Tuesdays.**
- **North Observatory: 9:30–17:00, closed 2nd & 4th Mondays** (extends to 22:00 when South is closed).
- Also closed Dec 29–31, Jan 2–3 and for maintenance. Waits typically 20–30 min. Mt. Fuji visible Dec–Feb mostly, but clear November mornings work.
- **Projection mapping is real and free.** Official name **"TOKYO Night & Light"** (東京都プロジェクションマッピング事業), on the No.1 Building's east wall, viewed from Citizens' Plaza. Runs **nightly, year-round**, several shows per evening on a seasonal timetable (winter shows start earlier, from around 17:30). Holds the Guinness record for largest permanent architectural projection-mapped display. Confirmed operating in 2026 with rotating anime/game programming. [tokyoprojectionmappingproject.jp](https://tokyoprojectionmappingproject.jp/)
- **This pairs perfectly: North deck at dusk, then the projection mapping downstairs, both free.**

## Tsukiji Outer Market / Toyosu
- **Tsukiji Outer Market: free, no tickets.** Hours pattern per [tsukiji.or.jp](https://www.tsukiji.or.jp/calendar/): **6:00–9:00 trade-focused, 9:00–14:00 the main retail window, winding down after 14:00.** Arrive **8:00–9:30** for the best balance of open shops and manageable crowds.
- **Closures follow the Tokyo Central Wholesale Market calendar: Sundays, national holidays, and roughly 2–3 Wednesdays a month.** ⚠️ **Flag: I could not extract the specific November 2026 closed Wednesdays** — the calendar widget only served August. Check tsukiji.or.jp/calendar in October. Note individual shops vary even on open days.
- ⚠️ **Flag: Toyosu Market visitor details (tuna auction observation deck, whether the lower-deck lottery is still running) and Toyosu Senkyaku Banrai hours / Manyo Club onsen pricing could not be verified** — both official sites blocked or returned errors. Toyosu is closed on the same market-holiday calendar as Tsukiji; the upper observation walkway has historically been free and walk-up, with the lower deck by advance lottery.

## teamLab — venue status CONFIRMED
- ✅ **Odaiba Borderless is permanently CLOSED** — it closed **August 31, 2022** and relocated. Confirmed on teamLab's own page. [teamlab.art/e/borderless_odaiba](https://www.teamlab.art/e/borderless_odaiba/)
- ✅ **teamLab Borderless TOKYO, Azabudai Hills** (Toranomon-Azabudai) — open. **Adult tickets ¥3,600–¥5,600 depending on date (dynamic pricing).** **Typical hours 8:30–21:00**, with some dates 17:00 or 22:00. Timed-entry, **advance booking strongly recommended**; same-day tickets sometimes available. [borderless-azabudai.ticket.teamlab.art](https://borderless-azabudai.ticket.teamlab.art/) ⚠️ **Flag: closure days not enumerated on the official ticket calendar** — secondary sources say 1st and 3rd Tuesdays. Time: 2–3h.
- ✅ **teamLab Planets TOKYO, Toyosu** — open, and **the closure was extended: the official exhibition period now reads "July 7, 2018 – End of 2027."** So it will definitely be open in November 2026. **Adult (18+) from ¥3,600, dynamic pricing** (roughly ¥3,600 weekday to ¥4,200+ weekend). **Hours 8:00–22:00, last entry 1 hour before close.** Closed on scattered individual days (e.g. Sept 3 and Oct 1, 2026 were listed) — **check the calendar for your specific November date.** Timed entry; tickets non-refundable but the date/time can be changed up to 3 times, no later than 2h before. You walk **barefoot through water — wear shorts or easily-rolled trousers.** [teamlab.art/e/planets](https://www.teamlab.art/e/planets/) · [ticket store](https://teamlabplanets.dmm.com/en) Time: 1.5–2h.
- **New venue:** teamLab has expanded to 8 permanent locations; a large new **teamLab Bio Vortex Kyoto** opened recently — **not in Tokyo**, and ⚠️ **flagged as secondary-source only.** No new *Tokyo* venue beyond the two above.

## Imperial Palace East Gardens
- **Free.** ✅ **Closed Mondays AND Fridays — confirmed** (open on national holidays except Feb 23; if a holiday falls Monday, closed Tuesday instead), plus Dec 28–Jan 3 and for court functions.
- **November hours: 9:00–16:00, last entry 15:30.** Gates: Ote-mon, Hirakawa-mon, Kitahanebashi-mon. [kunaicho.go.jp](https://www.kunaicho.go.jp/en/visit/event/higashigyoen/) Time: 1–1.5h.
- ⚠️ The old numbered plastic entry token is no longer mentioned on any official page — possibly discontinued. No fee either way.
- Separate **free guided tour of the inner palace grounds** (~1h, 2.2km): apply online from the 1st of the preceding month, or **walk up at Kikyo-mon where 300 same-day tickets are given out at 9:00 and 12:30.** Not held Sun/Mon/holidays. [sankan.kunaicho.go.jp](https://sankan.kunaicho.go.jp/english/guide/koukyo.html)

## Gardens
| Garden | Adult | Hours | Closed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Rikugien** | **¥300** | 9:00–17:00 (last 16:30) | Dec 29–Jan 1 only |
| **Koishikawa Korakuen** | **¥300** | 9:00–17:00 (last 16:30) | Dec 29–Jan 1 only |
| **Hamarikyu** | **¥300** | 9:00–17:00 (last 16:30) | Dec 29–Jan 1 only |

All from [tokyo-park.or.jp/teien](https://www.tokyo-park.or.jp/teien/en/rikugien/outline.html). 65+ ¥150; elementary and under free.

[suijobus.co.jp/en/price](https://www.suijobus.co.jp/en/price) This is an excellent Asakusa→Hamarikyu→Ginza half-day chain.

**IC cards — the shortage is over.** JR East resumed registered Suica sales **1 Sept 2024** and **unregistered/anonymous Suica on 1 March 2025**. # Japan 10-Night First-Timer Itinerary — November 2026

**First, an arithmetic flag:** 4+1+3+2 = **10 nights = 11 days on the ground** (arrival day + 10). I've written Days 1–11. If you truly have only 10 days door-to-door, cut the Osaka leg to 1 night.

---

## 1. NOVEMBER SPECIFICS

### Autumn foliage (koyo) — the single biggest planning variable

**Textbook peaks** ([japan-guide](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2014_when.html)): Tokyo late Nov–early Dec · Hakone mid–late Nov · Kyoto mid–late Nov · Nara late Nov–early Dec.

**But recent actuals have run late** — this is well-evidenced, not folklore:

| Year | Kyoto peak | Tokyo peak |
|---|---|---|
| 2023 | Nov 26 | Dec 4 |
| 2024 | **Nov 28** (still peak Dec 4) | **Dec 3** |
| 2025 | ~Nov 22 (still full swing Nov 29) | Nov 26 |

Sources: [koyo24](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo24/), [koyo25](https://www.japan-guide.com/blog/koyo25/). Note the nuance: 2023 and 2024 were markedly late; **2025 was roughly normal** — japan-guide explicitly said Tokyo 2025 "aligns quite closely with the typical year." So it's a warm-autumn effect that varies, not a clean drift. 2026 forecasts don't publish until September.

**Safe planning window for Kyoto/Nara/Tokyo city maples: Nov 25 – Dec 5.** Before ~Nov 18 the city temples will be green-to-turning.

**Hakone is the forgiving one** — the standard loop climbs ~900 m in a day, so you cross the whole gradient and will hit *something* at peak:

| Hakone area | Elevation | Typical peak |
|---|---|---|
| Owakudani | ~1,000 m | late Oct – mid Nov |
| Sengokuhara / Lake Ashi | 645–725 m | early–mid Nov |
| Gora / Miyanoshita | 430–550 m | mid–late Nov |
| Hakone-Yumoto | ~110 m | late Nov – early Dec |

Same logic in Kyoto: **Takao, Ohara and Kurama peak ~Nov 5–20**, a week or two before the city-floor Higashiyama temples. If your dates land early, go north.

**Tokyo caveat:** ginkgo runs ~1 week ahead of maple. You generally **cannot** catch peak Gaien ginkgo and peak Rikugien maple on the same day.

### Weather and packing

| City | Avg high | Avg low | Rain | Rainy days |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tokyo | 18 °C | 10 °C | 96 mm | ~13 |
| Hakone (town) | 17.5 °C | 7.1 °C | 139 mm | ~11 |
| Kyoto | 17 °C | 7 °C | 84 mm | ~16 |
| Osaka | 18 °C | 9 °C | 82 mm | ~14 |
| Nara | 16.5 °C | 6.4 °C | 71 mm | ~8 |

Aggregator figures ([weather-and-climate.com](https://weather-and-climate.com/kyoto-November-averages)), ±1 °C.

Three things that break naive packing:
1. **Diurnal swing, not absolute cold.** Kyoto and Nara are basins — a 10 °C intraday spread, and mornings bite far more than "high 17 °C" suggests.
2. **Hakone is a different climate zone.** Sengokuhara/Gora run 3–4 °C colder than Yumoto; Owakudani at 1,000 m is colder and windy.
3. **Night illuminations are the coldest thing you'll do** — standing still outdoors 17:30–21:00 in late November.

Pack: merino base layers, packable down mid-layer, **water-resistant shell** (Kyoto averages ~16 rainy days — drizzle, not downpours), compact umbrella, broken-in walking shoes, and **easy on/off shoes** (constant temple removals). Late-Nov travel: add scarf/light gloves. Ryokan supply yukata and towels — skip sleepwear for Hakone. Early vs late November is a real difference: Kyoto drops from ~20 °C to ~14 °C across the month.

### Public holidays — confirmed against the Cabinet Office

Verified at [cao.go.jp](https://www8.cao.go.jp/chosei/shukujitsu/gaiyou.html):

- **Culture Day (文化の日): Tuesday 3 November 2026**
- **Labour Thanksgiving Day (勤労感謝の日): Monday 23 November 2026**
- **No substitute holiday applies** — neither falls on a Sunday.

What actually gets crowded:
- **Mon 2 Nov is a bridge day** → Sat 31 Oct–Tue 3 Nov is a four-day domestic travel peak. Hakone and Kyoto hotels full and expensive.
- **Sat 21 – Mon 23 Nov is a true three-day weekend, and it collides almost exactly with peak Kyoto foliage.** This is the worst period in the window. **My itinerary below deliberately avoids putting Kyoto here.**
- **Sun 15 Nov is Shichi-Go-San** — Meiji Jingu especially congested that weekend.
- **Tue 3 Nov:** Hakone's Route 1 closes ~11:00–15:00 for the Daimyo Gyoretsu procession.

### November 2026 events

**Confirmed:**
- **Tori-no-ichi, Asakusa Otori Shrine — Sat 7 Nov and Thu 19 Nov 2026** ([torinoichi.jp](https://torinoichi.jp/), [otorisama.or.jp](https://otorisama.or.jp/kotoshi.html)). Only two fairs this year. ⚠️ Many English pages still show Nov 12/24 — those are 2025 dates and are **wrong**. Ichi-no-tori falling on a Saturday makes **Ni-no-tori (Thu 19) the far better visit**. ## 4. HAKONE — 1 night

**Ropeway status: CONFIRMED OPERATING, full line.** [Hakone Navi official](https://www.hakonenavi.jp/hakone-ropeway/) shows Sounzan–Owakudani–Togendai running with no suspended sections. Hours **9:00–17:00 (Feb–Nov)**. Volcanic gas is monitored continuously and suspension is decided on multiple readings; the site notes no special restrictions are in force for volcanic activity. **Check the day before** — closures also happen for wind and maintenance. Substitute buses run Sounzan↔Togendai when it's down.

⚠️ **Owakudani nuance:** the station area, shops and **black eggs (kuro-tamago)** are freely accessible from the ropeway. The **Owakudani Nature Research Path (自然研究路)** — the walk up toward the vents — is a *separate* guided-entry product requiring **advance online reservation + ¥800 cooperation fee**, because Owakudani remains a designated alert zone ([Kanagawa Prefecture, updated 27 May 2026](https://www.pref.kanagawa.jp/docs/j8g/cnt/f532566/)). Optional; skip unless you want the hike.

### The loop, in order

Hakone-Yumoto → **Tozan Railway** (~40 min, switchbacks) → Gora → **cable car** (~10 min) → Sounzan → **ropeway** (~30 min with an Owakudani stop) → Togendai → **pirate ship** (~30 min) → Moto-Hakone → **Tozan bus** (~40 min) → Hakone-Yumoto. **Total ~4–5 hours** with stops. All covered by the Free Pass.

**Do it as an overnight, not a day trip, and split it:** museum + ryokan on arrival afternoon, **loop the next morning**. Reason: **Mt Fuji visibility is best 6:00–9:00**, before afternoon cloud builds. November through February is the **best season** — cold dry air, with north-side morning visibility running 82–100% versus 27% in June. The ropeway opening at 9:00 puts you over Owakudani at ~9:15 with excellent odds.

- **Afternoon:** **Ueno Park** + **Tokyo National Museum** (¥1,000; open Fri to 20:00). Autumn colour in the park.
- **Late afternoon:** **Yanaka** — Yanaka Ginza, the cemetery avenue, Nezu Shrine. Old-Tokyo counterweight to the morning's crowds.
- **Evening:** **Akihabara** (2 stops from Ueno).

### DAY 3 — Sat 21 Nov · Central spine
- **Early:** **Tsukiji Outer Market 07:00–09:00** (closed Sundays — must be today). Eat breakfast there.
- **Late morning:** **Hamarikyu Gardens** (walkable from Tsukiji), then **Ginza**.
- **Afternoon:** **Imperial Palace East Gardens** (free; open Sat; **closes 16:00 in November** — don't dawdle).
- **Evening:** **teamLab Borderless, Azabudai Hills** — pre-booked timed slot. ⚠️ Verify price/hours yourself.

### DAY 4 — Sun 22 Nov · West Tokyo
- **Morning:** **Meiji Jingu at opening** (free, sunrise). Sunday means Shichi-Go-San families in formal dress — charming but slow.
- **Late morning:** **Harajuku / Takeshita St** → **Omotesando** (architecture walk).
- **Afternoon:** **Meiji Jingu Gaien ginkgo avenue** — 2025 light-up was Nov 22–30, so this may be your window. ⚠️ Redevelopment construction is active; check access.
- **Evening:** **Shibuya Sky, pre-booked sunset slot** (~16:15 in late Nov), then Shibuya Crossing from ground level and dinner.
- *Forward your large bags to the Kyoto hotel tonight (~¥3,200, next-day). Pack an overnight bag for Hakone.*

### DAY 5 — Mon 23 Nov · Tokyo → Hakone *(Labour Thanksgiving)*
- **Morning:** Slow start. Romancecar from **Shinjuku ~10:00** (Hakone Free Pass ¥7,100 + ¥1,200 surcharge).
- **Afternoon:** Arrive Hakone-Yumoto ~11:30. Tozan Railway to **Chokoku-no-Mori** → **Hakone Open-Air Museum** (¥2,000; 9:00–17:00; open year-round), ~2 hours.
- **Late afternoon:** Check into ryokan (Gora or Sengokuhara) **by 17:00**. Onsen, then kaiseki dinner 17:30–19:00.
- *Holiday Monday means busy daytime, but Monday **night** is post-holiday — quieter and cheaper.*

### DAY 6 — Tue 24 Nov · Hakone loop → Kyoto
- **Early morning:** Cable car from Gora → Sounzan → **ropeway at 09:00 opening** → **Owakudani** (black eggs, and **the best Mt Fuji odds of your trip** — Nov mornings run very high). ~40 min.
- **Late morning:** Ropeway to Togendai → **pirate ship across Lake Ashi** (~30 min) → **Moto-Hakone** → **Hakone Shrine and the Heiwa-no-Torii**. Expect a photo queue.
- **Midday:** Tozan bus back to Hakone-Yumoto (~40 min), then Odawara.
- **Afternoon:** **Kodama to Kyoto** (~¥11,770 unreserved, ~2h15). Arrive ~16:30.
- **Evening:** Check in. Gentle **Gion / Shirakawa canal** walk and dinner. If you want a first illumination: **Kodai-ji** (open from late Oct, ¥600, to 22:00).

### DAY 7 — Wed 25 Nov · Kyoto's big autumn day (south + east)
- **06:45:** **Fushimi Inari** — through the torii before the crowds. Up to Yotsutsuji and back, ~90 min.
- **08:30:** **Tofuku-ji** at opening (2 min by JR from Inari). Tsutenkyo + Hojo = **¥1,600** during the autumn period. Out by 10:30.
- **Late morning:** Back to the hotel or a long lunch. **Deliberate rest block** — you've been up since 06:00.
- **Afternoon:** Keihan to Kiyomizu-Gojo → walk up **Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka** → **Kiyomizu-dera** (¥500).
- **Evening:** **One** night illumination — **Kiyomizu-dera** if the 2026 dates (listed as Nov 21–30) hold, else **Kodai-ji**. Budget a second ¥500 for Kiyomizu evening entry.

- **07:15:** **Bamboo grove** before 08:00 — non-negotiable.
- **07:30:** **Tenryu-ji** garden (**opens 07:30 Nov 14–30, 2026** — confirmed). ¥500.
- **Morning:** **Okochi Sanso** (¥1,000 incl. matcha — genuinely quiet) and **Jojakko-ji** (¥600, excellent autumn). Togetsukyo Bridge.
- **Afternoon:** Randen tram to **Kinkaku-ji** (¥500) and **Ryoan-ji** (¥600). Kinkaku-ji closes 17:00.
- **Evening:** Downtown Kyoto — Pontocho for dinner.
- *Cut the monkey park unless you're keen; it's a 10-min uphill hike for a view you've already had.*

### DAY 9 — Fri 27 Nov · Northern Higashiyama → Osaka
- **08:30:** **Ginkaku-ji** (¥1,000) at opening.
- **Morning:** **Philosopher's Path** south → **Honen-in** (free) → **Eikan-do** (¥1,000) → **Nanzen-ji aqueduct** (free). This is the best autumn *walking* route in the city.
- **Midday:** **Nishiki Market** ~11:30 for lunch (accept it'll be busy) or skip to a proper sit-down.
- **Afternoon:** **JR Special Rapid to Osaka, ¥580, ~29 min.** Check in around Namba.
- **Evening:** **Kuromon Market** (open Fri) → **Dotonbori** and the Glico sign after dark → **Umeda Sky Building** (¥2,000, open to 22:30) for the night panorama.

- **08:00:** **Kintetsu Namba → Kintetsu Nara** (~40 min, ¥680).
- **Morning:** **Todai-ji Daibutsuden** at 08:00 opening (¥800) — before the coach tours. Deer throughout. Walk up behind to **Nigatsudo** for the view and the best foliage.
- **Midday:** **Isuien Garden** (open Sat; closed Tuesdays) — the borrowed-scenery garden, and the quietest thing in Nara.

- **Morning:** **Osaka Castle** at 09:00 opening (¥1,200, now including the Toyotomi stone-wall museum) and the park's autumn colour.

## 1. Tsukiji Outer Market (築地場外市場) — free, no ticket

**CLOSURE DAYS, NOVEMBER 2026 — confirmed from the official source.** The outer market has no calendar of its own; it follows the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market 休市日 calendar (tsukiji.or.jp explicitly says so and just republishes it). I pulled the official seafood-market CSV for 2026 ([www.shijou.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/calendar/2026](https://www.shijou.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/calendar/2026), file [08suisancsv-csv](https://www.shijou.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/documents/d/shijou/08suisancsv-csv)). Rows are labelled 休市日 (closed). November 2026:

**Closed: Nov 1, 3, 8, 11, 15, 18, 22, 23, 29**
- Sundays: 1, 8, 15, 22, 29
- Holidays: Tue 3 (Culture Day), Mon 23 (Labor Thanksgiving)
- Closed Wednesdays: **11 and 18**
- **Wednesdays Nov 4 and Nov 25 are OPEN** — this is the trap; don't assume "all Wednesdays."

Caveat printed on the official calendar page: this is the *wholesale* market calendar; in the outer market a fair number of shops still open on 休市日 and some shops close on other days. Treat closed days as "many shutters down, much quieter," not "nothing open." ([www.tsukiji.or.jp/calendar/](https://www.tsukiji.or.jp/calendar/))

**Hours / timing** — official three-block guidance from tsukiji.or.jp:
- 6:00–9:00 — trade buyers prioritized
- 9:00–14:00 — general retail hours
- after 14:00 — shops wind down at their own pace

Practical: **arrive 8:00–9:30**. Before 8:00 many food stalls aren't up yet and you're in the pros' way; by 13:00 the popular tamagoyaki/uni/scallop stalls start selling out and by 14:00–15:00 it's largely over. Budget **1.5–2.5 hours** including standing-and-eating. No admission fee anywhere. It's about a 5-min walk from Tsukiji Station (Hibiya) or Tsukijishijo (Oedo).

## 2. Toyosu Market + Senkyaku Banrai

**Toyosu Market — free, self-guided.** Official visitor page: [shijou.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/info/0/kenngaku/kenngaku1](https://www.shijou.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/info/0/kenngaku/kenngaku1)
- 見学者通路 (visitor walkways, incl. the windows over the seafood/tuna floors and the restaurant/retail blocks): **5:00–17:00**
- PR Corner (7-block, 3F): **8:30–14:30**, Saturdays to 11:30
- Rooftop garden: **5:00–23:00** — stays open even on market closure days
- **Closed days = same calendar as above** (so the same Nov 1/3/8/11/15/18/22/23/29). On those days the walkways and PR corner are shut. No admission fee. No visitor parking or bike parking — Yurikamome to Shijō-mae, or bus.

**Tuna auction viewing.** Two tiers:
- The **upper visitor walkway** over the tuna wholesale floor is part of the free 5:00–17:00 walkway route — no booking, glass-window view from above. (Hours confirmed officially; that this specific window needs no reservation is my read of the official structure, not a verbatim quote — treat as high-confidence but not quoted.)
- The **lower observation deck** (close-range, on the auction floor level) is **advance-application lottery only, not first-come**. Official page: [kenngaku2](https://www.shijou.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/info/0/kenngaku/kenngaku2); applications go through [toyosu.jcdlotterysite.jp](https://toyosu.jcdlotterysite.jp). Meeting time **5:30** at the PR Corner (7-block management building 3F). Roughly 20 viewing dates per month.

**For a NOVEMBER 2026 visit, the exact dates (from the official schedule table):**
> **Application window: Wed 7 Oct 2026 15:00 → Tue 13 Oct 2026 23:59 JST. Results announced Thu 22 Oct 2026, 18:00.**
Miss that week and there is no lower-deck option for November. (Dec viewing: apply Nov 4–10, results Nov 19 — useless if you're already home.)

*Could not confirm:* per-session capacity, age limit, and whether the lower deck charges anything — those live in a PDF that wouldn't parse and the lottery portal doesn't state them. It has historically been free; verify on the application page in October.

**Toyosu Senkyaku Banrai (豊洲 千客万来)** — opened Feb 2024, directly across the pedestrian deck from the market. Official site is [www.toyosu-senkyakubanrai.jp](http://www.toyosu-senkyakubanrai.jp/) but it's a JavaScript app and **I could not extract its floor-by-floor hours or closed days** — flagging as unconfirmed. Two parts:
- **食楽棟 "Toyosu Senkyaku Ichiba"** — Edo-styled food street, seafood bowls, snacks, souvenir shops. Free to enter. Note it does *not* close when the wholesale market closes, so it's a decent fallback on a 休市日.
- **東京豊洲 万葉倶楽部 (Manyo Club onsen)** — real hot-spring water trucked from Hakone/Yugawara, **24 hours, open year-round** ([tokyo-toyosu.manyo.co.jp](https://tokyo-toyosu.manyo.co.jp/)). Prices ([/price/](https://tokyo-toyosu.manyo.co.jp/price/)):
  - Adults (junior-high+) **¥3,850**, elementary **¥2,000**, 3–preschool **¥1,500**, under 3 free — the "マル得セット" covers bathing + yukata + bath towel + face towel + in-house facility fee, valid **10:00–翌3:00**
  - **Late-night surcharge from 3:00am: +¥1,400 adults / +¥1,500 children**
  - Morning bath extension 5:00–9:00: ¥400/hr adults, ¥200/hr under-elementary
  - **Bathing tax ¥150** per adult on top
- **Worth it?** ¥4,000 is high for a day onsen, but it's genuinely well-suited to *this* itinerary: the rooftop footbath garden and open-air baths look over Tokyo Bay and the Rainbow Bridge, and if you're doing the 5:30am tuna lottery, the 24-hour operation means you can arrive the night before and go straight to the auction. As a standalone stop it's skippable. Tattoo policy not verified.

Rough time: market walkways 60–90 min; Senkyaku Banrai food street +60–90 min; onsen +2–3 hrs.

## 3. Ginza

**Hokosha Tengoku (歩行者天国)** — confirmed on the official Ginza street association page, [ginza.jp/townguide/pedestrian-zone](https://www.ginza.jp/townguide/pedestrian-zone):
- **Saturdays, Sundays and national holidays**, Ginza-dori (Chuo-dori) 1-chome through 8-chome
- **Oct–Mar: 12:00–17:00** ← your November window. (Apr–Sep is 12:00–18:00.)
- Runs year-round except Dec 29–Jan 2.
- Note the rules: **no street performing, no busking, no vending, no costumes/cosplay displays, no cycling** (walk your bike). It's a calm shopping promenade, not a street-fair — some visitors expect the latter and are disappointed.
- **Best time: Saturday or Sunday, arrive ~12:00** and walk the centre of the avenue. Nov 3 and Nov 23 are holidays, so hokoten runs those Mondays/Tuesdays too.

**Kabukiza single-act tickets (一幕見席) — this is now fully online.** Official system: [e-tix.jp/shochiku_makumi](https://www.e-tix.jp/shochiku_makumi/) (linked from [shochiku.co.jp/play/theater/kabukiza/makumi/](https://www.shochiku.co.jp/play/theater/kabukiza/makumi/)).
- **On sale from 12:00 noon the day before each performance day**, all parts and all acts released at once. There is no same-day box-office queue any more — the old line-up-at-the-door system is gone.
- **Max 4 tickets per person.** ¥110 system fee per ticket on top.
- Prices are **per act and vary by act** — the August 2026 program ran **¥2,000–¥3,500** (e.g. 牡丹燈籠 act 1 ¥3,000, らくだ ¥2,000, 鬼神のお松 ¥3,500). Budget ¥2,000–3,500 for November; the exact November lineup and prices post to the same site.
- Seats are **4th floor**, reserved (指定席); entry is via a dedicated 4F entrance, QR on phone or A4 printout. Sightlines are partial — you lose part of the stage and most of the hanamichi. Plan **60–90 min** for one act. English earphone guide is generally not offered in the 4F single-act seats — verify at purchase.

**Other Ginza stops:** **G.Itoya** (Ginza 2-7-15) **weekdays 10:00–20:00, Sun/holidays 10:00–19:00**, 12 floors of stationery, Cafe Stylo on 12F 11:30–21:00 ([ito-ya.co.jp/store](https://www.ito-ya.co.jp/store/index.html)). Uniqlo Ginza (12 floors) and Muji Ginza (with Muji Diner and Muji Hotel) are both on/near Chuo-dori. **GINZA SIX rooftop garden is free and one of central Tokyo's best free open-air spaces** — but ginza6.tokyo returns 403 to automated fetches, so **I could not verify its current hours or that it's still open**; check on arrival.

**Best time:** Sat/Sun from noon for the pedestrian street; add Kabukiza in the afternoon or evening. 2–4 hours.

## 4. Akihabara

**Pedestrian Sunday — confirmed RUNNING, from the merchants' association** ([akiba.or.jp/pedestrianzone/](https://akiba.or.jp/pedestrianzone/)):
- **Sundays only**, Chuo-dori between Sotokanda 5-chome and Manseibashi intersections, ~570 m
- **Oct–Mar: 13:00–17:00** ← your November window. (Apr–Sep 13:00–18:00.)
- Cancelled for rain/severe weather/heat alerts — the site was actively posting cancellations in Aug 2026, so **check that page the morning of**.
- Prohibited: vending, performances, street live music, cycling. So no maids/idol performances in the roadway.

**TAX-FREE SHOPPING CHANGES ON EXACTLY YOUR TRIP — this is the single most important finding here.** The Japan Tourism Agency's traveller page ([mlit.go.jp/kankocho/tax-free/page01_000001_00021.html](https://www.mlit.go.jp/kankocho/tax-free/page01_000001_00021.html)) confirms:
- **From 1 November 2026, Japan switches to a refund-at-departure ("リファンド方式") system.**
- You now **pay the full tax-inclusive price in the shop**, then get the 10% consumption tax refunded at the **airport/seaport departure area** after customs verification, before check-in, at dedicated terminals.
- **The consumables/general-goods split and the sealed-bag packaging rule are abolished** — but consumables actually consumed in Japan before departure won't be approved for refund.
- Threshold stays **¥5,000+ (pre-tax) per store per day**.
- Customs procedure must be done **within 90 days of purchase** and the goods must actually leave Japan.
- **Practical impact:** budget more cash/credit headroom at the till than you'd expect, keep purchases sealed and in carry-on/accessible baggage, keep receipts and your passport together, and **arrive at the airport meaningfully earlier** — this is a brand-new system in its first month, and queues at the refund terminals in November 2026 are a real risk.

# Japan, 10 nights, November 2026 — two people, moderate budget

## The date decision (do this first)

November 2026 has two traps and one opportunity:

- **Mon 23 Nov is Labour Thanksgiving Day**, making 21–23 Nov a three-day weekend — the worst price-and-crowd stretch of the month.
- **Tue 3 Nov is Culture Day**; the night of 1–2 Nov carries pre-holiday pricing.
- **Kyoto's 2026 foliage is forecast late** — central temples ~18 Nov–2 Dec, Tofuku-ji and Arashiyama ~22 Nov–5 Dec.

**Recommended dates: arrive Thu 19 Nov, depart Sun 29 Nov.** This deliberately parks the holiday weekend in Tokyo (which absorbs crowds fine) and lands Kyoto on **weekdays inside peak foliage**. It also puts your Hakone night on Mon 23 — the night *after* the holiday, when day-trippers have gone home and ryokan charge weekday rates rather than the ~30% pre-holiday premium.

If you'd rather trade colour for calm, shift a week earlier (arrive ~12 Nov): Kyoto will be green-to-turning, but everything is cheaper and emptier.

*Day-of-week basis: 1 Nov 2026 is a Sunday. Worth a 5-second sanity check against a calendar before you book anything.*

---

## Getting around: skip the JR Pass

This is the biggest money finding. The 7-day nationwide pass is ¥50,000 per person. Every JR-eligible leg on this route totals **≈¥21,290**. You'd lose about **¥29,000 per person — ¥58,000 for the two of you.**

Three reasons it fails here: it's a 7-day pass against a 10-night trip with airport transfers at both ends; Hakone is almost entirely non-JR (Odakyu, Tozan, ropeway, cruise — none covered); and Nozomi/Mizuho now require a supplement even with the pass.

**Buy point-to-point plus one regional pass.**

| Leg | Cost pp | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Haneda → Tokyo (Keikyu to Shinagawa) | ¥327 | Narita is ~¥2,700 pp worse — pick Haneda if your flights allow |
| Tokyo local, 4 days | ~¥4,400 | ~¥1,100/day |
| **Hakone Free Pass, 2-day from Shinjuku** | **¥7,100** | Covers Odakyu, Tozan train, cable car, ropeway, pirate ship, buses |
| Romancecar surcharge | ¥1,200 | Not included in the pass; worth it |
| Odawara → Kyoto (Hikari, reserved) | ¥12,300 | **Nozomi doesn't stop at Odawara** |
| Luggage forward Tokyo → Kyoto, 1 bag | ~¥2,600 | See below — not optional |
| Kyoto local, 3 days | ~¥2,700 | |
| Kyoto → Nara → Osaka | ~¥1,400 | |
| Osaka local, 2 days | ~¥2,000 | |
| Namba → KIX (Nankai Airport Express) | ~¥970 | Direct, no transfer |
| **Per person** | **≈¥35,000** | **≈¥70,000 for two** |

**Two things that changed recently:** JR East raised fares ~7% in March 2026 (any guide written earlier understates Tokyo fares), and from 1 Oct 2026 overseas travel-agency JR Pass prices rise to ¥53,000 while the official JR site holds at ¥50,000.

**Luggage forwarding is effectively mandatory, not a luxury.** The shinkansen oversized-baggage rule requires a free advance reservation for any bag whose three dimensions sum to 160–250cm, with a ¥1,000 penalty otherwise — and non-reserved cars have no oversized baggage areas at all, so the cheap ticket is exactly the one you can't use with a big suitcase. Yamato takkyubin Tokyo→Kyoto is ¥2,170–3,160 per case, next-day. Hand the big bags over the morning you leave for Hakone; they'll be in Kyoto when you arrive, and you do Hakone's six transfers — switchback trains, cable car, ropeway, boat — with a daypack. **Best ¥2,600 on the trip.**

**IC cards:** the shortage is over; Suica and PASMO are freely sold again. iPhone users should add Suica to Apple Wallet (works with a non-Japanese Apple ID; top up with cash or Mastercard/Amex — foreign-issued **Visa is blocked** for top-ups). Android is effectively a dead end without Osaifu-Keitai hardware. Contactless Visa/Mastercard tap-at-gate now works on Tokyo Metro and Osaka Metro but **not** on JR or Kyoto buses/subway, so you still genuinely need an IC card.

---

## Where to stay

**Total: ~¥281,000 for 10 nights (≈$1,780).** Rates are modelled ±25% — the live booking sites wouldn't yield November 2026 quotes to automated checking.

**Tokyo — 4 nights, Kyobashi/Nihonbashi (Tokyo Station area), ~¥22,000/night.** The Tokaido Shinkansen *originates* at Tokyo Station, so you board an empty train with luggage space — and you do that twice. Deep business-hotel supply, quiet streets, 10 min walk to Ginza. Candidates: **Sotetsu Fresa Inn Tokyo-Kyobashi** (¥19–26k; book a *twin*, the cheap doubles are tiny; free membership gets 14:00/12:00), **Dormy Inn Premium Kodenmacho** (¥23–31k, rooftop bath, breakfast included, free late-night ramen), **Dormy Inn Hatchobori** (¥25–35k, real natural onsen).
*Runner-up: Shinjuku* — better network reach and the only direct Romancecar to Hakone, but disorienting for four days. Asakusa is off the Yamanote line, which is a real handicap.

**Hakone — 1 night, the splurge, ~¥73,000 for two with dinner and breakfast.** Base in **Gora** (hinge of the loop) or **Tonosawa/Hakone-Yumoto** (cleanest departure to Kyoto). Skip Sengokuhara — bus-only, awkward with luggage.
- **Yama no Chaya** (Tonosawa, 15 rooms) ~¥36,400pp — **explicitly tattoo-friendly in the public bath**, which is rare and worth knowing if it applies to either of you. My pick.
- **Setsugetsuka** (Gora) ~¥25,500pp weekday — better value; *every* room has a private hinoki open-air bath, plus three free reservation-free kashikiri baths.
- **Hakone Ginyu** (Miyanoshita) ¥46,750–69,740pp — the cliff-over-the-gorge splurge.

Ryokan have **hard arrival cutoffs** tied to dinner service (typically 17:00–18:00 check-in close). Plan to arrive by 16:30. Add **¥150pp bathing tax**.

**Kyoto — 3 nights, downtown Shijo-Karasuma / Karasuma-Oike, ~¥26,000/night.** This matters more than usual: **the ¥700 one-day bus pass was abolished** specifically to push tourists onto the subway, and in foliage season the buses are the failure mode — they fill to capacity and drive past your stop. Downtown is the only base that's on the subway spine *and* walkable to dinner, Nishiki, Pontocho and Gion. Higashiyama/Gion has no subway station at all — don't base there in November. Candidates: **Mitsui Garden Kyoto Sanjo Premier** (large bath, 12:00 checkout), **Mitsui Garden Kawaramachi Jokyoji**, **Dormy Inn Premium Kyoto Ekimae** (real hot spring, cheaper, station-side).
*Useful:* Mitsui's Kyoto Baggage Service moves bags between Kyoto Station and their properties for ¥500/piece.

**Osaka — 2 nights, Namba, ~¥19,000/night.** With one full day and two evenings, the evenings *are* the trip, and Dotonbori/Kuromon/Shinsekai are walkable from Namba. Namba also has the direct Nankai to KIX; Umeda has no direct airport rail. Candidates: Dormy Inn Premium Namba, Sotetsu Fresa Inn Osaka Namba, Hotel Gracery Osaka Namba. No foliage premium here — this is the easy booking.

**Lodging tax is smaller than headlines suggest** — the band is set by *room total ÷ occupants*, so sharing usually drops you a band. Budget ~¥4,300 total across the trip. (Kyoto's scary ¥10,000 figure applies only to ¥100,000+/person luxury.)

---

## Day by day

### Day 1 — Thu 19 Nov · Arrive Tokyo
Land Haneda, Keikyu to Shinagawa, check in Kyobashi. Deliberately nothing ambitious: Tokyo Station Ramen Street or a walk through Ginza, early night. Buy your IC card / set up Suica at the airport.

### Day 2 — Fri 20 Nov · Asakusa, Ueno, Yanaka
**Morning:** Senso-ji at **07:30–08:00** — the temple grounds are always open and this is the difference between a photograph and a scrum. Nakamise shutters open ~09:30. Sumida riverside for the Skytree view.
**Midday:** Ueno Park — pick *one* museum (Tokyo National Museum is the right choice for a first trip).
**Afternoon:** **Yanaka**, the least crowded neighbourhood in this plan and a Friday-specific win: the **Asakura Museum of Sculpture** (¥500, 09:30–16:30) is closed Mon *and* Thu, and **SCAI the Bathhouse** (free) is closed Sun/Mon — Friday clears both. Route: Nippori → Yanaka Cemetery → Asakura Museum → SCAI → Yanaka Ginza down the **west-facing sunset stairs** (~16:30 in late November) → Hebi-michi → Nezu Shrine. 2.5–4 hours, essentially free.
**Evening:** dinner around Nezu/Ueno. Optional swap: Akihabara instead — note it has **no morning** (Mandarake opens 12:00), so it only works as an afternoon/evening.

### Day 3 — Sat 21 Nov · Tsukiji, Toyosu, Ginza, kabuki
**Early:** **Tsukiji Outer Market**, 09:00–10:00 (05:00–14:00). Verified: it is **open** Sat 21 Nov. Note the closure calendar is counterintuitive — Wed 11 and 18 are closed but **Wed 4 and 25 are open**; don't assume "closed Wednesdays."
**Late morning:** **teamLab Planets** at Toyosu — adjacent, and you wade barefoot through knee-deep water, so wear rollable trousers, not skirts. Timed ticket, booked weeks ahead.
**Afternoon:** Ginza. **Hokoten** closes Chuo-dori to cars **Sat/Sun 12:00–17:00** in November — a calm promenade rather than a street fair.
**Evening:** **Kabukiza single-act tickets.** November is *Kichirei Kaomise*, the most prestigious month of the kabuki year (Kabukiza runs 1–25 Nov, dark on the 9th and 17th). ¥2,000–3,500 for 60–90 minutes — an excellent low-commitment cultural hit.

### Day 4 — Sun 22 Nov · Meiji Jingu, Harajuku, Shibuya, Shinjuku
**Morning:** Meiji Jingu at opening — the forest approach is the point, and it empties out by 10:00.
**Midday:** Takeshita Street (fair warning: Sunday afternoon is its worst), then Omotesando, **Tokyu Plaza Harakado** (free rooftop terrace), and **Cat Street** as the walking link to Shibuya — 15–20 min, no cars.
**Late afternoon:** **Shibuya Sky**, booked for a slot around **15:30–16:30**; November sunset is ~16:30 and those are the contested slots. It's an open-air rooftop that closes in rain or wind with no notice, so keep a backup. Free crossing views: Shibuya Hikarie 11F, or the Hachiko-side elevated walkway. (The MAGNET deck is now a paid lounge, MAG8, ¥1,800 with a drink.)
**Evening:** Shinjuku — Omoide Yokocho or Golden Gai.

### Day 5 — Mon 23 Nov · Tokyo → Hakone, the loop
**Before you leave:** hand your big suitcases to the hotel front desk for **Yamato forwarding to your Kyoto hotel**. Take an overnight bag only.
Romancecar from Shinjuku to Hakone-Yumoto, ~85 min. Then the classic loop in order: **Tozan switchback railway** to Gora → **Hakone Open-Air Museum** (~2h, the single best sight in Hakone) → cable car → **ropeway over Owakudani** → Togendai → **pirate ship across Lake Ashi** → Motohakone for the **lake torii** around 15:30–16:00 → bus to your ryokan by 16:30 for dinner.
Everything above is covered by the Free Pass. **Check the ropeway before you go** — it suspends service for volcanic activity at Owakudani, and the bus substitution changes your timings. Mt Fuji visibility is genuinely good in November — clear, dry air makes it one of the better months, but treat a sighting as a bonus.

### Day 6 — Tue 24 Nov · Hakone → Kyoto
Onsen and a leisurely ryokan breakfast; check out ~10:00. Yumoto → Odawara → **Hikari to Kyoto** (~2h05), arriving early afternoon. Your luggage is already at the hotel.
**Evening:** ease in with Nishiki Market's tail end and Pontocho, or go straight to an **autumn night illumination** — Kodai-ji or Kiyomizu-dera, both pay-at-gate, ~¥500–600. **Shoren-in (~¥800) is the least crowded and the best of them.**

### Day 7 — Wed 25 Nov · Arashiyama and the northwest
**07:30 at the bamboo grove.** This is not optional advice — by 09:30 it's a single-file queue. Then Tenryu-ji (¥500 garden), Okochi Sanso villa, and **Jojakko-ji**, which is one of Kyoto's best foliage spots and a fraction of the crowd.
**Afternoon:** Kinkaku-ji (¥500) then Ryoan-ji (¥600). Kinkaku-ji is a 20-minute sight — accept that and don't over-plan around it.
**Evening:** downtown, walkable from your hotel.
*Swap option:* Ginkaku-ji and the Philosopher's Path instead of Kinkaku-ji, which puts you next to **Eikando** — the best foliage illumination in the city (~¥600–700).

### Day 8 — Thu 26 Nov · Fushimi Inari and Higashiyama
**07:00 at Fushimi Inari.** It's free and never closes; at 07:00 you'll have the lower torii almost alone, and at 10:00 you won't. Walk up at least as far as the Yotsutsuji viewpoint (~30 min).
**Then Tofuku-ji**, one stop away and at peak colour this week — be there for the 08:30 opening. Autumn admission rises to **¥1,000** (14 Nov–6 Dec), and **photography is banned on both the Tsutenkyo and Gaunkyo bridges** during peak. The **night viewing is reservation-only with no gate sales** (¥2,800, 1,020 places, booked through JR Tokai's platform rather than the temple) — 2026 dates publish in early-to-mid October.
**Afternoon:** Kiyomizu-dera (¥500) — go at **08:00 or after 16:00**, never midday — then down Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka to Yasaka Shrine and Gion.
**Honest warning:** Higashiyama on a late-November *weekend* evening is genuinely unpleasant — 45–90 minute entry queues and gridlocked buses. On a Thursday it's manageable. Pick two venues, and walk or take a taxi rather than trusting a bus.

### Day 9 — Fri 27 Nov · Nara, then Osaka
Forward your bags Kyoto → Osaka hotel in the morning. Nara is a **strong half-day to three-quarter day**, not a full one. Kintetsu from Kyoto (~45 min) drops you far closer to the park than JR.
Todai-ji Daibutsuden (¥800), the deer (crackers ¥200 — they bow, and they also mug you), **Isuien garden** for autumn colour, and Kasuga Taisha's lantern approach. *One thing to check:* the **Shosoin Exhibition** at Nara National Museum traditionally runs late Oct–mid Nov with advance timed tickets — verify 2026 dates at narahaku.go.jp if it interests you.
Late afternoon: Kintetsu Nara → **Osaka-Namba direct**, ~40 min. Dotonbori for dinner.

### Day 10 — Sat 28 Nov · Osaka
Osaka Castle in the morning (the park and exterior are the good part), **Kuromon Ichiba** for a grazing lunch (¥500–1,000 a dish, best in the morning), **Shinsekai** and Tsutenkaku in the afternoon — **Kushikatsu Daruma**, ¥100–250 a skewer, and never double-dip the communal sauce. Evening: Dotonbori properly, then **Umeda Sky Building** for the night view.
**Verdict on USJ: skip it.** For a first-time ten-day trip it costs you a full day plus an unresolved Express Pass scramble, in exchange for something you can do at home.

### Day 11 — Sun 29 Nov · Depart
Nankai Airport Express from Namba to KIX, ~45 min, ~¥970, no transfer. **Get to the airport early** — see the tax-free warning below.

### Just turn up

Note the trend, though: Tofuku-ji and Rurikoin both moved to reservations, so re-check in October.

### Skip these
**Ghibli Park** (a full day plus 2h of Nagoya transit — do Mitaka instead), **Warner Bros. Studio Tour** (excellent, but it's a British attraction that happens to be in Tokyo), **sumo** (the November Kyushu Basho is in Fukuoka, ~5h from Osaka — do a morning practice tour instead), and **Robot Restaurant**, which closed permanently in 2020.

### Restaurants — the honest version
The line is roughly **¥8,000–10,000pp for dinner**. Below it, walk in. Above it, book.

**Book exactly two things**: one Tokyo mid-tier omakase (¥15,000–30,000) and one **Kyoto kaiseki lunch** (from ~¥9,900). The lunch-versus-dinner gap at good kitchens is 40–50% for substantially the same food — the single best value lever on the trip. Walk in for everything else.

Use **TableCheck** first (fully English, foreign cards). **Pocket Concierge** is prepaid, which neatly solves the foreign-card and no-show-trust problem. Research on Tabelog, book elsewhere. Your **hotel concierge, emailed at booking time rather than on arrival**, still has the highest success rate for anything hard.

Two realities worth accepting: *ichigensan okotowari* — "no first-time customers" — is alive in Gion, and introduction-only counters like Sushi Saito are simply closed to you. And no-show deposits are real and enforced (100% same-day, ¥30,000–50,000pp exposure), so don't speculatively double-book a night. The top 1% is out of reach; the ¥15,000–30,000 omakase band is where the pleasure actually lives.

**Worth queueing for:** Fuunji tsukemen (~¥1,200), Tsuta (~¥1,500, now just a queue since it relocated), Nakiryu (numbered tickets from a tablet at 08:00 — no dawn queue), Rokurinsha at Tokyo Station, Mizuno okonomiyaki in Osaka.

**Realistic range: $3,600–6,500**, driven almost entirely by accommodation and how many meals you splurge on.
Add international flights: roughly **$1,000–1,600 per person** from the US in November.

**Scenario levers:** swapping Yama no Chaya for Setsugetsuka in Hakone alone moves the total by ~¥42,000. Going lean across the board lands near ¥225,000 on accommodation; peak-weekend Kyoto plus Ginyu pushes it to ¥355,000.

**Daily food, per person:** ¥700 konbini breakfast + ¥1,400 casual lunch + ¥4,500 mid-range dinner + ¥900 drinks ≈ **¥7,500/day**. The cheap floor in Japan is still genuinely cheap (7-Eleven onigiri ¥160–227, Yoshinoya gyudon ¥453); it's the mid-tier that has inflated.

**Cash:** carry **¥80,000 for the two of you**, withdrawn on arrival in two ¥50,000 pulls to minimise fees. Seven Bank ATMs (28,000+ of them) take every major card 24/7, ¥100,000 per withdrawal. Still cash-only: **temple and shrine admissions — near-universally**, which is your most reliable drain at ~¥2,000pp/day in Kyoto and Nara — plus small owner-run restaurants, ticket-machine ramen shops, deer crackers, and some coin lockers.

**One rule that saves real money: always decline Dynamic Currency Conversion.** Terminals and ATMs will offer to charge you "in USD" with a 3–7% markup. Accepting it throughout could cost $150–300. Always choose yen. A Wise or Revolut card saves another ~$100–135 versus a typical US bank's FX fee — but carry one true credit card for hotel pre-authorisations.

**Tipping: none, anywhere.** Staff will chase you down the street to return it.

## Admin

**Visit Japan Web** (vjw.digital.go.jp) for immigration and customs QR codes — officially recommended rather than mandatory, but it saves real time.

**Tax-free shopping changes on 1 November 2026 — right before you arrive.** Japan switches to refund-at-departure: you pay full price including tax at the till and claim back at the airport. The consumables/general-goods split and the sealed-bag rule are abolished; the ¥5,000 threshold stands. Practically: **budget ~10% more headroom at the register than the shelf price**, keep receipts and passport together, **keep purchases accessible rather than checked**, and get to KIX meaningfully early — this will be a brand-new system in its first month and refund-terminal queues are a real risk. Don't plan large purchases around either system.

**Packing:** November is one of the best months — dry, clear, 10–18°C in Tokyo and Kyoto, colder in Hakone at elevation. Layers, a warm mid-layer for evenings, a light rain shell, and **shoes you can walk 20,000 steps in and slip off easily** — you'll remove them at temples, the Asakura Museum, and your ryokan. Socks without holes. A small daypack for the Hakone night.
